=== NOTES 2:78 | Centralization vs Decentralization – Concepts, Arguments and Indian Experience
## SUB 0 | Concepts – Centralisation, Decentralisation and Its Forms
[78:0:0] - **Centralisation**: decision-making authority **concentrated at a single central point** (Union, State capital, HQ). **Decentralisation**: authority **distributed across various levels**.
[78:0:1] - Disadvantage of centralisation: **slow response to local issues**; uniform central policies may **hinder regional policy innovation**; centralisation is a **hindrance to liberty and independence** (Laski/Tocqueville view).
[78:0:2] - **Democratic decentralisation** = community participation and local accountability; features: **autonomy, people's participation, empowerment** ("instilling non-confidence" is NOT one).
[78:0:3] - **Local government attributes: statutory status, community participation, power to tax** – **central control is NOT** one.
[78:0:4] - State control over local bodies runs through **legislation, finance and personnel** (administrative control) – **citizens' grievances** is not a field of State control.
[78:0:5] - Local functions: public health, sanitation, water supply – **not** public order or **judicial review** (higher courts).
[78:0:6] TABLE head: Form | What happens | Control
  [78:0:6.0] Deconcentration | Work shifted to field offices of the same government | Centre keeps full control – weakest
  [78:0:6.1] Delegation | Tasks given to semi-autonomous bodies | Can be withdrawn at will
  [78:0:6.2] Devolution | Powers to elected local governments that elect their own officials, raise own revenue, decide independently | Not withdrawable at will – strongest (73rd, 74th)
[78:0:7] - **Dimensions** of decentralisation (India's weakest = **fiscal**):
[78:0:8] TABLE head: Dimension | Transfers
  [78:0:8.0] Political | Power to decide – elected local bodies
  [78:0:8.1] Administrative | Power to implement
  [78:0:8.2] Fiscal | Power to spend and raise funds and taxes
[78:0:9] > Angles: definitions (×4), devolution, attributes of local government, liberty.
[78:0:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.96-98); app notes 2:78 sub 0
## SUB 1 | Gandhi, Article 40 and the Indian Experience
[78:1:0] - **Ancient village panchayats**: the **village as a self-sufficient unit of governance** ("little republics"); AP: **12-Ayagar** system of the **Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara**.
[78:1:1] - **Mahatma Gandhi**: strongest advocate of village self-government – **Gram Swaraj**, republic of self-sufficient villages.
[78:1:2] - **Ambedkar (4 Nov 1948)**: village "a **sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism**"; unit = **individual**. Nehru: centralised planned state, heavy industry. **Gandhian Plan (1944): Sriman Narayan Agarwal**.
[78:1:3] - **Article 40 (DPSP, Part IV)**: the State shall **organise village panchayats** as units of self-government – the constitutional base of Panchayati Raj (Art. 243 / Part IX / Schedule XI came only in 1992); **non-justiciable**; a compromise between Gandhi and Ambedkar (Art. 39, 41, 42, 33, 48, 50 are distractors).
[78:1:4] - **64th Amendment Bill (1989)** passed Lok Sabha, **failed in the Rajya Sabha**; **73rd Amendment** gave Art. 40 shape (**Articles 243A, 243B, 243G**).
[78:1:5] - **CDP (1952)** top-down; **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee: January 1957**.
[78:1:6] - **First Panchayati Raj: Nagaur, Rajasthan, 2 October 1959** (Nehru); **AP second, 1 November 1959**.
[78:1:7] - Outcome: political power passed, fiscal least – the decentralisation gap.
[78:1:8] > Angles: Article 40 (×3), Gandhi, ancient village, first panchayat (Nagaur).
[78:1:9] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 (laxmikanth-indian-polity-02 p.96-97); Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5; app notes 2:78 sub 2-4
## SUB 2 | Arguments For and Against
[78:2:0] TABLE head: For centralisation | For decentralisation
  [78:2:0.0] Nation-building after Partition, unity, security | Proximity: local bodies know local needs
  [78:2:0.1] Planned heavy industry | Participation
  [78:2:0.2] Weak local capacity | Accountability and speed
  [78:2:0.3] Elite capture by dominant castes | Political education
[78:2:1] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:78 sub 1
## SUB 3 | Subsidiarity and the Three Fs
[78:3:0] - **Subsidiarity**: function at the **lowest competent level**; moves up only if it cannot do it; invoked by the **2nd ARC**.
[78:3:1] - **3 Fs: Funds, Functions, Functionaries**; incomplete devolution keeps PRIs **implementing agencies**, not planning units; without **fiscal decentralisation** elected bodies stay powerless.
[78:3:2] ~~ Sources: Second ARC 6th Report (Local Governance); app notes 2:78 sub 5

=== NOTES 2:79 | Democratic Decentralisation – Meaning, Objectives and Preconditions
## SUB 0 | Meaning and Objectives of Democratic Decentralisation
[79:0:0] # Meaning
[79:0:1] - **Democratic decentralisation:** transfer of power to **elected local bodies** so that people take part in the decisions that affect them – the scheme that "ultimately came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**" (Laxmikanth).
[79:0:2] - **Term coined by:** the **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** (report November 1957), not the Ashok Mehta Committee.
[79:0:3] - **Local self-government / a constitutional provision for local government** = an exercise in **democratic decentralisation** (UPSC 2017; AP Sachivalayam) – not delegation, de-concentration, federalism or a confederation.
[79:0:4] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [79:0:4.0] Democratic decentralisation | Power passed to elected local bodies
  [79:0:4.1] De-concentration | Field offices of the same government get work; no transfer to elected bodies
  [79:0:4.2] Delegation | Power lent by a superior authority – revocable at will
  [79:0:4.3] Federalism | Union–State division of power
  [79:0:4.4] Confederation | Union of sovereign States
  [79:0:4.5] Direct democracy | Citizens decide without representatives
[79:0:5] # Objectives and purpose of Panchayati Raj
[79:0:6] - **Fundamental objects:** **people's participation in development** and **democratic decentralisation** – code "**1 and 3 only**" (UPSC 2015, WBCS 2019).
[79:0:7] - **Political accountability** and **financial mobilisation** are not its fundamental objects (they may follow from it).
[79:0:8] - **Main purpose:** to enable people to **participate in developmental administration** (UPPSC 2004) – not merely to raise farm output, jobs or political awareness.
[79:0:9] - **Why adopted:** **to decentralise the power of democracy** (UPPSC 2016).
[79:0:10] - **What PRIs brought:** **formal representation of the weaker sections** in village governance (SCs, STs, women through reservation) – not eradication of untouchability, land to depressed classes or spread of education.
[79:0:11] - **Democratic governance:** **participation of the public in power** – power rests with the people and is exercised by them or their representatives.
[79:0:12] - After the **73rd Amendment**, effective PRIs need decentralisation of **decision-making**, of **administrative powers** and of **the system as a whole** – **not judicial powers**.
[79:0:13] > Code trap: a single-answer version of the UPSC 2015 item has two right options (participation + democratic decentralisation) – the full answer is both.
[79:0:14] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.96; PMF Polity Part 2 p.136, Part 3 p.1; Rocket Polity #37 p.94; app notes 2:79
## SUB 1 | Local Self-Government – Features, Direct Democracy, Imperium in Imperio
[79:1:0] TABLE head: Is a feature | Is NOT a feature
  [79:1:0.0] Elected by and accountable to local people | Sovereignty
  [79:1:0.1] Defined local area and functions | Legislative supremacy
  [79:1:0.2] Own funds / power to tax | Judicial powers (Nyaya Panchayats are separate)
  [79:1:0.3] Autonomy within State law | Central control
[79:1:1] - **Sovereignty and legislative supremacy** belong to **Parliament and State legislatures**, never to local bodies.
[79:1:2] - **Core principle (Rocket):** democratic decentralisation, community participation and **local accountability** – NOT central control or mere administration.
[79:1:3] - **Direct democracy example: the Gram Sabha** – all registered voters of the village decide directly; the **L.M. Singhvi Committee** called the Gram Sabha the **embodiment of direct democracy**.
[79:1:4] - **Imperium in imperio** = "an **empire within an empire**" = a **State within a State** – how panchayats are described as self-governing units inside the State (APPSC G2 2011); not State immunity, liability or division of a State.
[79:1:5] - **Charles Metcalfe** called Indian village communities "**Little Republics**".
[79:1:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.100; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 19 p.6; Rocket Polity #37 p.94; app notes 2:79
## SUB 2 | Colonial Roots – Mayo (1870) and Ripon (1882)
[79:2:0] TABLE head: Viceroy | Resolution | Significance
  [79:2:0.0] Lord Mayo | 1870 (14 December) | Financial decentralisation; fixed grants to provinces; aim mainly fiscal relief
  [79:2:0.1] Lord Ripon | 18 May 1882 | Resolution on Local Self-Government – the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government
[79:2:1] - **Ripon = "Father of Local Self-Government in India"** (APPSC G2 2008) – not Canning, Minto, Mayo or Mountbatten.
[79:2:2] # Points of Ripon's resolution
[79:2:3] - Local bodies as instruments of **political and popular education** and better administration.
[79:2:4] - Local affairs run by rural and urban local bodies with **definite duties** and **suitable sources of revenue**.
[79:2:5] - **Non-officials in majority**, **elected** where possible; **non-official chairmen**.
[79:2:6] - **Official interference to the minimum** – to **revise and check, not to dictate** (control from outside); so "**direct State control** over local bodies" is **NOT** part of it.
[79:2:7] - Official sanction still needed for loans, new taxes, alienation of property, big works, bye-laws.
[79:2:8] - Later: Royal Commission on Decentralisation 1907-09 (**Hobhouse**); **GoI Act 1919** – local self-government a **transferred subject**; GoI Act 1935 – provincial subject.
[79:2:9] - India's **municipal model** comes from the **British** pattern (Ripon's boards).
[79:2:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.9; Spectrum Modern India p.560-561; PMF Modern History Part 3 p.392; Rocket Polity #37 p.94
## SUB 3 | Committees – Recommendations and Preconditions
[79:3:0] TABLE head: Committee | Key point / precondition
  [79:3:0.0] Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) | Coined "democratic decentralisation"; three-tier PRI; genuine transfer of power and adequate resources (not constitutional status); NDC accepted it January 1958
  [79:3:0.1] Ashok Mehta (1977-78) | Two-tier; compulsory taxation powers; no supersession (or elections within 6 months); social audit; district the first point of decentralisation
  [79:3:0.2] Dantwala (1978) | Block-level planning
  [79:3:0.3] Hanumantha Rao (1984) | District planning, coordinated by the Collector
  [79:3:0.4] G.V.K. Rao (1985) | Development bureaucratised – "grass without roots"; restore the Zila Parishad's role
  [79:3:0.5] L.M. Singhvi (1986) | Constitutional recognition of PRIs – a new chapter in the Constitution; Gram Sabha = direct democracy
  [79:3:0.6] Committee on Policy and Programmes (1988) | Constitutional status, 5-year term, direct elections, State Finance and Election Commissions
[79:3:1] - **Constitutionalisation of PRIs** was recommended by the **L.M. Singhvi Committee** – realised by the **73rd Amendment (1992)**.
[79:3:2] - **Mehta tiers:** Gram Panchayat (village) – Panchayat Samiti (block) – Zila Parishad (district).
[79:3:3] - **Whose cooperation:** the Mehta Committee held **local public participation** indispensable for development.
[79:3:4] # First rollouts
[79:3:5] - **First State:** **Rajasthan – Nagaur, 2 October 1959**; **second: Andhra Pradesh – 1 November 1959**.
[79:3:6] - AP's **13 Zilla Parishads** are being reorganised into **28** (one per district) after their terms ended on 24 Sep 2026 (as of 2026).
[79:3:7] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.96-100; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.14-15; Rocket Polity #37 p.94; app notes 2:79
## SUB 4 | Gram Swaraj, Article 40 and RGSA
[79:4:0] - **Gram Swaraj:** **Mahatma Gandhi**'s self-reliant **village republic** (Hind Swaraj, 1909) – not Vinoba Bhave, JP or Dayananda.
[79:4:1] - **Article 40 (DPSP):** the **constitutional root** of Gram Swaraj – the State shall organise village panchayats as units of self-government.
[79:4:2] - **Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA):** Ministry of **Panchayati Raj**, from **2018-19**; objective – develop PRIs' governance capabilities so rural local bodies become **self-sustainable, financially stable and more efficient**; **trains PRI members**.
[79:4:3]   - Revamped for **1 Apr 2022 – 31 Mar 2026**; funding **60:40**, **NE and hill States 90:10**.
[79:4:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket Polity #37 p.94; Praveen CA360 May 2026; myscheme.gov.in (RGSA); app notes 2:79
## SUB 5 | Decentralised Planning and Participatory Budgeting
[79:5:0] - **Participatory budgeting:** citizens **deliberate and negotiate** over distribution of public resources, **directly decide** how and where money is spent, and **historically excluded** citizens gain access to decision-making – all three make local bodies transparent and accountable (CDS 2013: I, II and III).
[79:5:1] - **District Planning Committee:** constitutional coordinating body under **Article 243ZD**.
[79:5:2] - **Kerala People's Plan Campaign:** launched **17 August 1996**; about **35-40%** of plan funds devolved to local bodies (not 60-70%); turned 30 in Aug 2026.
[79:5:3] - **T.M. Thomas Isaac** proposed "**People's Plan Campaign 2.0**" – student internships and an online portal (25 Aug 2026).
[79:5:4] - **Economic Survey 2025-26:** PRI own-source revenue, **e-GramSwaraj**, **SabhaSaar** (**AI tool** for writing **Gram Sabha minutes**); low Gram Sabha participation.
[79:5:5] - J&K DDCs' term ended 24 Feb 2026 with no fresh polls.
[79:5:6] ~~ Sources: CDS 2013 key; Economic Survey 2025-26; app notes 2:79 (current affairs 2026)

=== NOTES 2:80 | Evolution of Panchayati Raj – Community Development Programme, Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.v.k. Rao and L.m. Singhvi Committees
## SUB 0 | Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) – Appointment, Report and Democratic Decentralisation
[80:0:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [80:0:0.0] Appointed | 16 January 1957, by the Government of India (Team for the Study of Community Projects and NES; NDC/Planning-side review)
  [80:0:0.1] Chairman | Balwantrai Gopalji Mehta
  [80:0:0.2] Reviewed | Community Development Programme (1952) and National Extension Service (1953) – not IRDP
  [80:0:0.3] Report | 24 November 1957 (so "constituted / reported" = 1957)
  [80:0:0.4] Accepted | National Development Council, January 1958
[80:0:1] - **Remedy proposed:** the scheme of **"democratic decentralisation"**, which "ultimately came to be known as **Panchayati Raj**" – the committee **first recommended / used** the idea; Ashok Mehta, Rajagopalachari, Kripalani, Pannikar and Kunjru are distractors.
[80:0:2] - **Balwant Rai Mehta = "Architect / Father of Panchayati Raj"**; the present pattern of panchayats "owes its parentage" to this committee; the **Panchayati Raj system was recommended by its 1957 report** – not by the GoI Act 1935, Cripps Mission or Independence Act.
[80:0:3] - **Associated with:** **Panchayati Raj** (it was set up to review Community Development, but its report is identified with Panchayati Raj); also the basis of **decentralised planning** through PRIs (APPSC G1 2002) – not Mahalanobis or Gadgil.
[80:0:4] - **Finding:** public participation is indispensable – Panchayati Raj needs the **full co-operation of the local public**; PR stands for **decentralisation of powers, participation of the people and community development** ("all of these"), i.e. **grass-root democracy**.
[80:0:5] - **NDC (January 1958):** did **not insist on a single rigid pattern** – States free to **evolve their own patterns suited to local conditions**, basic principles identical.
[80:0:6] - Other heads: **Jivraj Mehta, Shriman Narayan, Jagjivan Ram, B.R. Ambedkar, Krishna Iyer** – never chaired a PR committee.
[80:0:7] > Most-asked: chairman, year (1957), CDP + NES reviewed, "democratic decentralisation", NDC flexibility.
[80:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.13-14; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.96-97; Rocket Polity Part 1 p.94; PMF Polity Part 2 p.128
## SUB 1 | Balwant Rai Mehta Model – Three Tiers and Detailed Recommendations
[80:1:0] TABLE head: Tier | Level | Election (BRM) | Role
  [80:1:0.0] Gram Panchayat | Village | Direct | Village body
  [80:1:0.1] Panchayat Samiti | Block | Indirect | Executive body; block (samithi) = basic unit of planning and development
  [80:1:0.2] Zila Parishad | District | Indirect | Advisory, coordinating and supervisory
[80:1:1] - **Three-tier** system – **first recommended** by BRM; tiers "**organically linked**" through **indirect elections**; samithis filled by **indirect election from the village panchayats** (not from graduates, co-operatives or sarpanches alone).
[80:1:2] - **Panchayat Samiti** is an **administrative (executive) authority** at the **block level** – not advisory/consultative; it is the body for planning (APPSC Panchayat Secretary).
[80:1:3] - **District Collector = chairman of the Zila Parishad**.
[80:1:4] - **All planning and development activities** entrusted to these bodies; **genuine transfer of power and responsibility**; **adequate resources** to be transferred; further devolution in future.
[80:1:5] - BRM did **NOT** recommend: a **two-tier** system, **direct election to the Zila Parishad**, the ZP as **executive**, a **village panchayat of indirectly elected members**, a samiti as **advisory**, or PRI power to levy **income tax / property tax** at all levels.
[80:1:6] - **Report details (APPSC Social Welfare Mains):** each **municipality lying as an enclave in a samithi elects one member** to the samithi; a samithi **can be superseded in public interest**; the **village panchayat collects land revenue as an agency on payment of commission**.
[80:1:7] - **Not a tier:** **Nyaya Panchayat**; **not a PRI:** a **Gram Cooperative Society** (Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, Nyaya Panchayat are PR bodies).
[80:1:8] - Today the PR set-up (73rd Amendment) is also **three-tier – village, block (intermediate), district**; middle tier optional below 20 lakh population.
[80:1:9] - Under the **73rd Amendment**, Panchayat Samiti members are **directly elected** (UP name: **Kshetra Panchayat**) – unlike BRM's indirect model.
[80:1:10] > Code items: BRM = c and d (planning to PRIs; Collector ZP chairman); not a and b (two tiers; direct ZP elections).
[80:1:11] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.96; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.14; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 05 p.2; app notes 2:80
[80:1:12] - **Features:** three tiers; plans for **economic development and social justice** (Art. 243G); MPs/MLAs may be represented in panchayats (Art. 243C).
## SUB 2 | First States – Rajasthan (Nagaur) and Andhra Pradesh, 1959
[80:2:0] TABLE head: State | Date | Note
  [80:2:0.0] Rajasthan | 2 October 1959 | FIRST – inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru at Nagaur; three-tier
  [80:2:0.1] Andhra Pradesh | 1 November 1959 | Second – Shadnagar; CM N. Sanjiva Reddy
[80:2:1] - "Which State first implemented PR in 1959?" – **Rajasthan**; AP followed in 1959 itself ("both in 1959"). Not Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar, UP or Gujarat.
[80:2:2] - AP books add that AP was the first to cover the **whole State at once**; Laxmikanth, NextGen and Rocket only say AP was **second**.
[80:2:3] - **Three-tier** PR first adopted by **Rajasthan**; by mid-1960s most States had PRIs.
[80:2:4] - **Name "Panchayati Raj":** most keys credit **M.K. Gandhi** (Gram Swaraj; UPRO 2017); George Mathew credits **Nehru** with coining it – Nehru inaugurated it, BRM is its architect.
[80:2:5] - **No PRIs:** **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram** (traditional/ADC bodies); Kerala, Assam, Tripura have PRIs.
[80:2:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.97; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.14; Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5, p.94; PMF Polity Part 2 p.128
[80:2:7] - **1999 status (UPSC 2000):** sub-divisional Zila Parishad – **Assam**; Mandal Praja Parishad – **AP**; Janajati Parishad – **Meghalaya**; no Gram Panchayats – **Mizoram**.
## SUB 3 | Community Development Programme (1952) and National Extension Service (1953)
[80:3:0] # Grow More Food Inquiry Committee (1952)
[80:3:1] - Chairman: **V.T. Krishnamachari** (APPSC G2 2008) – not Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta or G.V.K. Rao; campaign (1943) found too narrow → **integrated village development** and a **nationwide extension organisation** → CDP and NES.
[80:3:2] # CDP
[80:3:3] - Launched **2 October 1952** (Gandhi Jayanti) by **Nehru**, **First Five Year Plan**; **55** pilot community projects; pioneered by **S.K. Dey** (later Union Minister of Community Development).
[80:3:4] - **First major rural development programme / first effort at local governing bodies** in independent India; "mother of social development programmes"; launched **before** BRM (1957).
[80:3:5] - **Aim:** **development of villages through public participation**; a step towards **Article 40**; raising the standard of living under **Article 47**.
[80:3:6] - **Components:** agriculture, irrigation, communications, health, housing, education and **social education** (adult literacy, community centres) – social education was part of the **CDP**.
[80:3:7] - **Statements (APPSC JA):** launched 1952 for comprehensive rural development ✔; focuses on infrastructure, education, health, agriculture ✔; "top-down, communities minimal" ✘ (its idea was people's participation).
[80:3:8] - **Community development approach:** asset-based (build existing strengths), inclusive of diversity, aims at **sustainable self-sufficiency** and solving **community** issues – not individual prosperity in place of the community.
[80:3:9] # NES and extension
[80:3:10] - **National Extension Service (1953)** – described as the **first programme** of community development (spread the CDP pattern); NES followed CDP.
[80:3:11] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [80:3:11.0] Block | Unit of planning and development (about 100 villages)
  [80:3:11.1] Block Development Officer | Heads the block team of extension officers
  [80:3:11.2] Village Level Worker (Gram Sevak) | Multipurpose extension worker for a group of villages
[80:3:12] - **Extension principle:** the extension worker translates laboratory findings so farm families adopt them **voluntarily** = **principle of applied science and democratic approach**.
[80:3:13] - **Failure:** seen as **government-imposed**, inadequate people's participation → BRM review.
[80:3:14] TABLE head: Year | Programme
  [80:3:14.0] 1952 | CDP
  [80:3:14.1] 1953 | NES
  [80:3:14.2] 1975 | ICDS
  [80:3:14.3] 1977 | Food for Work
  [80:3:14.4] 2 Oct 1978 | National Adult Education Programme (15-35)
  [80:3:14.5] 1978-79; nationwide 2 Oct 1980 | IRDP
[80:3:15] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 05 p.2; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.96; Rocket Polity Part 1 p.5; app notes 2:80
## SUB 4 | Ashok Mehta Committee (1977-78)
[80:4:0] - Appointed **December 1977** by the **Janata government** (PM **Morarji Desai**); chairman **Asoka (Ashok) Mehta**; report **August 1978**, **132 recommendations** – a committee on PRIs (not Abid Hussain, Khusro, Chakravarty).
[80:4:1] - **Finding:** PRIs had declined, yet they had **generated a new leadership** committed to development.
[80:4:2] - **Two-tier:** **Zila Parishad** (district, **executive**, district planning) + **Mandal Panchayat** (group of villages, **15,000-20,000** people) – the **Mandal Panchayat system** was its idea (not BRM, Vengal Rao, Narasimham); **executive powers to Mandal Panchayats**; the Mandal Panchayat to **assist Regional Rural Banks** with infrastructure.
[80:4:3] - **Term 4 years**; **district = first point of decentralisation** below the State (not the village or block).
[80:4:4] - **Official participation of political parties**; **periodic elections at all levels**; elections by the State CEO with the CEC; no supersession – elections **within 6 months**.
[80:4:5] - **Compulsory taxation powers**: besides grants, panchayats must **mobilise their own resources** – no democratic body stays viable on external resources (1978).
[80:4:6] - **Social audit** by a district agency and a legislators' committee; **Minister for PR** in the State cabinet; SC/ST reservation by population; separate **Nyaya Panchayats** under a qualified judge; **constitutional recognition**; **voluntary agencies** to mobilise support.
[80:4:7] - **Fate:** Janata government fell → no central action; **Karnataka, West Bengal, Andhra Pradesh** acted on it ("second generation panchayats"; WB Act 1973, polls June 1978); Sixth Plan (1978-83) gave PRIs new life.
[80:4:8] TABLE head: Point | Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) | Ashok Mehta (1978)
  [80:4:8.0] Tiers | 3 | 2
  [80:4:8.1] Unit | Block (Samiti executive) | District (ZP executive)
  [80:4:8.2] Elections | Direct at village, indirect above | Party participation at all levels
  [80:4:8.3] Collector | ZP chairman | Reduced role
  [80:4:8.4] Constitutional status | Not proposed | Recommended
[80:4:9] > Incorrect-statement items: "village as first point of decentralisation" and "three tiers" are NOT Ashok Mehta.
[80:4:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.14-15; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.98-99; Rocket Polity Part 1 p.94
[80:4:11] - **Approach:** the Ashok Mehta Committee adopted the **'concentrated circles' approach** – interaction and interdependence of the levels (APPSC Panchayat Secretary key).
## SUB 5 | Precursors – Colonial Roots and Rural Reconstruction Experiments
[80:5:0] TABLE head: Milestone | Year | Significance
  [80:5:0.0] Lord Mayo's resolution | 1870 | Financial decentralisation
  [80:5:0.1] Lord Ripon's resolution | 18 May 1882 | Local self-government; Ripon = "Father of LSG"
  [80:5:0.2] Royal Commission on Decentralisation | 1907-09 | Chair Sir Henry Primrose, then C.E.H. Hobhouse; village panchayats as base of rural administration
[80:5:1] # Rural reconstruction experiments
[80:5:2] TABLE head: Project | Person | Region / year
  [80:5:2.0] Gurgaon experiment | F.L. Brayne | Punjab, 1920
  [80:5:2.1] Sriniketan | Rabindranath Tagore (with Leonard Elmhirst) | Bengal, 1921
  [80:5:2.2] Marthandam | Spencer Hatch (YMCA) | Travancore, 1921
  [80:5:2.3] Baroda | V.T. Krishnamachari | 1932
  [80:5:2.4] Sevagram | Mahatma Gandhi | Wardha, 1930s
  [80:5:2.5] Firka Development Scheme | T. Prakasam's Madras ministry | Madras Presidency (incl. Andhra), 1946
  [80:5:2.6] Nilokheri | S.K. Dey | East Punjab, 1948
  [80:5:2.7] Etawah Pilot Project | Albert Mayer | UP, 1948
[80:5:3] - **Marthandam:** **five-fold development** (physical, spiritual, mental, economic, social – not political); method "**self-help with intimate expert counsel**"; based on principles called the **"Pillars of Policy"** (APPSC G2 2019 key).

## SUB 8 | Road to Constitutional Status (1989-1993)
[80:8:0] TABLE head: Step | Fact
  [80:8:0.0] 64th Amendment Bill | Rajiv Gandhi government, Lok Sabha, July 1989; passed LS August 1989; based on Singhvi, Thungon, Gadgil
  [80:8:0.1] Fate | Defeated in the Rajya Sabha (October 1989) – special majority not secured
  [80:8:0.2] 65th Amendment Bill | Nagarpalika (municipalities) bill; also defeated in the Rajya Sabha (1989)
  [80:8:0.3] National Front (V.P. Singh) bill | September 1990 – lapsed when the government fell / Lok Sabha dissolved
  [80:8:0.4] Narasimha Rao bills | Introduced September 1991 → Joint Parliamentary Committee → passed December 1992
  [80:8:0.5] 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 | Panchayati Raj constitutionalised; in force 24 April 1993; Part IX (Art. 243-243O); Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects)
[80:8:1] - Opposition objection: **Local Government is a State List** subject (entry 5) – the Bill would **centralise power**.
[80:8:2] - Effect: PRIs made **justiciable**; constitutional obligation on States; **uniform** three-tier structure.
[80:8:3] - Key Articles: **243B(2)** middle tier optional below **20 lakh**; **243D(3)** at least **one-third** seats for women; **243K** State Election Commission; regular remuneration to members is **not** a provision.
[80:8:4] - **National Panchayati Raj Day: 24 April**.
[80:8:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.102-103; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 23 p.13, 15
[80:8:6] - **Women 50%:** AP and 20 other States + 2 UTs reserve **50%** of PRI seats for women by State law (MoPR, 2026); the constitutional minimum (Art. 243D) is one-third.
[80:8:7] - **National Panchayati Raj Day 2025:** main event at **Madhubani, Bihar** (24 April 2025, PM).
## SUB 9 | Andhra Pradesh – Early Panchayat Laws and State Committees
[80:9:0] TABLE head: Law / reform | Provision
  [80:9:0.0] Madras Village Panchayats Act, 1920 | Village with 500 and above population could be declared a panchayat
  [80:9:0.1] Firka Development Scheme, 1946 | T. Prakasam's ministry
  [80:9:0.2] AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 | Three-tier structure from 1 November 1959
  [80:9:0.3] AP Gram Panchayats Act, 1964 | Consolidated village-panchayat law
  [80:9:0.4] Mandal system, 1985 (NTR) | Ended hereditary Patel-Patwari system; 1104 mandals replaced talukas and firkas
  [80:9:0.5] Mandal Praja Parishads Act, 1986 | MPPs replaced block Panchayat Samithis (Ashok Mehta idea) – aim: minimise the gap between the common man and officials
  [80:9:0.6] AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 | Implements the 73rd Amendment: Gram Panchayat – Mandal Parishad – Zilla Parishad
[80:9:1] # AP State committees
[80:9:2] TABLE head: AP committee | Recommendation (APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys)
  [80:9:2.0] M.T. Raju Committee | District Development Boards
  [80:9:2.1] C. Narasimham Committee | Modify AP Panchayat Raj on the Maharashtra pattern (ZP-centred)
  [80:9:2.2] Vengal Rao Committee | AP review of PR (distractor for the Mandal and DDB items)
[80:9:3] - Intermediate tier in AP = **Mandal Praja Parishad**; **NIRDPR** is in **Hyderabad**.
[80:9:4] - **2026:** 13 Zilla Praja Parishads reorganised into **28** (one per district); MPTC/ZPTC polls on 5 November 2026; SEC **Anil Chandra Punetha** ordered photo electoral rolls (as of Nov 2026).
[80:9:5] ~~ Sources: APPSC Panchayat Secretary 2017 keys; NextGen previous papers p.67 (NTR mandals); app notes 2:80
[80:9:6] - **AP 1959 Act samithi:** sarpanches **ex-officio** members (indirect); **MLAs** members; **two persons with public-life experience co-opted**; met at least **once in 3 months**; **ad hoc samithis in 1958**; before the 1963 amendment the **Collector could become ZP chairperson** (APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys).
[80:9:7] - **MPPs set up:** **15 January 1987** under the 1986 Act (APPSC key).
[80:9:8] - **Vengal Rao Committee (AP):** recommended **Social Justice Committees in Zilla Parishads** (APPSC JL 2001 key).
[80:9:9] - **At formation (1956):** Andhra area under the **Madras Village Panchayats Act, 1950**; superseded by the **AP Gram Panchayats Act, 1964** for Andhra and Telangana.

=== NOTES 2:81 | 73RD Amendment – Part Ix, Eleventh Schedule, Three-tier Structure, Gram Sabha, Reservations, State Election Commission
## SUB 0 | Eleventh Schedule – 29 Subjects (Article 243G)
[81:0:0] - **Eleventh Schedule:** added by the **73rd Amendment**; **29 functional items** of the Panchayats, linked to **Article 243G** – not 18 (that is the **Twelfth Schedule**, Municipalities).
[81:0:1] - **Nature:** a menu – the State Legislature "**may**" devolve them; it divides powers between the **State Legislature and the Panchayats** (not Union–State, not Gram Sabha–Panchayat).
[81:0:2] - **First item:** **Agriculture**, including agricultural extension. **Last (29th) item:** **Maintenance of community assets**.
[81:0:3] TABLE head: No. | Items (Eleventh Schedule)
  [81:0:3.0] 1–7 | Agriculture; land improvement, land reforms, land consolidation, soil conservation; minor irrigation, watershed; animal husbandry, dairying, poultry; fisheries; social and farm forestry; minor forest produce
  [81:0:3.1] 8–15 | Small-scale industries incl. food processing; Khadi, village and cottage industries; rural housing; drinking water; fuel and fodder; roads, culverts, bridges, ferries, waterways; rural electrification; non-conventional energy sources
  [81:0:3.2] 16–22 | Poverty alleviation programme; education incl. primary and secondary schools; technical training and vocational education; adult and non-formal education; libraries (item 20); cultural activities; markets and fairs
  [81:0:3.3] 23–29 | Health and sanitation; family welfare; women and child development; social welfare incl. handicapped; welfare of weaker sections, SCs and STs; public distribution system; maintenance of community assets
[81:0:4] - **NOT in the Eleventh Schedule:** **higher education**, **rural sports**, **public order**, police; and the **Twelfth Schedule** (municipal) items – **slum improvement and upgradation**, **regulation of land use**, **urban planning**, **slaughter houses**, **burials and burial grounds**, **fire services**, cattle pounds.
[81:0:5] - **Model Accounting System (MAS) for PRIs:** prescribed by the **C&AG** (with MoPR, 2009); its **major accounting heads follow the 29 Eleventh Schedule functions** – so PRIASoft keeps **29** major heads.
[81:0:6] > Most-asked angle: the number (29) – asked 10+ times; then "which is / is NOT an item" (libraries vs land use, slum improvement, higher education, rural sports).
[81:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.6-7; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.106-107 (book p.558-559); app notes 2:81
## SUB 1 | The 73rd Amendment and Part IX – Significance and Articles 243 to 243O
[81:1:0] - **73rd Amendment Act, 1992:** deals with **Panchayati Raj** (rural local government); the **74th** deals with Municipalities (Nagar Palika). Bill introduced **September 1991** (Narasimha Rao Government), Act of **1992**, in force **24 April 1993**.
[81:1:1] - **Third tier of the federal system:** added in **1992** (73rd and 74th Acts; in force 1993).
[81:1:2] - Added **Part IX "The Panchayats"** – **Articles 243 to 243O** = **16 Articles** – and the **Eleventh Schedule**.
[81:1:3] - Gave a **practical shape to Article 40** (DPSP: organise village panchayats as **units of self-government**) and **constitutional status** to PRIs.
[81:1:4] - **Justiciable part:** it brought PRIs under the **justiciable part** of the Constitution – States are under a **constitutional obligation** to adopt the system; formation of panchayats and regular elections no longer depend on the State Government's will.
[81:1:5] - **Significance:** a **landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions**; turns **representative into participatory democracy**; rural local bodies **rejuvenated**.
[81:1:6] - It did **not** create **caste panchayats** or khap panchayats – only the **Gram Panchayat** is a body under the Panchayati Raj system.
[81:1:7] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [81:1:7.0] 243 | Definitions – Gram Sabha (243(b)), intermediate level, Panchayat, village
  [81:1:7.1] 243A | Gram Sabha
  [81:1:7.2] 243B | Constitution of Panchayats – three tiers in every State
  [81:1:7.3] 243C | Composition – by State law; direct election of members
  [81:1:7.4] 243D | Reservation of seats (SC/ST, women, BCs optional)
  [81:1:7.5] 243E | Duration – 5 years
  [81:1:7.6] 243F | Disqualifications – minimum age 21
  [81:1:7.7] 243G | Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats – Eleventh Schedule
  [81:1:7.8] 243H | Power to impose taxes; Panchayat funds
  [81:1:7.9] 243I | State Finance Commission
  [81:1:7.10] 243J | Audit of accounts of Panchayats
  [81:1:7.11] 243K | State Election Commission
  [81:1:7.12] 243L | Application to Union Territories
  [81:1:7.13] 243M | Part not to apply to certain areas
  [81:1:7.14] 243N | Continuance of existing laws
  [81:1:7.15] 243O | Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters (last Article)
[81:1:8] - **Article 243G:** powers and functions of **Panchayats** (village, intermediate, district) – not finances (243H), not Nyaya Panchayats.
[81:1:9] - **Article 243J:** the **State Legislature** may provide for maintenance and **audit of Panchayat accounts**.
[81:1:10] - **Pair check (CGPSC 2024):** 243A = Gram Sabha, 243B = Constitution, **243C = Composition** – only the 243C pair is right.
[81:1:11] - **Exemption Articles:** **243M** (Part IX) vs **243ZC** (Part IXA); Part IXA = **243P–243ZG**, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects, in force **1 June 1993**.
[81:1:12] - **Ministry of Panchayati Raj:** created **27 May 2004**; handles Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees.
[81:1:13] > A-R (APPSC G2): "73rd CAA is a landmark for grassroots democracy" (A) because "it brought PRIs under the justiciable part" (R) – both true, R explains A (Laxmikanth's own linkage).
[81:1:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.1, p.4-8; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.102-106 (book p.554-558); app notes 2:81
## SUB 2 | Gram Sabha – Article 243(b) and 243A
[81:2:0] - **Gram Sabha (Art. 243(b)):** body of **persons registered in the electoral rolls** relating to a village within the Panchayat area – i.e. **all registered voters**, not all residents, all adults, elders or employees.
[81:2:1] - **Minimum age:** **18 years** (voting age); the **age to contest** a Panchayat seat is **21**.
[81:2:2] - **Article 243A:** Gram Sabha exercises such powers at the village level as the **State Legislature provides by law** – in function it is to the village what the **State Legislature** is to the State.
[81:2:3] - **Compulsory:** a Gram Sabha **must be constituted in each village** (or group of villages) – not optional, not abolishable; it is the **electorate** for direct elections (243C).
[81:2:4] - **Direct democracy:** the **Gram Sabha** is the best example – voters decide directly; Gram Panchayat, Nagar Panchayat and Zila Panchayat are representative bodies; caste panchayats, opinion polls and people's courts are not.
[81:2:5] - **Meetings:** at least **twice a year** (NextGen: April 13 and Oct 3; State Acts fix dates); Gram Sabha meetings may be held in each village (by rotation); Gram Panchayat meetings at the GP headquarters.
[81:2:6] # Gram Sabha's statutory roles
[81:2:7] - **MGNREGA social audit:** vested in the **Gram Sabha** (MGNREGA s.17).
[81:2:8] - **PMAY-Gramin:** the **Gram Sabha verifies the housing-deprivation (SECC) data** for selecting beneficiaries.
[81:2:9] # Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP)
[81:2:10] - **People's Plan Campaign "Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas":** from **2 October 2018**; GPDPs prepared through Gram Sabhas.
[81:2:11] - **GPDP** converges all village plans – sanitation, MGNREGS labour budget, nutrition, agriculture, school education, water, livelihoods, natural-resource and disaster plans (**all of them**).
[81:2:12] - **Vital first step:** **collection of data and situation analysis**, before prioritisation and resource mapping.
[81:2:13] - **Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans** are linked to **PM Gati Shakti**.
[81:2:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.2, p.4-5; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.103 (book p.555); app notes 2:81
[81:2:15] - **GPDP convergence (APPSC key):** schemes of **19 Ministries/Departments** (Mission Antyodaya now counts 27).
## SUB 3 | Three-tier Structure, Composition, Term and Qualification
[81:3:0] - **Article 243B:** Panchayats at **village, intermediate and district** levels in **every State**; a State with population **not exceeding 20 lakh may not** constitute the intermediate tier – so intermediate Panchayats do **not** exist in all States ("may not", not "shall not").
[81:3:1] - **Composition (243C):** made by the **Legislature of the State** by law; a **Gram Panchayat can cover more than one village**.
[81:3:2] - **Area:** the intermediate level and villages are specified by the **Governor / State Government** by public notification (e.g. the territory of a Kshetra Panchayat).
[81:3:3] TABLE head: Who | How chosen
  [81:3:3.0] Members at all three levels (incl. Panchayat Samiti) | Directly elected from territorial constituencies
  [81:3:3.1] Intermediate and district chairpersons | Indirectly, by and from among elected members
  [81:3:3.2] Village chairperson (Sarpanch) | As State law provides
  [81:3:3.3] MPs, MLAs, MLCs | May be given representation (voluntary)
[81:3:4] - **Qualification (243F):** minimum age **21 years** (not 25, not 30); other disqualifications by State law.
[81:3:5] - **Term (243E):** **5 years from the date of the first meeting**; if dissolved, fresh polls **within six months** (not three); no poll if **less than six months** remain.
[81:3:6] - **Reconstituted Panchayat:** serves only the **remainder** of the term – first meeting **10 Feb 2014** → new body ends **10 Feb 2019**.
[81:3:7] - **Proxy rule:** a woman Sarpanch **cannot nominate her husband** to attend meetings ("Sarpanch-pati" is not legal); ex-officio MLAs/MPs may send representatives under some State Acts.
[81:3:8] - **Nominated members** attend but have no vote (State Acts).
[81:3:9] TABLE head: Intermediate tier name | State
  [81:3:9.0] Mandal Parishad (Mandal Praja Parishad) | Andhra Pradesh
  [81:3:9.1] Janpad Panchayat | Madhya Pradesh (also Chhattisgarh)
  [81:3:9.2] Kshetra Panchayat | Uttar Pradesh (Uttarakhand)
  [81:3:9.3] Taluka Panchayat / Taluka Parishad | Gujarat (Taluk Panchayat – Karnataka)
  [81:3:9.4] Anchalik Panchayat | Assam
  [81:3:9.5] Panchayat Samiti | Most States, e.g. Rajasthan, Maharashtra, West Bengal
[81:3:10] - **CGPSC 2019 code** pairs Anchalik Parishad with **West Bengal** (code 3 4 2 1); Anchalik Panchayat is Assam's term.
[81:3:11] - **AP tiers:** Gram Panchayat – **Mandal Parishad** – Zilla Parishad.
[81:3:12] > Statement traps: "intermediate tier in all States", "minimum age 25/30", "elections within 3 months", "Panchayats have constitutional autonomy" – all wrong.
[81:3:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.2-3, p.5-6; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.103-104 (book p.555-556); app notes 2:81
[81:3:14] - **Suspended Zila Panchayat President (Chhattisgarh Act, CGPSC 2017 key):** the members elect a President temporarily.
## SUB 4 | State Election Commission and State Finance Commission
[81:4:0] # State Election Commission (Article 243K)
[81:4:1] - **SEC:** superintendence, direction and control of **preparing electoral rolls** and **conducting all elections to the Panchayats** – not the Election Commission of India; municipal polls under **243ZA** by the same SEC "referred to in 243K".
[81:4:2] - **State Election Commissioner:** appointed by the **Governor** (conditions and tenure also by the Governor); removable only like a **High Court judge**; service conditions cannot be varied to his disadvantage.
[81:4:3] - **Law on Panchayat elections:** made by the **State Legislature** (243K(4)).
[81:4:4] - **Constitutional authorities:** **SEC (243K)**, **SFC (243I)** and the **District Panchayat (243B)**; the **Chief Electoral Officer** is a statutory officer (RPA 1950, s.13A).
[81:4:5] - **Created by the 73rd and 74th Amendments:** **SEC, SFC, District Planning Committee (243ZD, 74th)** – not a property-tax valuation board.
[81:4:6] - **Rajasthan SEC:** constituted in **July 1994** (Governor's order 17 June 1994, working from 1 July 1994); its **Secretary is also the Chief Electoral Officer** of the State.
[81:4:7] - **Madhya Pradesh SEC:** constituted **1 February 1994**; Panchayat general elections held **five** times by 2020 (1994, 1999-2000, 2004-05, 2009-10, 2014-15).
[81:4:8] # State Finance Commission (Article 243I)
[81:4:9] - Constituted by the **Governor** within one year of 24 April 1993 and then **every five years**; reviews Panchayat finances (and Municipalities' – **243Y**).
[81:4:10] - **Recommends** to the Governor: sharing of **net proceeds of State taxes**, duties, tolls and fees between State and Panchayats; **taxes assigned** to Panchayats; **grants-in-aid**; measures to improve finances.
[81:4:11] - Governor lays the report before the **State Legislature** with an **action-taken memorandum**; it does **not** appoint the State Election Commissioner.
[81:4:12] - **Article 243H:** the **State Legislature** may authorise Panchayats to **levy, collect and appropriate** taxes, duties, tolls and fees.
[81:4:13] - **Own tax domain:** the **Gram Panchayat** has the main own taxes (house/property tax), so it is better placed for own revenue; the intermediate and district tiers depend mostly on grants, tolls and fees.
[81:4:14] - **Union FC link:** **Art. 280(3)(bb)** (Panchayats) and **280(3)(c)** (Municipalities) – measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund on SFC recommendations.
[81:4:15] TABLE head: Basis | Union FC | SFC
  [81:4:15.0] Article | 280 | 243I (Panchayats), 243Y (Municipalities)
  [81:4:15.1] Appointed by | President | Governor
  [81:4:15.2] Divides | Union ↔ States | State ↔ local bodies
[81:4:16] > Code trap: "SFC = Article 243" (it is 243I); "SEC appointed by CEC/President" (it is the Governor).
[81:4:17] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.3-4, p.7, p.12; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.104-105 (book p.556-557); app notes 2:81
## SUB 5 | Compulsory vs Voluntary Provisions
[81:5:0] TABLE head: Compulsory | Voluntary (State's choice)
  [81:5:0.0] Gram Sabha in a village or group of villages | Powers of the Gram Sabha
  [81:5:0.1] Three tiers (middle optional, 20 lakh or less) | Manner of electing the village chairperson
  [81:5:0.2] Direct election of all members; indirect election of intermediate/district chairpersons | Representation of MPs, MLAs and chairpersons in higher tiers
  [81:5:0.3] Minimum age 21 | Reservation for backward classes
  [81:5:0.4] SC/ST seats in proportion to population | Devolution of the 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects
  [81:5:0.5] One-third seats and chairpersons for women | Financial powers – taxes, assigned taxes, grants, funds
  [81:5:0.6] 5-year term; fresh polls within six months | –
  [81:5:0.7] State Election Commission; SFC every 5 years | –
[81:5:1] - **Strictly:** only the **constitution** of the SFC is mandatory – its recommendations (transfer of funds) are **advisory**, and **devolution of the 29 subjects** is discretionary; that voluntary devolution is the main cause of **uneven devolution** of funds, functions and functionaries.
[81:5:2] - **NOT a provision of the 73rd:** a **two-tier** system, caste panchayats, compulsory BC reservation, "18 functional items".
[81:5:3] - **Courts:** the Act **bars court interference** in Panchayat electoral matters (243O) – a correct statement.
[81:5:4] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.107-108 (book p.559-560); NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.1; app notes 2:81
## SUB 6 | Exempted States and Areas – Article 243M
[81:6:0] TABLE head: Exempted | Detail
  [81:6:0.0] States | Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram (traditional / village councils)
  [81:6:0.1] Scheduled and tribal areas | Fifth Schedule areas (until PESA 1996) and Sixth Schedule areas
  [81:6:0.2] Manipur | Hill areas with District Councils
  [81:6:0.3] West Bengal | Darjeeling hill council area (district-level provisions)
  [81:6:0.4] Arunachal Pradesh | Only SC reservation does not apply – no SC population (243M(3A), 83rd Amendment 2000)
[81:6:1] - **Assam and Tripura** are covered (only their Sixth Schedule areas excluded); **Odisha, Kerala, Goa, Puducherry** have PRIs.
[81:6:2] - **J&K:** outside Part IX until **2019** (own Panchayati Raj Act, 1989); now covered as a UT.
[81:6:3] - **NCT of Delhi:** has **no Panchayati Raj** institutions (only urban bodies).
[81:6:4] - **PESA, 1996:** Parliament extended Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas under **243M(4)(b)** (Bhuria Committee) – details in the PESA row.
[81:6:5] > Old-key trap: APPSC G1 2004 key gave "Goa, J&K, Pondicherry" – Goa and Puducherry have panchayats; the true set is Meghalaya, Delhi, Nagaland.

## SUB 7 | Reservation – Article 243D
[81:7:0] - **Article 243D:** seats for **SCs and STs** in proportion to population at all levels; **not less than one-third** of seats (and of chairpersons, **243D(4)**) for **women** – a floor, not a ceiling, not "50% for SC/ST women".
[81:7:1] - **Rotation:** reserved seats are **allotted by rotation** – not fixed for 10/25/50 years.
[81:7:2] - **BC reservation:** optional (**243D(6)**).
[81:7:3] TABLE head: Case | Year | Holding
  [81:7:3.0] K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India | 2010 | Upheld 243D(6)/243T(6); political backwardness ≠ social/educational backwardness; vertical reservation normally within 50%
  [81:7:3.1] Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v. Maharashtra | 2021 | Triple test: dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportion, SC+ST+OBC within 50%
[81:7:4] - **AP:** **34% BC quota** plus SC/ST shares must stay within Gawali's **50% ceiling**.
[81:7:5] # Women's 50% and data
[81:7:6] - **Bihar** – first to give **50%** to women (2006). By **2009-10**, **Bihar, Himachal Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh** had 50% (Govt statement, 112th Amendment Bill 2009); many States now, including **AP**.
[81:7:7] - **MoPR, April 2026:** **12.14 lakh of 24.41 lakh** elected PRI representatives are women (**49.75%**); short of 50%: **Haryana 42.12%**, Gujarat 49.9%, Tripura 45.25%.
[81:7:8] - **Proxy problem:** IRMA's **State of Panchayats Report 2008-09** – about **59%** of SC/ST women representatives were proxies.
[81:7:9] - **2026:** **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** and **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats** – against token representation.
[81:7:10] - **EWS link:** **Gujarat** was the first State to implement the 10% EWS quota (January 2019).
[81:7:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.2-3, p.5; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.103-104; PRS – Constitution (112th Amendment) Bill 2009 statement of objects; app notes 2:81
## SUB 8 | Panchayati Raj Day, Firsts and State Rules
[81:8:0] - **National Panchayati Raj Day:** **24 April** – the 73rd Amendment came into force on **24 April 1993**; National Panchayat Awards are given that day.
[81:8:1] TABLE head: First | Fact
  [81:8:1.0] First to launch PRIs | Rajasthan – Nagaur, 2 October 1959 (Andhra Pradesh second, 1 November 1959)
  [81:8:1.1] First to implement the 73rd Amendment (MPPSC key) | Madhya Pradesh – "in true spirit" (MoPR / MPPSC 2015 key)
  [81:8:1.2] First 50% women's quota | Bihar
  [81:8:1.3] Pioneer three-tier revival | West Bengal (1973 Act, 1978 polls); Karnataka (Mandal Panchayats, 1987)
  [81:8:1.4] First Municipal Corporation | Madras, 1687-88
[81:8:2] - **Minimum education to contest:** **Haryana (2015 Act, upheld in Rajbala, 2015)** and **Rajasthan (2015)** – Rajasthan dropped it in **2019**.
[81:8:3] - **Haryana 2015 conditions:** functional **toilet**, no arrears of **power bills**, not a **cooperative loan defaulter**, minimum education **by category** (not uniform matriculation).
[81:8:4] - **Chhattisgarh:** three-tier Panchayat poll notification – **23 December 2019**.
[81:8:5] - **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** (conformity Act, 21 April 1994) – details in the AP local bodies row.

=== NOTES 2:82 | 74TH Amendment – Part Ixa, Twelfth Schedule, Types of Urban Local Bodies, Ward Committees, Dpc and Mpc
## SUB 0 | The 74th Amendment and Part IXA – Dates, Names, 73rd vs 74th
[82:0:0] - **74th Amendment Act, 1992:** gave **constitutional status to urban local governments** (municipalities); State governments are under a constitutional obligation to adopt the new system.
[82:0:1] - **Popular name:** the **Nagarpalika Act**; the Bill that became it was the **Municipalities Bill** (Sep 1991, **P.V. Narasimha Rao** government) – Part IXA is titled "**The Municipalities**".
[82:0:2] - **Dates:** passed by both Houses **December 1992**; Presidential assent **April 1993** (20 April 1993); in force **1 June 1993** – so "provision for Panchayats and Municipalities was made in **1993**" (1992 Acts, in force 1993).
[82:0:3] - **Inserted:** **Part IXA** (Articles **243P to 243ZG**) and the **Twelfth Schedule** (18 items, linked to **Art. 243W**).
[82:0:4] - **Part IXA = urban local bodies only**; rural Panchayats are in **Part IX** (73rd Amendment, 1992) – so the 74th is "not concerned with the Panchayats".
[82:0:5] - **DPC (243ZD) and MPC (243ZE)** were both added by the **74th**, not the 73rd.
[82:0:6] - **Earlier attempt:** the **65th Amendment Bill (Nagarpalika Bill), 1989** of the Rajiv Gandhi government passed the Lok Sabha but was **defeated in the Rajya Sabha** (Oct 1989).
[82:0:7] - **Local Government** is in the **State List** (Seventh Schedule).
[82:0:8] - **Existing laws:** inconsistent State municipal laws could continue for at most **one year** (243ZF).
[82:0:9] TABLE head: Basis | 73rd (1992) | 74th (1992)
  [82:0:9.0] Concerns | Rural – Panchayats | Urban – Municipalities
  [82:0:9.1] Part / Articles | IX / 243–243O | IXA / 243P–243ZG
  [82:0:9.2] Schedule | Eleventh – 29 items | Twelfth – 18 items
  [82:0:9.3] In force | 24 April 1993 | 1 June 1993
  [82:0:9.4] Bodies | Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad | Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation
[82:0:10] - **Parts added by amendments:** Part IVA – 42nd (1976); Part IXA – 74th (1992); **Part IXB (Co-operative Societies) – 97th (2011)**.
[82:0:11] - **Local self-government amendments:** **73rd and 74th**.
[82:0:12] > UPSC 2005: "Art. 243Q envisages **two** types of municipalities" is false – it envisages **three** (Nagar Panchayat, Council, Corporation).
[82:0:13] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.119, 132); NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.9-10; app notes 2:82
## SUB 1 | District and Metropolitan Planning Committees (243ZD, 243ZE)
[82:1:0] TABLE head: Feature | DPC | MPC
  [82:1:0.0] Article | 243ZD | 243ZE
  [82:1:0.1] Area | Every district | Every metropolitan area – 10 lakh+
  [82:1:0.2] Elected share | At least four-fifths | At least two-thirds
  [82:1:0.3] Elected by | Elected members of district panchayat and municipalities, from amongst themselves | Elected municipal members and panchayat chairpersons
  [82:1:0.4] Ratio | Rural : urban population of the district | Population of municipalities : panchayats
  [82:1:0.5] Job | Consolidates panchayat and municipal plans; draft district development plan | Prepares draft development plan for the metropolitan area
  [82:1:0.6] Sends plan to | State Government (by its chairperson) | State Government (by its chairperson)
[82:1:1] - **Both inserted by the 74th Amendment** (Part IXA); composition, chairperson and functions are left to **State law**.
[82:1:2] - **DPC is not wholly elected** – only four-fifths (APPSC: "a and b only" for "74th / consolidates plans / all elected").
[82:1:3] - **MPC is a constitutional body**, prepares draft plans – but has **no sole responsibility** for implementing schemes (UPSC 2011: 1 and 2 only).
[82:1:4] - **Operationalising DPCs** remains a mandate of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
[82:1:5] # DPCs in Andhra Pradesh
[82:1:6] - **AP District Planning Committees Act, 2005 (Act 40 of 2005)** – deemed in force from 30 Dec 2003; DPCs **constituted in 2007**.
[82:1:7] - **Chairperson:** the **Chairperson, Zilla (Praja) Parishad** (ex officio); **District Collector = Member Secretary**; 30 members (24 elected from ZPTCs and municipal councillors, 4 nominated); MPs, MLAs, MLCs, municipal chairpersons/Mayors are permanent special invitees.
[82:1:8] TABLE head: State | DPC chaired by
  [82:1:8.0] Andhra Pradesh | Zilla Parishad Chairperson (Collector – member secretary)
  [82:1:8.1] Rajasthan | Zila Pramukh
  [82:1:8.2] Kerala | District Panchayat President (Collector – member secretary)
[82:1:9] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.123-124; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.1-2; MCRHRDI (AP) "Decentralized Planning" slides (mcrhrdi.gov.in/Group12012/decentralizedplan.pdf); app notes 2:82
## SUB 2 | Composition, Reservation, Term, Disqualification and Elections
[82:2:0] - **Composition (243R):** **all members directly elected** by the people from territorial constituencies called **wards**; State law may add persons with **municipal-administration experience (no vote)**, MPs/MLAs of the area, Rajya Sabha/MLC members registered there, chairpersons of committees.
[82:2:1] - **Chairperson / Mayor:** manner of election left to the **State Legislature**.
[82:2:2] - **Reservation (243T):** SC and ST seats **in every municipality** in proportion to their population; **not less than one-third of SC/ST seats for SC/ST women**; **not less than one-third of all directly-elected seats for women** (including SC/ST women); backward-class reservation optional.
[82:2:3] - **Duration (243U):** **five years** from the date appointed for its **first meeting**; reasonable opportunity of being heard before dissolution; fresh election before expiry or **within six months** of dissolution.
[82:2:4] - **Disqualification (243V):** as for elections to the **State Legislature** or under a State law; **minimum age 21** – no one is disqualified for being under 25 if he/she is 21.
[82:2:5] - **Being on the electoral roll** of the area is the basic condition for contesting – no party membership or permission needed.
[82:2:6] - **Elections (243ZA):** superintendence, direction and control of rolls and all municipal elections vested in the **State Election Commission** (not the State Government).
[82:2:7] - **Finance (243Y):** the same **State Finance Commission** (243I) reviews municipal finances every five years.
[82:2:8] - **Mayor's tenure:** fixed by **State law** – Laxmikanth: in a majority of States **one year, renewable**; States with directly elected Mayors (e.g. UP) give **five years**, matching the municipality's term (UPPSC key: 5 years).
[82:2:9] > APPSC 2011 key gave "25" for the minimum age because 21 was not offered – the constitutional age is **21**.
[82:2:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.120-122, 126; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.10-15; NextGen 25 p.1
## SUB 3 | Types of Municipalities (243Q) and Urban Local Bodies
[82:3:0] TABLE head: Type (243Q) | Area
  [82:3:0.0] Nagar Panchayat | Transitional area – in transition from rural to urban
  [82:3:0.1] Municipal Council | Smaller urban area
  [82:3:0.2] Municipal Corporation | Larger urban area – big cities
[82:3:1] - **Who specifies the areas:** the **Governor**, by public notification, on population, density, revenue, share of non-agricultural employment, economic importance.
[82:3:2] - **Industrial township** (243Q proviso): where an **industrial establishment** provides municipal services, the Governor may specify it as an industrial township and no municipality need be constituted.
[82:3:3] - **Municipal Corporations** are for big cities because urban administration there is very complex (CGPSC 2021 A-R: both true, R explains A); set up by **State Acts** (Acts of Parliament in UTs).
[82:3:4] - **Corporation's three authorities:** **Council** (headed by the **Mayor**), **Standing Committees**, **Municipal Commissioner** (chief executive, appointed by the State, usually IAS).
[82:3:5] - **Municipal Council:** council headed by a **president/chairman** (real executive pivot), standing committees, chief executive officer.
[82:3:6] - **Eight types of ULBs:** Municipal Corporation, Municipality, **Notified Area Committee** (entirely nominated), Town Area Committee, **Cantonment Board**, Township, **Port Trust**, Special Purpose Agency.
[82:3:7] - **Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils and Nagar Panchayats** are all **urban** local governments.
[82:3:8] - **Cantonment Board:** outside 243Q; set up under the **Cantonments Act, 2006** (replaced the **1924 Act**); under the **Ministry of Defence**; 62 boards. **MoHUA** is the main ministry for ULBs; Home Affairs for UTs.
[82:3:9] - **Panchayat vs Cantonment Board dispute** (Chhattisgarh Municipalities Act, 1961, s.79(2)): decided by the **State Government, subject to Central Government approval**.
[82:3:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.117, 119, 126-129; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.3-5; NextGen 24 p.13; app notes 2:82
## SUB 4 | Twelfth Schedule – 18 Functions of Municipalities
[82:4:0] - **18 items**, added by the 74th; linked to **Art. 243W**; an illustrative list the State may devolve.
[82:4:1] TABLE head: # | Item | # | Item
  [82:4:1.0] 1 | Urban / town planning | 10 | Slum improvement and upgradation
  [82:4:1.1] 2 | Regulation of land use and construction of buildings | 11 | Urban poverty alleviation
  [82:4:1.2] 3 | Planning for economic and social development | 12 | Parks, gardens, playgrounds
  [82:4:1.3] 4 | Roads and bridges | 13 | Cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects
  [82:4:1.4] 5 | Water supply | 14 | Burials, cremations, electric crematoriums
  [82:4:1.5] 6 | Public health, sanitation, solid waste | 15 | Cattle pounds; prevention of cruelty to animals
  [82:4:1.6] 7 | Fire services | 16 | Vital statistics (births and deaths)
  [82:4:1.7] 8 | Urban forestry, environment | 17 | Street lighting, parking, bus stops, conveniences
  [82:4:1.8] 9 | Weaker sections incl. disabled | 18 | Slaughter houses and tanneries
[82:4:2] - **Eleventh only (not Twelfth):** non-conventional energy, small-scale industries, technical and vocational education, libraries, markets and fairs, PDS.
[82:4:3] - **Maintenance of public order** is NOT a local-government function (it is State police work).
[82:4:4] - The Schedule is not only physical infrastructure – social (poverty, slums), environmental, cultural and regulatory items too.
[82:4:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.125; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.2-3; app notes 2:82
## SUB 5 | Wards Committees (243S) and Area Sabhas
[82:5:0] - **Wards Committee:** compulsory in every municipality with a **population of three lakh or more**; consists of **one or more wards**.
[82:5:1] - **State Legislature** decides its composition, territorial area and how seats are filled; the ward **councillor** is a member.
[82:5:2] - Nagar Panchayat wards committee (Chhattisgarh law, CGPSC 2017 key): formed of some wards; elected ward councillors members; **two residents nominated**; chairman not nominated by the President.
[82:5:3] - **Area Sabha:** all voters of a **polling-booth area** – proposed in the **Model Nagara Raj Bill, 2008**; the **Community Participation Law** was a mandatory reform under **JNNURM**.
[82:5:4] > 3 lakh = Wards Committee; 10 lakh = metropolitan area (MPC).
[82:5:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.120; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.11, 14; app notes 2:82
## SUB 6 | Functionaries and Andhra Pradesh Urban Bodies
[82:6:0] TABLE head: Functionary | Institution
  [82:6:0.0] Sarpanch | Village (Gram) Panchayat
  [82:6:0.1] Pradhan | Panchayat Samiti (block)
  [82:6:0.2] Chairperson | Municipality (Municipal Council / Nagar Panchayat); also Zilla Parishad
  [82:6:0.3] Mayor (with Deputy Mayor) | Municipal Corporation
  [82:6:0.4] Councillor | Elected member for a ward
[82:6:1] - **State control over ULBs:** **legislative, financial and personnel** matters (not citizens' grievances).
[82:6:2] - **AP SES 2025-26:** **123 ULBs = 17 Municipal Corporations + 76 Municipalities + 30 Nagar Panchayats**.
[82:6:3] - **Department:** **Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD)**; **DIGIT** e-Governance platform.
[82:6:4] - **Laws:** **AP Municipalities Act, 1965**; **AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994** (applies the **Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act, 1955**).
[82:6:5] - **2026:** Cabinet (18 Aug 2026) – **direct election of Mayors** and chairpersons; **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** (19 Aug 2026) – **33.33% BC quota** in ULBs; SEC **Anil Chandra Punetha** – ward-wise photo rolls for **41 ULBs**.
[82:6:6] - **VMRDA** (2018) replaced **VUDA**; **APCRDA** (Dec 2014) plans the capital region and **Amaravati**.
[82:6:7] - ULBs: "**stepchild**" of federalism; **property tax** – main own revenue, under-collected.
[82:6:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.40 p.126-127; app notes 2:82 (AP SES 2025-26; current affairs 2026)

## SUB 8 | Evolution of Urban Local Government
[82:8:0] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [82:8:0.0] 1688 | First Municipal Corporation – Madras (charter 30 Dec 1687; came into being 29 Sep 1688)
  [82:8:0.1] 1726 | Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta
  [82:8:0.2] 1870 | Lord Mayo's resolution – financial decentralisation
  [82:8:0.3] 1882 | Lord Ripon's resolution – "Magna Carta" of local self-government
  [82:8:0.4] 1907-09 | Royal Commission on Decentralisation (Hobhouse)
  [82:8:0.5] 1919 | GoI Act – local self-government a transferred subject
  [82:8:0.6] 1924 | Cantonments Act
  [82:8:0.7] 1935 | GoI Act – a provincial subject
  [82:8:0.8] 1954 | Central Council of Local Self-Government (Art. 263)
[82:8:1] - **Charles Metcalfe** called village communities "**Little Republics**".
[82:8:2] - **Hanumantha Rao Committee (1984)** made the **Collector** central to district planning.

=== NOTES 2:83 | Pesa Act 1996; Fifth and Sixth Schedule Areas and Tribal Self-governance
## SUB 0 | Fifth Schedule – Scheduled Areas, Governor and Tribes Advisory Council
[83:0:0] - **Article 244(1), Part X:** the **Fifth Schedule** governs the administration and control of **Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes** in any State **other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram**.
[83:0:1] - **Ten States** have Scheduled Areas: **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan**.
[83:0:2] - STs reside in what the Constitution calls **Scheduled Areas** (Fifth Schedule); the purpose of both Fifth and Sixth Schedules is to **protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes**.
[83:0:3] # Declaration
[83:0:4] - **President** declares an area a Scheduled Area **by Order**; can increase, decrease, **alter boundaries**, rescind – in consultation with the Governor (not the Governor, Parliament or Assembly).
[83:0:5] - **Criteria** (not in the Constitution): **preponderance of tribals**, compactness and reasonable size, viable administrative unit (**largest unit the district, lowest a cluster of villages in a block**), **economic backwardness** – not industrial development.
[83:0:6] # Executive power
[83:0:7] - The **State's executive power extends** to Scheduled Areas – the State does not lose it, and no local body takes over (UPSC 2025: neither statement correct).
[83:0:8] - The **Union** can only **give directions** to the State on their administration – it does not take over the area.
[83:0:9] - The **Governor** reports to the **President**, **annually or whenever required** – not the Chief Minister to the Home Ministry (UPSC 2023: only two statements correct).
[83:0:10] # Tribes Advisory Council (Para 4)
[83:0:11] - Compulsory in every State **with Scheduled Areas**; the President may direct one in a State having STs but no Scheduled Areas.
[83:0:12] - **Not more than 20 members** ("up to 20"), about **three-fourths** of them **ST members of the State Assembly**; advises the Governor on ST welfare – no legislative or judicial power.
[83:0:13] # Laws and regulations (Para 5)
[83:0:14] - The **Governor** may direct that **any Act of Parliament or the State Legislature shall not apply**, or apply with modifications, to a Scheduled Area (after consulting the TAC).
[83:0:15] - The **Governor** makes **regulations for peace and good government**: may **prohibit or restrict transfer of land** by or among STs (so declaring an area Scheduled **prevents tribal land passing to non-tribals**), regulate land allotment and **money-lending**; may repeal or amend Acts – all need the **President's assent**.
[83:0:16] - **Parliament** may amend the Fifth and Sixth Schedules by **ordinary law** (not an Art. 368 amendment).
[83:0:17] > APPSC G2 "all correct except": the false one is "Governor is **not** authorised to direct that an Act shall not apply".
[83:0:18] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.42 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.142-143, 145); NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.11-12; NextGen 18 p.7; Rocket Polity Part 2 p.10; app notes 2:83
## SUB 1 | Sixth Schedule – Tribal Areas and Autonomous District Councils
[83:1:0] - **Articles 244(2) and 275(1):** **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** only – NOT Nagaland (371A), **Manipur** (371C), Arunachal or Sikkim.
[83:1:1] - **Not** applicable wherever STs exceed 40% – the four States are named; the areas stay **within the State's executive authority** (and State Legislature's, subject to the Schedule).
[83:1:2] - **Ten autonomous districts:** Assam 3, Meghalaya 3, Tripura 1, Mizoram 3.
[83:1:3] - The **Governor** (not the President) organises and re-organises autonomous districts, alters areas, names and boundaries; where there are different tribes he can divide a district into **autonomous regions**.
[83:1:4] - **Autonomous region** = a unit **within an autonomous district**, with its own **Regional Council**.
[83:1:5] - **District Council: 30 members – 26 elected** by adult franchise, **4 nominated** by the Governor; elected members 5 years (not 24 + 6).
[83:1:6] - **Powers:** laws on land, forests, canal water, shifting cultivation, village administration, **inheritance**, marriage and divorce, social customs (Governor's assent); village courts – **High Court jurisdiction specified by the Governor**; land revenue and taxes.
[83:1:7] - **Application of laws:** Acts do not apply or apply with modifications – direction by the **Governor in Assam** (Acts of Parliament and State); in Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram by the **President** for Acts of Parliament.
[83:1:8] - **Article 244A:** Parliament may form an **autonomous State within Assam** comprising certain tribal areas, with a local legislature or council of ministers or both.
[83:1:9] - **Income Tax Act s.10(26):** STs residing in specified Sixth Schedule areas are exempt on certain incomes.
[83:1:10] > APPSC G2 Mains 2025 (40%-rule / outside State authority / only President reorganises / no High Court): **none** is correct.
[83:1:11] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.42 p.143-145; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.12-14; NextGen 18 p.8; app notes 2:83
## SUB 2 | PESA Act, 1996
[83:2:0] - **Why:** **Art. 243M** keeps Part IX out of Scheduled and Tribal Areas; **243M(4)(b)** lets Parliament extend it by an **ordinary law** – done by the **Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996** (PESA / Extension Act).
[83:2:1] - **Passed 1996**; in force **24 December 1996**; based on the **Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee** (1995).
[83:2:2] - Extends the **73rd Amendment (Part IX)** to **Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) Areas** only – not to Sixth Schedule Tribal Areas, not J&K.
[83:2:3] - **Ten PESA States** = the ten Fifth Schedule States; **not** in Assam, Meghalaya, **Tamil Nadu** (RAS 2016).
[83:2:4] - **Objectives:** extend Part IX with modifications; **self-rule** for tribals; **Gram Sabha the nucleus**; administration consistent with **traditional practices**; safeguard traditions and customs; free tribals from exploitation; stop higher Panchayats taking over lower-level powers – so "**all of the above**".
[83:2:5] - **NOT an objective:** creating **autonomous regions** (that is the Sixth Schedule) – UPSC 2013.
[83:2:6] # Gram Sabha powers
[83:2:7] TABLE head: Subject | Power
  [83:2:7.0] Plans and projects | Approves before the village Panchayat takes them up; identifies beneficiaries
  [83:2:7.1] Use of funds | Village Panchayat must get a certificate of utilisation of funds from the Gram Sabha (mandatory)
  [83:2:7.2] Traditions | Safeguards customs, cultural identity, community resources, customary dispute resolution
  [83:2:7.3] Land acquisition / resettlement | Consultation (not consent)
  [83:2:7.4] Minor minerals | Recommendation mandatory for prospecting licence / mining lease – minor minerals only, not "any mineral"
  [83:2:7.5] Minor forest produce | Ownership
  [83:2:7.6] Tribal land | Prevent alienation; restore unlawfully alienated land
  [83:2:7.7] Liquor, money-lending, village markets | Prohibit / regulate; control; manage village markets
[83:2:8] - **UPSC 2012:** stop land transfer + MFP ownership correct, "recommendation for **any** mineral" wrong → **1 and 2 only**.
[83:2:9] - **Reservation:** STs at least **one-half** of seats; **all chairpersons ST**; State may nominate unrepresented tribes (≤ one-tenth).
[83:2:10] - **Gram Sabha meeting:** presided over by an **ST member elected by the Gram Sabha** (not the Sarpanch), for one year; else the oldest ST woman present.
[83:2:11] - Gram Sabha may be at **habitation** level (para, majra, tola); conflicting State laws lapse **one year** after assent.
[83:2:12] - **Zila Panchayat:** minor water bodies, social-sector institutions, Tribal Sub-Plans.
[83:2:13] - **Implementation gaps:** minor-mineral and MFP provisions least implemented; **40%+** PESA representatives could not explain a Gram Sabha (MoPR, Dec 2025); Tana Bhagats – no Gram Sabha consent for Bharatmala; **Odisha** – only draft rules (Apr 2026).
[83:2:14] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.108-110); NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 24 p.4; app notes 2:83
## SUB 3 | Andhra Pradesh – Scheduled Areas, PESA and ITDAs
[83:3:0] - **AP PESA law:** **AP Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 1998 (Act 7 of 1998)** amended the AP PR Act 1994 – AP implemented PESA from **1998**; **AP PESA Rules, 2011** (G.O.Ms.No.66, PR&RD, 24 Mar 2011).
[83:3:1] - **AP PESA Rules, 2011:** the **Gram (village) Panchayat** concerned acts as the **market committee** for village markets/shandies in Scheduled Areas.
[83:3:2] - **PESA districts (13-district map):** **5** – Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, **Visakhapatnam**, East Godavari, West Godavari; since **April 2022** the agency tracts lie mainly in **Alluri Sitharama Raju** (carved from Visakhapatnam) and **Parvathipuram Manyam** districts.
[83:3:3] - **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:** **s.29 + its Sixth Schedule** amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950** for AP (the Act's own Sixth Schedule, not the Constitution's).
[83:3:4] - **Agency tracts** of the **Eastern Ghats**; **34** ST communities; **2,038** PESA Gram Sabhas.
[83:3:5] - **7 ITDAs, 76 mandals:** **Paderu, Rampachodavaram, Chintoor** (Alluri Sitharama Raju; Chintoor – Godavari Koya belt); **Seethampeta, Parvathipuram** (Parvathipuram Manyam); **KR Puram** (Eluru); **Srisailam** (Chenchus, Nallamala).
[83:3:6] - **Alluri Sitharama Raju** district: tribal-majority, with **PVTGs**; **Araku** – ST Lok Sabha seat; **Tribal Medical College, Paderu** (2024-25, 50 seats).
[83:3:7] - **PESA Mahotsav** (30 years of PESA) – **Visakhapatnam**, Dec 2025.
[83:3:8] ~~ Sources: MCRHRDI "Implementation of PESA Act" slides (mcrhrdi.gov.in, 2026); 5-district list: APPSC key + general knowledge, not checked; advocatekhoj.com AP Reorganisation Act 2014, Sixth Schedule; app notes 2:83
## SUB 4 | Land, Forest Rights and Landmark Cases
[83:4:0] - **Samatha v. State of AP (1997, SC):** transfer/lease of **tribal land in Scheduled Areas to private parties for mining** is **null and void** – under the **Fifth Schedule**.
[83:4:1] - **AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959**, amended by **Regulation 1 of 1970** – bars transfers between tribals and non-tribals and among non-tribals.
[83:4:2] - **Forest Rights Act, 2006:** the **Gram Sabha** is the authority to **initiate the process** of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights; MFP ownership; diversion for public utilities needs Gram Sabha recommendation; OTFDs – **three generations (75 years)** before 2005.
[83:4:3] - **Niyamgiri (2013):** Gram Sabhas decided whether bauxite mining affected their **religious and forest rights** – rejected **Vedanta**.
[83:4:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket Polity Part 2 p.10; Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 p.110; app notes 2:83
## SUB 5 | Fifth vs Sixth Schedule and Committees
[83:5:0] TABLE head: Basis | Fifth Schedule | Sixth Schedule
  [83:5:0.0] Article | 244(1) | 244(2), 275(1)
  [83:5:0.1] Called | Scheduled Areas | Tribal Areas
  [83:5:0.2] States | 10 (AP, Telangana …) | Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
  [83:5:0.3] Key body | Tribes Advisory Council (advisory) | Autonomous District / Regional Councils (legislative, judicial)
  [83:5:0.4] Union | Can give directions | Stays within State executive
  [83:5:0.5] PESA | Applies | Does not apply
[83:5:1] - **Bearing on education:** DPSP, rural and urban local bodies (Eleventh/Twelfth Schedules), **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** (district councils run primary schools) and the Seventh Schedule – **all five** (UPSC 2012).
[83:5:2] TABLE head: Committee | Year | Note
  [83:5:2.0] U.N. Dhebar Commission | 1960-61 | First Scheduled Areas and ST Commission
  [83:5:2.1] Lokur Committee | 1965 | Five ST criteria
  [83:5:2.2] Dilip Singh Bhuria Committee | 1995 | Basis of PESA (MoRD)
  [83:5:2.3] Bhuria Commission | 2002-04 | Second Scheduled Areas Commission
  [83:5:2.4] Virginius Xaxa Committee | 2013 (PMO); report May 2014 | Tribal socio-economic status
[83:5:3] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.42 p.142-143; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams 25 p.14; app notes 2:83
## SUB 6 | Scheduled Tribes – Articles and Data
[83:6:0] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [83:6:0.0] 15(4) | Special provisions for educational advancement (seats, scholarships)
  [83:6:0.1] 46 | DPSP – educational and economic interests of SCs, STs
  [83:6:0.2] 164(1) proviso | Tribal welfare Minister – Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP, Odisha (94th Amendment, 2006 dropped Bihar)
  [83:6:0.3] 243M | Part IX not to apply to Scheduled and Tribal Areas
  [83:6:0.4] 275(1) | Grants-in-aid for ST welfare and Scheduled Areas – an economic safeguard
  [83:6:0.5] 330 / 332 | ST seats in Lok Sabha / State Assemblies
  [83:6:0.6] 338A | NCST – 89th Amendment, 2003
  [83:6:0.7] 339 | Union control over Scheduled Area administration and ST welfare
  [83:6:0.8] 342 | President, after consulting the Governor, notifies STs; later changes only by Parliament by law
  [83:6:0.9] 371A / 371C | Nagaland / Manipur hill-area committee
[83:6:1] - **ST vs SC:** ST status is **religion-neutral**; SC status only Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists.
[83:6:2] - **Census 2011:** STs **8.6%**; about **705** groups; largest tribe **Bhil**; largest ST population **Madhya Pradesh**; no STs notified in **Punjab**, Haryana, Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry.
[83:6:3] - **NCST focus:** ownership of minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, rehabilitation.

  1 and 2 only | 2 and 3 only | *1 and 3 only | 1, 2 and 3
  x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the TAC is advisory, with no legislative or judicial power.

  x: The Lokur Committee (1965) set the five classic tests for listing a group as a Scheduled Tribe: primitive traits, distinct culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness.
