=== NOTES 2:84 | Panchayati Raj and Urban Bodies in Andhra Pradesh – Structure, Elections, Finances, Performance
## SUB 0 | Gram Panchayat at Work – Sarpanch, Panchayat Secretary, Meetings
[84:0:0] # Who does what in a Gram Panchayat (AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994)
[84:0:1] TABLE head: Function | Answer
  [84:0:1.0] Convenes Gram Panchayat meetings | Panchayat Secretary – with the approval of, or on the direction of, the Sarpanch (s.31); the Sarpanch directs that the meeting be held
  [84:0:1.1] Presides over GP meetings | Sarpanch; in his absence the Upa-Sarpanch
  [84:0:1.2] Implements resolutions of the GP and its committees | Panchayat Secretary (the executive authority)
  [84:0:1.3] Collects taxes; calculates house tax of a new building | Panchayat Secretary
  [84:0:1.4] Written permission for any advertisement in the village (s.64) | Panchayat Secretary (executive authority)
  [84:0:1.5] Expels a convicted bye-law offender from a public market (s.107) | Panchayat Secretary (executive authority)
  [84:0:1.6] Marriage Officer of the gram panchayat (appointed by the Governor) | Panchayat Secretary
  [84:0:1.7] Bans sewage on public roads, sanitation orders; cremation/burial of destitute bodies | Gram Panchayat (the body)
  [84:0:1.8] Scrutinises the records of the GP | Sarpanch
  [84:0:1.9] Forms Joint Action Committees for joint works and settles disputes between panchayats | Sarpanch
  [84:0:1.10] Reports epidemics, atrocities on SCs, prepares the draft BPL list | Panchayat Secretary
  [84:0:1.11] Reports births/bodies found in hospitals, jails, choultries, open places | the officer in charge / the person who first sees it
[84:0:2] - **Sarpanch:** **executive head** and political head of the GP; **directly elected**; **controls** the Panchayat Secretary.
[84:0:3] - **Panchayat Secretary:** the **Government's representative** (functionary) in each panchayat; **executive authority**; works under the **administrative control of the Gram Panchayat** and is its **immediate subordinate** (all officers and employees are **subordinate to the Gram Panchayat**, s.36(5)).
[84:0:4] - **Not** a Secretary's function: **school supervision** (his work is village administration, community welfare and community development).
[84:0:5] - **Appeal:** an order of the Panchayat Secretary granting, refusing, suspending or revoking a **licence or permission** → appeal to the **Gram Panchayat** (s.128).
[84:0:6] - **Obstruction:** wrongfully restraining the Secretary or his delegate from entering any place to exercise lawful powers is **an offence under the Indian Penal Code** (now the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023**).
[84:0:7] - **Annual report:** the Secretary prepares an **Administration Report** on the panchayat's governance each year, submitted by **May**.
[84:0:8] - **Other Acts:** the competent authority under the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948** can notify the Panchayat Secretary as an **Inspector**.
[84:0:9] - **Dissolution:** if a GP abuses its powers, the **State Government** (through the administration) can dissolve it.
[84:0:10] - **Body corporate:** every Gram Panchayat (and every Mandal Praja Parishad) is a **body corporate** with perpetual succession and a common seal.
[84:0:11] - **Disqualification:** contractors for the panchayat, its employees and honorary magistrates are disqualified; a person who served the last term as a **ward member can contest**.
[84:0:12] # Obligatory vs discretionary functions
[84:0:13] TABLE head: Type | Examples
  [84:0:13.0] Obligatory | Sanitation, drinking water, drains, street lighting, village roads, burial grounds
  [84:0:13.1] Discretionary | Tree planting, libraries, markets, mother-child welfare homes, modern farming practices
[84:0:14] - **Municipal Corporation:** **water supply** is an **obligatory** function; relief to destitutes, fairs and exhibitions and roadside tree planting are **discretionary**.
[84:0:15] - GP **property protection:** the 10% open-space land of layouts and parks is a **Category A** property to be protected; district **GP Properties Protection Wing** committees are supervised at the Commissionerate by the **Vigilance (Encroachment) Wing**.
[84:0:16] > Exam angle: "convenes / implements / collects / permits" = **Secretary**; "presides / directs / scrutinises / controls" = **Sarpanch**; "the body that orders" = **Gram Panchayat**.
[84:0:17] ~~ Sources: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 (simpliance.in text) s.31, s.36(5), s.64, s.107, s.128, s.148(4); app notes 2:84; APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys
[84:0:18] - **District authority:** the **Collector (Panchayat Raj)** is the district-level administrative authority of the Gram Panchayats.
## SUB 1 | Gram Panchayat Finances – Taxes, Accounts and Funds
[84:1:0] # Taxes (s.60)
[84:1:1] - **Compulsory taxes:** **House tax** (main own revenue, levied every year) and **Kolagaram / Katarusum** – tax on village produce sold in the village **by weight, measurement or number** (i.e. by weight and by volume).
[84:1:2] - **Optional taxes:** a **vehicle tax** and a **tax on agricultural land for a specific purpose**.
[84:1:3] - **Land cess:** 2 naya paise in the rupee on annual rental value; a fee for a specific purpose over and above taxes on land is a **cess**.
[84:1:4] - **Surcharge on land:** with the prescribed authority's prior approval, up to **25 naya paise in the rupee** (s.60(5)).
[84:1:5] - **Betterment charges:** **Rs 50 per sq m** in GPs under a municipal master plan, at mandal headquarters, or with 10,000+ population.
[84:1:6] - **Gated Community:** minimum site area **1000 sq m** (AP key).
[84:1:7] - **Not** a source of GP funds: **fees on services to SHGs** (taxes, Central grants and loans are).
[84:1:8] # Accounts
[84:1:9] - **Model Accounting System (MAS)** – the framework prepared by the **Central Government** (MoPR with the **C&AG**, 2009); PRIs keep accounts on a **cash basis**.
[84:1:10] - MAS classifies transactions on a **three-tier structure**: **Function (Major Head), Programme (Minor Head), Object (Object Head)**; "weekly upgradation of accounts" is **not** a MAS feature.
[84:1:11] - Book-keeping: **double entry** (PRIASoft); some keys say "both single and double entry".
[84:1:12] - **PRIASoft** – MoPR's web-based **accounting software for PRIs**, for accountability and transparency; the most popular accounting application in panchayats.
[84:1:13] - Fiscal year ends **31 March**; salaries paid through the **Acquittance Register**; durable goods first entered in the **Stock Register**; approved bills stamped **"Paid and cancelled"**.
[84:1:14] - Working balance: at least **5%** of estimated receipts; surplus money invested for at most **three years**; contractor's **EMD 2.5%** of the estimate; **10%** of GP funds for welfare activities.
[84:1:15] - **Surcharge certificate** – enforceable like a **civil court decree**.
[84:1:16] - **Zilla Parishad markets:** income shared **35 : 65** among PRIs.
[84:1:17] - **Internal audit** of Zilla Praja Parishads – inspected by the **Commissioner, Panchayat Raj**.
[84:1:18] - **m-FMS pilot** (Government of India) in AP – **East Godavari** district.
[84:1:19] # Devolution and State Finance Commissions
[84:1:20] - **SFC** (243I/243Y) – formed by the **Governor** (not the SEC) every five years; Part VI of the 1994 Act. **4th SFC** report Oct 2019; **5th SFC** constituted 20 March 2023 for **2025-30**.
[84:1:21] - **3rd SFC** per-capita grant **ZP : MP : GP = Rs 8 : 16 : 8**.
[84:1:22] - **14th and 15th FC** grants favoured **drinking water and sanitation**. **16th FC (2026-31):** AP rural local bodies **Rs 16,627 crore** (AP Budget 2026-27); only **duly constituted** (elected) bodies get grants.
[84:1:23] - **Main own revenue of a GP – property (house) tax**; intermediate and district tiers rely on grants.
[84:1:24] - **Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program:** GP own revenue **≥ Rs 50 lakh** (Block ≥ Rs 1 crore).
[84:1:25] - **3Fs – Funds, Functions, Functionaries** – still not fully devolved.
[84:1:26] TABLE head: Devolution Index (MoPR-TISS 2015-16) component | Weight
  [84:1:26.0] Transfer of Finances | 50
  [84:1:26.1] Transfer of Functionaries | 15
  [84:1:26.2] Autonomy of PRIs | 15
  [84:1:26.3] Transfer of Functions | 10
[84:1:27] ~~ Sources: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 (simpliance.in text) s.60, s.61; MoPR-TISS Devolution Report 2015-16 p.71 (Table 2.2), p.99; app notes 2:84; APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys
## SUB 2 | Evolution of Panchayati Raj in AP – Acts and Committees
[84:2:0] # Order among States
[84:2:1] - **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957)** – accepted by the **NDC, January 1958**; three tiers – **Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad** (no Mandal Parishad); **Panchayat Samiti** the executive body; the **Zilla Parishad approves the Samiti's budget**.
[84:2:2] - **Rajasthan** first – **Nehru** inaugurated it on **2 October 1959** at **Nagaur**; **Andhra Pradesh** second – **1 November 1959**.
[84:2:3] - **Kasu Brahmananda Reddy** – Minister for Local Bodies in N. Sanjiva Reddy's cabinet.
[84:2:4] # AP laws
[84:2:5] TABLE head: Law / reform | Year
  [84:2:5.0] AP Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act (first AP law) | 1959 (amended 1961: standing committees 5 → 7)
  [84:2:5.1] AP Gram Panchayats Act – integrated Andhra and Telangana panchayats; provided for the Gram Sabha | 1964
  [84:2:5.2] Mandal system (NTR Government, Act 31 of 1986): Panchayat Samithis abolished → Mandal Praja Parishads; ZPs → Zilla Praja Parishads | 1986
  [84:2:5.3] AP Panchayat Raj Act (Act 13 of 1994) – incorporates the 73rd Amendment | 21 April 1994
  [84:2:5.4] AP Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act for Scheduled Areas (PESA) | 1998
[84:2:6] - **1104 mandals** were formed in united AP after the Samithis were abolished.
[84:2:7] - 1994 Act: **278 sections**; Part II Gram Panchayat; III Mandal Parishads; IV Zilla Parishads; V elections; VI Finance Commission; **s.40** – functional committees at GP level (agriculture, public health, water supply, sanitation, education …).
[84:2:8] - **Revenue village** (s.3): a local area recognised as a village in the revenue accounts, after excluding municipal, cantonment and similar areas.
[84:2:9] - The 1986 Mandal system drew on **Ashok Mehta**'s "Mandal Panchayat".
[84:2:10] # AP committees on Panchayati Raj
[84:2:11] TABLE head: Committee | Key recommendation
  [84:2:11.0] Vengala Rao (AP) | No party symbols in panchayat polls; reduce the importance of the Sarpanch
  [84:2:11.1] C. Narasimham (AP) | Direct election of the Sarpanch; model AP Panchayat Raj on Maharashtra
  [84:2:11.2] Purushottam Pai (AP) | Categorisation of Blocks
  [84:2:11.3] B.P.R. Vithal (AP) | Taluk Panchayat Samithis for 80,000–1,00,000 population
  [84:2:11.4] Ashok Mehta (1977-78) | Two tiers (ZP + Mandal Panchayat); party participation
  [84:2:11.5] G.V.K. Rao (1985) | PRIs "grass without roots"
  [84:2:11.6] L.M. Singhvi (1986) | Constitutional recognition; Gram Sabha as direct democracy
  [84:2:11.7] Thungon (1988) | ZP as pivot; supersession max six months; constitutional recognition
[84:2:12] - **N.T. Rama Rao** – Chief Minister three times between 1983 and 1994 (1983, 1984, 1985) and again in 1994; brought the Mandal system.
[84:2:13] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.39 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt) p.97; AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 (simpliance.in text) s.3, s.40; app notes 2:84; APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys
## SUB 3 | Three Tiers, Elections and the AP State Election Commission
[84:3:0] TABLE head: Tier | Members | Head and mode | Term / age
  [84:3:0.0] Gram Panchayat | Ward members, directly elected | Sarpanch, directly elected | 5 years; 21
  [84:3:0.1] Mandal Parishad | MPTC members, directly elected | MPP President, indirect from MPTCs | 5 years; 21
  [84:3:0.2] Zilla Parishad | ZPTC members, directly elected | ZP Chairperson, indirectly elected from ZPTCs | 5 years; 21
[84:3:1] - AP's intermediate tier = **Mandal Parishad**, not Panchayat Samiti; **13 Zilla Praja Parishads → 28** after district reorganisation.
[84:3:2] - **Article 243C:** village chairperson's mode left to the State; intermediate and district chairpersons indirect.
[84:3:3] - **Members:** a GP of population **up to 300** has **5 members including the Sarpanch**. **Mandal Parishad permanent invitees – five** (Collector, Sarpanches, ZPTC member, ZP Chairperson, Agricultural Market Committee President; no vote); one minority member co-opted.
[84:3:4] - **Zilla Praja Parishad:** **7 standing committees** (1994 Act).
[84:3:5] - **Non-party polls:** **Gram Panchayat** (Sarpanch and ward) polls are **without party symbols** – no party competition at GP level; MPTC/ZPTC polls are on party symbols.
[84:3:6] - **Two-child norm:** s.19(3) – a person with **more than two children** was disqualified; removed by the AP Panchayat Raj and Municipal Laws (Amendment) Acts, **Nov 2024**.
[84:3:7] - GP governing bodies' tenure (2013 batch) ended on **01.08.2018**.
[84:3:8] # State Election Commission
[84:3:9] - **Art. 243K** (panchayats) + **243ZA** (municipalities); conducts all local polls – **not** co-operative polls.
[84:3:10] - **Commissioner:** appointed by the **Governor** for **five years**; **status of a High Court Judge**; removed only like a HC judge.
[84:3:11] - Original AP SEC formed **17 June 1994**; for residuary AP the Governor constituted the SEC on **30 January 2016**.
[84:3:12] - **Anil Chandra Punetha** – SEC (appointed Apr 2026).
[84:3:13] - **Nigha** – AP app (March 2020) for citizens to report poll irregularities (money, liquor) in local body elections.
[84:3:14] # Reservation and recent polls
[84:3:15] - SC/ST by population, **by rotation**; women **at least one-third**.
[84:3:16] - **AP Cabinet, 18 Aug 2026:** **34% BC** in rural bodies; Mandal Parishad Presidents stay indirect.
[84:3:17] - **Unanimous-election incentives (Jan 2021):** Rs 5 lakh (< 2,000), 10 lakh, 15 lakh, 20 lakh (> 10,000); 2021 panchayat polls in **four phases**.
[84:3:18] - **Sarpanch honorarium** – Rs **3,000** a month (APPSC key).
[84:3:19] ~~ Sources: AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 (simpliance.in text) s.7, s.19(3), s.149, s.158; app notes 2:84; APPSC Panchayat Secretary keys
## SUB 4 | Gram Sabha, MGNREGA and Community Organisations
[84:4:0] - **Gram Sabha** (Art. 243A; defined in **Art. 243(b)**) – all persons registered in the electoral rolls of the panchayat area; convened and presided over by the Sarpanch (or Upa-Sarpanch).
[84:4:1] - **Article 243G** – powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats: plans for **economic development and social justice** – the main objective of PRIs.
[84:4:2] - **Requisition:** the Sarpanch must call a Gram Sabha on a written request of **10% of members or 50 members**.
[84:4:3] - **MGNREGA works** are identified by the **Gram Panchayat on the recommendation of the Gram Sabha and Ward Sabhas**.
[84:4:4] - **MGNREGA social audit** in AP culminates in an **open meeting (public hearing) at mandal level on the 7th day**.
[84:4:5] - **Community-based organisations** for PR purposes: **SHGs, Village Organisations, Mandal Samakhyas** – **not political parties**; SHGs must **encourage members to attend Gram Sabhas**.
[84:4:6] - **Gram Samvaad** – app giving single-window access to rural-development programme information at GP level.
[84:4:7] - **Jamabandi** – annual check (audit) of village revenue accounts.

## SUB 5 | Urban Local Bodies in AP
[84:5:0] - **AP SES 2025-26:** **123 ULBs = 17 Municipal Corporations + 76 Municipalities + 30 Nagar Panchayats** (16 corporations at the time of the older APPSC paper).
[84:5:1] TABLE head: Law | Key fact
  [84:5:1.0] AP Municipalities Act, 1965 | In force 2 April 1965; Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats
  [84:5:1.1] AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 | Corporations; Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act, 1955 as parent law
[84:5:2] - Municipal grades by **annual income**: Special, Selection, Grade I, II, III.
[84:5:3] - **Nagar Panchayat** – transitional area (243Q); classified by population, density, revenue, % non-farm employment.
[84:5:4] - **Article 243W** – State Legislature may endow Municipalities with powers and authority.
[84:5:5] - **33.33% BC quota** in ULBs under the **1994 and 1965 Acts** (not the PR Act).
[84:5:6] - **AP Municipal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024** – Minister **P. Narayana**; passed **without debate**; **removed the two-child norm** for municipal polls, to address the falling fertility rate (CM N. Chandrababu Naidu) – both statements correct.
[84:5:7] - **AP Municipal Laws (Third Amendment) Bill 2026** – **Uniform Mutation Fee**.
[84:5:8] - Mayor so far **indirect**; **AP Cabinet (18 Aug 2026)** approved **direct election** of Mayors and Chairpersons.
[84:5:9] - Corporation = Council (Mayor) + **Standing Committees** + Commissioner; **GVMC** has zonal commissioners.
[84:5:10] - First Municipal Corporation – **Madras (1688)**; 74th Amendment – Part IX-A, **243P–243ZG**, 18 subjects.
[84:5:11] - **APCRDA** (Act **2014**); **VMRDA** (2018); UDAs are **not under ULBs**.
[84:5:12] - **AIIB**-aided AP Urban Water Supply Project – 50 ULBs.

=== NOTES 2:86 | Actors in Policy-making – Executive, Legislature, Judiciary, Bureaucracy, Media, Civil Society, Think Tanks
## SUB 0 | Media and Civil Society
[86:0:0] - Mass media **shape the image of political personalities**, because of the outlet's **ideology and treatment of news** – (A) true, (R) the correct explanation.
[86:0:1] - **Free press** is necessary for a vibrant democracy; **new media** allow participatory, two-way communication – **both true**, but (R) does not explain (A).
[86:0:2] - **Fleet Street** (London) – historic centre of the **British newspapers**.
[86:0:3] - Speaking **from the floor instead of the dais** shows the audience a sense of **equality**.
[86:0:4] - **PIB** – briefings, accreditation, social media; **PM's Communication Wing** – PMO/Cabinet publicity (separate bodies).
[86:0:5] TABLE head: Campaign | Law
  [86:0:5.0] MKSS (Aruna Roy, Rajasthan) | RTI Act 2005
  [86:0:5.1] Right to Work / NAC | MGNREGA 2005
  [86:0:5.2] Right to Food (PUCL PIL 2001) | NFSA 2013 – the Right to Food Act that followed the RTE Act (2009)
[86:0:6] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:86; APPSC-GS 2018 keys
## SUB 1 | Executive and Bureaucracy
[86:1:0] - **Cabinet and Cabinet Committees** take key decisions – **policy making** is the Cabinet's major function.
[86:1:1] - **Cabinet Secretariat** – headed by the **Cabinet Secretary**, directly under the PM; runs the **Transaction of Business Rules**.
[86:1:2] - **PMO** – the PM's policy office; got the name **PMO in 1977** (earlier PM's Secretariat, 1947); headed by the **Principal Secretary to the PM**, **not** the Cabinet Secretary.
[86:1:3] - **NITI Aayog (2015)** replaced the Planning Commission; **non-constitutional, non-statutory**; chaired by the **Prime Minister**; cooperative federalism. Vice Chairperson **Ashok Kumar Lahiri** (2026).
[86:1:4] - **Permanent executive:** All-India Services, State services; advises, drafts, implements; concern – **discretion at the front line of implementation**.
[86:1:5] - **Split system** – separates **policy (Secretariat) from implementation (executive departments)**.
[86:1:6] - Recruitment by **UPSC and State PSCs**; PSC members removed for misbehaviour after a **Supreme Court inquiry**.
[86:1:7] - **Manifesto → policy:** **33.33% BC quota** in AP ULBs – an **NDA 2024 poll promise** – via **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** (Aug 2026).
[86:1:8] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:86; UPSC CSE 2019 key (PMO)
## SUB 2 | Legislature
[86:2:0] - **Parliament** – the **highest forum of debate** in the country and chief law-maker; but the **Cabinet decides substance and timing**; bureaucracy drafts Government Bills.
[86:2:1] - **Question Hour** – most effective control; also Zero Hour, adjournment motions, financial control.
[86:2:2] - Bills referred to committees: **71% (15th Lok Sabha) → 16% (17th Lok Sabha)**.
[86:2:3] TABLE head: Option against an SC decision | Limit
  [86:2:3.0] New law removing the basis of the judgment | Cannot simply overrule
  [86:2:3.1] Constitutional amendment (Art. 368) | Basic structure (Kesavananda Bharati)
  [86:2:3.2] Review / curative petition | Same Court
[86:2:4] - Examples: **Muslim Women Act 1986** after **Shah Bano**; **SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018** after **Subhash Kashinath Mahajan**.
[86:2:5] - **Article 143** reference – advisory opinion only, not binding.
[86:2:6] - **Accountability gaps:** Governors and Speakers **delay assent and Tenth Schedule decisions**; RTI backlog.
[86:2:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:86
## SUB 3 | Judiciary and PIL
[86:3:0] - **PIL began 1979** – filed **on behalf of prisoners**; basis **Arts. 32, 226, 142**.
[86:3:1] - **Overreach:** policy paralysis, backlog; PIL misused for **publicity or political ends**.
[86:3:2] - **Upendra Baxi's** fears: ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation, democratic (**not electoral**).
[86:3:3] TABLE head: Case | Guidelines acting as law
  [86:3:3.0] Vishaka (1997) | Workplace sexual harassment – until POSH Act 2013
  [86:3:3.1] Prakash Singh (2006) | Police reforms; fixed DGP tenure
  [86:3:3.2] T.S.R. Subramanian (2013) | Civil Services Boards; fixed tenure
[86:3:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:86
[86:3:5] - **PIL** – justice for the **poor, needy and weaker sections**, often with the help of **NGOs and the media**; any public-spirited person may move the court.
## SUB 4 | Stakeholders of Governance and Think Tanks
[86:4:0] TABLE head: Set | Includes
  [86:4:0.0] State | Legislature, judiciary, executive, bureaucracy
  [86:4:0.1] Market | Private sector
  [86:4:0.2] Civil Society | NGOs, VOs, media, trade unions, religious and pressure groups
[86:4:1] # Think tank type → Examples
[86:4:2] TABLE head: Think tank type | Examples
  [86:4:2.0] Government | NITI Aayog (DMEO); National Innovation Council (2010)
  [86:4:2.1] Independent | CPR, NCAER, PRS, ORF
  [86:4:2.2] Party-linked | Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation (BJP); Rajiv Gandhi Foundation (Congress)
[86:4:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:86

=== NOTES 2:87 | Governance and Good Governance – Meaning, Dimensions, World Bank/undp Indicators
## SUB 0 | Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Andhra Pradesh and Governance Institutes
[87:0:0] - **CGG** – set up by the Government of (undivided) **AP in 2001**, in **Hyderabad**, in collaboration with **DFID (UK) and the World Bank**; a governance-reform **think tank**.
[87:0:1] - **NCGG** – autonomous institute, upgraded from the National Institute of Administrative Research (LBSNAA); head office **New Delhi**, branch **Mussoorie**.
[87:0:2] - DARPG tools: **NeSDA (2019)**, Citizen's Charter portal, **CPGRAMS**; **National Awards for e-Governance** – a **DARPG** scheme.
[87:0:3] - **Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance** (AP): **500+ services**; **Rs 100 crore** for RTGS in 2026-27.
[87:0:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:87; APPSC Group 1 keys 2021, 2023
## SUB 1 | Features of Good Governance – UN/UNDP
[87:1:0] - The **8 attributes:** **consensus oriented, participatory, rule of law, effective and efficient, accountable, transparent, responsive, equitable and inclusive**.
[87:1:1] - UNDP's **three most critical**: transparency, accountability, responsiveness.
[87:1:2] - **NOT** features: **religiosity and emotionality**, **red tapism**, administrative **centralisation**, secrecy.
[87:1:3] - **Centralisation** may **reduce efficiency** of service delivery for lack of local adaptation to diverse contexts.
[87:1:4] TABLE head: Pillar | Meaning
  [87:1:4.0] Ethos | Service
  [87:1:4.1] Ethics | Honesty and integrity
  [87:1:4.2] Equity | Empathy for weaker sections
  [87:1:4.3] Efficiency | Speedy delivery using ICT
[87:1:5] - Tools: **people's participation** (most basic), RTI, Sevottam, Citizen's Charters, e-governance.
[87:1:6] > Exam angle: "which is NOT a feature" – red tapism, religiosity, centralisation.
[87:1:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:87; Jharkhand PCS 2016, 2021 keys
## SUB 2 | Meaning of Governance – Definitions and Origin
[87:2:0] TABLE head: Body | Definition / stress
  [87:2:0.0] World Bank | "The manner in which power is exercised in the management of a country's economic and social resources for development"
  [87:2:0.1] UNDP (1997) | Exercise of economic, political and administrative authority to manage a country's affairs at all levels
  [87:2:0.2] UNESCAP | Efficiency, effectiveness, equity, sustainability
[87:2:1] - **"Good governance"** was first brought into development discourse by the **World Bank** (1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa).
[87:2:2] - **Governance is broader than government**: **state + market + civil society**.
[87:2:3] - **Democracy** helps development by encouraging **citizen participation and accountability**.
[87:2:4] - **Aristotle**: "A good citizen makes a good state and a bad citizen a bad state".
[87:2:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:87; general knowledge (Aristotle)
## SUB 3 | Good Governance Day and the Good Governance Index
[87:3:0] - **Good Governance Day – 25 December**, birthday of **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**; first observed in **2014**.
[87:3:1] - **GGI** – launched by **DARPG** on Good Governance Day 2019; ranks States, UTs, districts; revised **every two years**; **10 sectors** (agriculture, commerce and industry, HRD, public health, public infrastructure, economic governance, social welfare, judicial and public security, environment, citizen-centric governance); **foreign affairs is NOT** a sector.
[87:3:2] - **GGI 2021** (25 Dec 2021; **58 indicators**): **Gujarat** 1st, then Maharashtra, Goa; **AP 1st in agriculture and allied**.
[87:3:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:87
## SUB 4 | Governance Indices – World Bank, UNDP and Others
[87:4:0] - **World Bank WGI** – since **1996**, 200+ countries; **DARPG** is India's nodal department; **six dimensions**: Voice and Accountability; Political Stability and Absence of Violence; Government Effectiveness; Regulatory Quality; Rule of Law; Control of Corruption. **HDI is NOT** a WGI dimension.
[87:4:1] - **UNDP Human Development Index** – **three basic dimensions**: long and healthy life, knowledge (education), decent standard of living.
[87:4:2] TABLE head: Index | Publisher | Latest
  [87:4:2.0] Good Governance Index; GRAI | DARPG | GRAI June 2026
  [87:4:2.1] Public Affairs Index | Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru | PAI 2018: Kerala best-governed large State
  [87:4:2.2] BRAP rankings | DPIIT (not NITI) | –
  [87:4:2.3] SDG India Index; National MPI | NITI Aayog | –
  [87:4:2.4] Investment Friendliness Index 2026 | NITI Aayog | Gujarat 1st
  [87:4:2.5] V-Dem | University of Gothenburg | India 106th of 179 (2026)
  [87:4:2.6] Responsible Nations Index | WIF, JNU, IIM Mumbai | India 16th of 154 (2026)
[87:4:3] - **WGI and V-Dem** are perception-based (expert opinion).
[87:4:4] - **India (WGI 2023):** moderate government effectiveness and rule of law; **low political stability**.
[87:4:5] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (src/economy/ramesh-singh-indian-economy-03.txt) p.55 (HDI); app notes 2:87
## SUB 5 | Second ARC – Ethics and Citizen-centric Administration
[87:5:0] - **Second ARC** set up **2005**; **15 reports**.
[87:5:1] TABLE head: Report | Year | Content
  [87:5:1.0] 4th – "Ethics in Governance" | 2007 | Codes of ethics, anti-corruption bodies
  [87:5:1.1] 12th – "Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance" | 2009 | Citizen's Charters, Sevottam; identifies the barriers to good governance
[87:5:2] - **Mission Satyanishta** – **Indian Railways** programme on ethics in public governance.
[87:5:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:87

=== NOTES 2:88 | E-governance – Models, Types of Interaction, NeGP, Digital India and Governance Outcomes
## SUB 0 | Andhra Pradesh E-governance Initiatives
[88:0:0] # Initiative → year → purpose
[88:0:1] TABLE head: Initiative | Year | Purpose
  [88:0:1.0] CARD (Computer-aided Administration of Registration Department) | 1998 | Complete computerisation of land/property registration – valuation, stamp duty, document scanning; newer version CARD-PRIMME (Sept 2023)
  [88:0:1.1] APSWAN (AP State Wide Area Network) | 1998-99 | Data/voice network linking the Secretariat with District (and mandal) administration – the G2G backbone
  [88:0:1.2] eSeva | 2001 | AP's pioneering integrated citizen service centres (bills, certificates)
  [88:0:1.3] e-Procurement | 2003 | Online tendering to stop collusion
  [88:0:1.4] Prajavani | Nov 2005 (Ranga Reddy district collector) | Web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of public grievances at District Collectorates, built with NIC; a public-private partnership letting citizens reach government without visiting an office; improved version of UP's Lokvani
  [88:0:1.5] MeeSeva ("At your service") | 2011 | Single-window G2C service centres
  [88:0:1.6] Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) | 2017 | AI, Big Data, GIS, IoT, real-time dashboards, Data Lake, Command and Control Centre
  [88:0:1.7] CM CORE Dashboard | – | Real-time dashboard for data-led decision making (not Meekosam or AP Fibergrid)
  [88:0:1.8] e-Pragati | – | Whole-of-government state enterprise architecture / unified state service portal; "faceless, paperless, cashless"
[88:0:2] - **e-Pragati is NOT** a network of district treasuries; **CARD ≠ MeeSeva** (MeeSeva = service centres; Spandana = grievance status).
[88:0:3] - Chronology: **CARD 1998 → eSeva 2001 → e-Procurement 2003 → MeeSeva 2011 → RTGS 2017**.
[88:0:4] - **Jawahar Knowledge Centres (JKC):** trained college students in technical and soft skills for employability; run by the **Institute for Electronic Governance (IEG)**, a society under the **IT&C Department** (not AP Online or APSFL).
[88:0:5] - **AP grievance sequence:** Prajavani → **Meekosam** (soft launch Feb 2015 in **Krishna and Anantapuram**; statewide **26 May 2015**) → **Spandana** (2019) → AI-based **Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS)**; Jan 2026: AI grievance redress and **Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance**.
[88:0:6] - AP's Prajavani differs from **Telangana's Prajavani** (8 Dec 2023, Praja Bhavan, Hyderabad).
[88:0:7] - **2026** declared AP's **Technology-Driven Decision Making Year** (CM Naidu).
[88:0:8] - **PRIASoft** (Panchayati Raj Institutions Accounting Software) – developed by **NIC** for the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
[88:0:9] > Angles: which AP project computerised land registration (CARD ×2), grievance portal at Collectorates (Prajavani ×2), Secretariat–district network (APSWAN), JKC society, data-led decisions (CORE).
[88:0:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 (src/science-tech/nextgen-st-group2-03.txt) p.26 (CARD), p.30 (e-Pragati); app's current notes 2:88 sub 7
## SUB 1 | National Digital Platforms and Services
[88:1:0] TABLE head: Platform | Expansion / nature | Key fact
  [88:1:0.0] ERSS | Emergency Response Support System | Single pan-India emergency number 112 (from 2019; launched for women's safety first in 16 States); AP signed an MoU with NDMA for ERSS on 13 Aug 2021
  [88:1:0.1] GeM | Government e-Marketplace | 2016, Commerce Ministry; one-stop online procurement of goods and services by government departments and PSUs (not MyGov, e-Kranti or eNAM)
  [88:1:0.2] e-Sampark | NIC/MyGov mailing system | Sends informational and public-service messages to citizens by e-mail/SMS
  [88:1:0.3] UMANG | Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance | Launched Nov 2017; 162 services from 33 departments and 4 States at launch; central and state services (tax, EPF, gas, passport) via web, SMS, IVR; DigiLocker integrated (Oct 2024)
  [88:1:0.4] BHIM | Bharat Interface for Money | Launched 30 Dec 2016; built on UPI (Unified Payments Interface, NPCI)
  [88:1:0.5] DigiLocker | Cloud locker for documents | Launched Feb 2015; key Digital India initiative; ~72 crore users (Aug 2026)
  [88:1:0.6] MyGov | Citizen-engagement platform | Participative governance
  [88:1:0.7] MeghRaj | GI Cloud | Hosts government applications
  [88:1:0.8] CSC | Common Service Centres | Village-level ICT kiosks for G2C services
  [88:1:0.9] Aadhaar | 12-digit biometric identity (UIDAI, Jan 2009) | First Aadhaar numbers: 29 Sep 2010, Tembhli (Nandurbar, Maharashtra); Aadhaar Act 2016, amended 2019; proof of identity, not citizenship
[88:1:1] - **ERSS = 112**, not 100/108/1090; CSCs have no link with 112.
[88:1:2] - **e-tendering:** suppliers **purchase tender documents and submit bids online**; the department raises indents, publishes the NIT and awards the contract.
[88:1:3] - **Trakea:** bar-coding software adopted by **Haryana Police (2019)** so that forensic reports cannot be tampered with.
[88:1:4] - **e-Governance = Electronic Governance.**
[88:1:5] > Angles: ERSS full form and number (×4), GeM (×2), BHIM–UPI, e-Sampark, first Aadhaar year, e-tendering, Trakea.

## SUB 2 | E-governance Awards and Conferences
[88:2:0] # National Awards for e-Governance (NAeG)
[88:2:1] - Instituted by **DARPG** (Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions) with MeitY; started **2003**; presented at the **National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG)**.
[88:2:2] - **2025** awards (with Ministry of Panchayati Raj): first-ever dedicated category for **Gram Panchayats**.
[88:2:3] - **NAeG 2026** (29th NCeG): 17 projects in 7 categories; **Rohini Gram Panchayat (Dhule, Maharashtra) – Gold**; e-Jagriti – Silver.
[88:2:4] # NCeG – hosts and themes
[88:2:5] TABLE head: NCeG | Year | Host | Note
  [88:2:5.0] 20th | 9-10 Jan 2017 | Visakhapatnam, AP | AP Gold for Aadhaar-enabled PDS (citizen-centric service delivery) and for Loan Charge Creation (process re-engineering); sectoral award "Digital Transformation towards Transforming India" – MyGov (MeitY) Gold
  [88:2:5.1] 22nd | Aug 2019 | Shillong, Meghalaya | Theme "Digital India: Success to Excellence"; organised by DARPG and MeitY with Meghalaya (not a "Department of Public Policy and Governance"); momentum to e-governance in the North-East
  [88:2:5.2] 23rd | Feb 2020 | Mumbai, Maharashtra | –
  [88:2:5.3] 28th | 2025 | Visakhapatnam, AP | Visakhapatnam Declaration: extend NeSDA to low-connectivity areas (Ladakh, North-East); theme "Viksit Bharat: Civil Service & Digital Transformation"
  [88:2:5.4] 29th | 2026 | Jaipur, Rajasthan | Jaipur Declaration: DPI, AI-enabled governance, cybersecurity, data governance
[88:2:6] - NIC AP's **Punarvas** project (Kovvada nuclear plant compensation) won the NAeG 2018 Gold for district-level IT initiatives.
[88:2:7] > Angles: host city (×3), theme, AP's 2017 award, the 2017 sectoral award, NOT-true statement on the 22nd NCeG.

## SUB 3 | Digital Divide and Governance Outcomes
[88:3:0] TABLE head: Initiative | Purpose | Status
  [88:3:0.0] BharatNet | Optical-fibre broadband to Gram Panchayats | 2.15 lakh GPs connected (Mar 2026); Amended BharatNet (Aug 2023) targets 2.64 lakh GPs in ring topology
  [88:3:0.1] PM-WANI | Public Wi-Fi hotspots via PDOs and PDOAs (Department of Telecommunications) | Launched December 2020; 4.09 lakh hotspots (Mar 2026)
  [88:3:0.2] PMGDISHA | Rural digital literacy | 6.39 crore trained (31 Mar 2024)
[88:3:1] - **Digital divide** = gap between those with internet access and digital skills and those without; BharatNet = **infrastructure** gap, PM-WANI = **access** gap, PMGDISHA = **skills** gap.
[88:3:2] - Outcomes: transparency, speed, lower corruption; risks: digital divide, cyber security, data privacy.

## SUB 4 | E-governance – Meaning, Models and Types of Interaction
[88:4:0] # Meaning and significance
[88:4:1] - E-governance = use of ICT to deliver government services, information and transactions; aim **"faceless, paperless, cashless"**.
[88:4:2] - Significance: **citizen engagement**, better **service delivery**, fewer face-to-face contacts, **audit trails** (e-governance **strengthens** them – "removal of audit trails" is not a benefit).
[88:4:3] # Arie Halachmi – five models
[88:4:4] TABLE head: Model | Meaning
  [88:4:4.0] Broadcasting / wider dissemination | Government information put in the public domain
  [88:4:4.1] Critical flow | Critical information to a targeted audience (e.g. corruption data → ombudsman)
  [88:4:4.2] Comparative analysis | Learning from best practices elsewhere
  [88:4:4.3] E-advocacy / mobilisation and lobbying | Online civil-society networks influence decisions
  [88:4:4.4] Interactive service | Two-way G2C services (filing, payments, feedback)
[88:4:5] # Types of interaction
[88:4:6] TABLE head: Type | Meaning | Examples
  [88:4:6.0] G2C | Government to Citizen | Online certificates; UMANG, MeeSeva, eSeva
  [88:4:6.1] G2B | Government to Business | MCA portal, GSTN, e-Procurement
  [88:4:6.2] G2G | Between departments/governments | NIC solutions, SWAN, e-Office
  [88:4:6.3] G2E | Government to Employees | HR and administrative tools
[88:4:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 p.18-19; app's current notes 2:88 sub 0-2
## SUB 5 | NeGP, e-Kranti and Digital India
[88:5:0] # NeGP (2006)
[88:5:1] - Formulated by **DeitY and DARPG**; approved **18 May 2006** with **27 Mission Mode Projects** and 10 components.
[88:5:2] - **2011**: 4 MMPs added – **Health, Education, PDS, Posts** → **31**.
[88:5:3] - Core infrastructure: **SWAN**, **State Data Centres**, **CSCs** (UMANG is not core NeGP infrastructure).
[88:5:4] - MMPs: **Central, State, Integrated**.
[88:5:5] # e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)
[88:5:6] - Approved by the Union Cabinet **25 March 2015**; a **pillar of Digital India**; vision **"Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance"**; **44 MMPs** = **15 Central, 17 State, 12 Integrated**.
[88:5:7] # Digital India
[88:5:8] - Launched **1 July 2015**; ministry **MeitY**; **nine pillars**: Broadband Highways; Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity; Public Internet Access Programme; e-Governance; **e-Kranti**; Information for All; Electronics Manufacturing; IT for Jobs; Early Harvest Programmes (a satellite launch programme is not a pillar).
[88:5:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen S&T Group 2 Part 3 (src/science-tech/nextgen-st-group2-03.txt) p.18-19 (NeGP 27 MMPs, 18 May 2006, SWAN, CSC); PMF Lens 2026-05-02 p.5 (NeGP 2006, DARPG); app's current notes 2:88 sub 3-4
## SUB 6 | Information Technology Act, 2000 – E-governance Sections
[88:6:0] TABLE head: Section | Provision
  [88:6:0.0] 4 | Legal recognition of electronic records
  [88:6:0.1] 5 | Legal recognition of digital (electronic) signatures
  [88:6:0.2] 6 | Use of electronic records and signatures in Government – online filing, licences, payments
  [88:6:0.3] 7 | Retention of electronic records
  [88:6:0.4] 9 | Sections 6-8 give no right to insist that a document be accepted in electronic form

=== NOTES 2:89 | Citizen-centric Administration – Citizens' Charter, Sevottam, Grievance Redress (cpgrams), Social Audit
## SUB 0 | Social Audit – MGNREGA and AP's SSAAT
[89:0:0] - **MGNREGA 2005, Section 17**: the **Gram Sabha** conducts the **social audit** of all works – the process used to **enhance accountability** in MGNREGA (not financial, political or legal audit).
[89:0:1] - **AP SSAAT** (**Society for Social Audit, Accountability and Transparency**): set up **2009** as an independent society; looks after social audit of Panchayat Raj / rural development programmes in AP (not SERP, Streenidhi or DWACRA).
[89:0:2] - **CAG** found that the Social Audit Unit **lacks functional independence**.
[89:0:3] - **Village Social Auditors**: short training of about **two days** at the mandal level before the audit.
[89:0:4] - **AP pioneered State-wide MGNREGA social audits**; **Meghalaya (2017)** passed the first law making social audit of government programmes mandatory.
[89:0:5] - **Second ARC (12th Report)**: social audits to be **institutionalised in all major welfare schemes**.
[89:0:6] > Angles: MGNREGA accountability process (×2), who conducts it (Gram Sabha), SSAAT, CAG finding, training days.
[89:0:7] ~~ Sources: app's current notes 2:89 sub 7; MGNREGA s.17 (app's current notes)
## SUB 1 | Andhra Pradesh Grievance Platforms
[89:1:0] TABLE head: Platform | Period | Purpose
  [89:1:0.0] Prajavani | Nov 2005 (Ranga Reddy) | Web-based online receipt, reply and monitoring of grievances at District Collectorates (with NIC)
  [89:1:0.1] Meekosam ("For You") | 2015 (TDP govt) | Single-window portal to lodge grievances/suggestions and track status
  [89:1:0.2] Spandana | 2019 (YSRCP govt) | One-stop public grievance redressal platform for the citizens of AP
  [89:1:0.3] PGRS | After Spandana | AI-based Public Grievance Redressal System
[89:1:1] - "Web-based grievance system at Collectorates" = **Prajavani**; "one-stop grievance platform for AP citizens" = **Spandana**; **CPGRAMS** is the Union platform, not AP's.
[89:1:2] ~~ Sources: app's current notes 2:89 sub 6 and 2:88 sub 7
## SUB 2 | Citizens' Charter and Ombudsman
[89:2:0] # Citizens' Charter
[89:2:1] - A **written commitment** on service standards; main purpose = **time-bound service delivery and grievance redress**.
[89:2:2] - Origin **UK, 1991** (John Major); India adopted **1997**; **DARPG** coordinates; charters are **non-justiciable**.
[89:2:3] - **Six principles**: quality, choice, standards, value, accountability, transparency (**participation is not** one).
[89:2:4] - **Basic elements (India)**: vision and mission; services provided and their standards; information on how to obtain them; **grievance redress**; **expectations from citizens** – **inspection of the agency's work is NOT** an element.
[89:2:5] - **Citizens Charter Bill, 2011** lapsed with the Lok Sabha in **2014**; **Second ARC** wanted statutory backing.
[89:2:6] # Ombudsman
[89:2:7] - Ombudsman = **Sweden, 1809**; banks, insurance and tax departments use an **Ombudsman** as the alternate grievance redress system for complaints (Banking/Insurance/Tax Ombudsman).
[89:2:8] - Classic ombudsman = **maladministration**; Lokpal/Lokayukta = **corruption** (Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act **2013**); terms coined by **L.M. Singhvi**; first Lokayukta **Maharashtra 1971**.
[89:2:9] - **First ARC** (1966-70, **Morarji Desai**): recommended a **Lokpal at the Union** and **Lokayuktas in the States**.
[89:2:10] ~~ Sources: app's current notes 2:89 sub 0-1, 8
## SUB 3 | Right to Services Acts
[89:3:0] - Idea grew out of the **Citizens' Charter** in **Great Britain**.
[89:3:1] - First law: **Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewa Guarantee Act, 2010**; **Bihar** 2011; among Punjab, Assam, Gujarat, Maharashtra the earliest is **Punjab**.
[89:3:2] - Features: notified services in a **fixed time**, appeals, **penalties**; they do **not** abolish other grievance mechanisms.
[89:3:3] - **AP Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017** – in force **18 Oct 2017**.
[89:3:4] - **Project Saksham** (railways) = time-bound skill upgradation of railway employees (a CA item, not a Right to Services law).
[89:3:5] ~~ Sources: app's current notes 2:89 sub 4
## SUB 4 | Sevottam, CPGRAMS and the Second ARC 12th Report
[89:4:0] # Sevottam
[89:4:1] - **Seva + Uttam**; suggested in the **Second ARC's 12th Report**; promoted by **DARPG** (framework for improving service delivery); from **2009**.
[89:4:2] - **Three modules**: Citizens' Charter; Public Grievance Redress; Service Delivery Capability; certification **IS 15700:2005**.
[89:4:3] # CPGRAMS
[89:4:4] - **Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System**; launched **2007** by **DARPG** (Ministry of **Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**, not Home Affairs); 24×7 via web, app and **UMANG**.
[89:4:5] - DARPG circular **23 Aug 2024**: maximum disposal time **30 → 21 days**; **GRAI**: 11 indicators, 4 dimensions (efficiency, feedback, domain, organisational commitment); pensioners: **CPENGRAMS**.
[89:4:6] # Second ARC 12th Report (2009)
[89:4:7] - **"Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance"**; Second ARC (2005), chairman **Veerappa Moily**; recommended Sevottam, statutory charters, social audits, right to public services laws.
[89:4:8] - **Punchhi Commission (2010)** volume on good governance argued for treating good governance / corruption-free delivery of services as a **right** of citizens.
[89:4:9] ~~ Sources: PMF Lens 2026-05-02 p.5 (CPGRAMS 2007, DARPG under Ministry of Personnel, Sevottam); app's current notes 2:89 sub 2-3, 5

=== NOTES 2:90 | Right to Information Act 2005 – Structure, Exemptions, Amendments and Issues
## SUB 0 | Background, Chronology and Enactment
[90:0:0] # Chronology
[90:0:1] TABLE head: Year | Landmark
  [90:0:1.0] 1766 | Sweden – Freedom of the Press Act: world's first RTI law
  [90:0:1.1] 1948 | UN – UDHR Article 19: right to seek and receive information
  [90:0:1.2] 1990 | MKSS (Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan), Rajasthan – Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey, Shankar Singh; jan sunwais on muster rolls started the RTI movement
  [90:0:1.3] 1997 | Tamil Nadu: first Indian State RTI law (Goa the same year)
  [90:0:1.4] 2002 | Freedom of Information Act 2002 – never notified; repealed by the RTI Act 2005
  [90:0:1.5] 2005 | Right to Information Act, 2005
[90:0:2] - Order: **Sweden → UN → FOI Act → RTI Act**.
[90:0:3] # Enactment
[90:0:4] TABLE head: Step | Date
  [90:0:4.0] Lok Sabha passed | 11 May 2005
  [90:0:4.1] Rajya Sabha passed | 12 May 2005
  [90:0:4.2] Presidential assent (A.P.J. Abdul Kalam) | 15 June 2005
  [90:0:4.3] Fully in force | 12 October 2005 (120 days after assent)
[90:0:5] - **CIC** constituted **12 October 2005** under the RTI Act (first CIC **Wajahat Habibullah**).
[90:0:6] - "Passed in 2005" / "enacted 2005" – the Act is dated **15 June 2005**; Parliament itself passed it on 11-12 May 2005.
[90:0:7] > Angles: year of Act (×3), assent, in force, FOI Act 2002 (×2), TN 1997 (×2), MKSS (×2), chronology.
[90:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Polity Part 1 (src/polity/rocket-polity-01.txt) p.54 (assent 15 June 2005, in force 12 Oct 2005, MKSS); Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.62 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.252); app's current notes 2:90 sub 0-1
## SUB 1 | Preamble, Objectives and Nature of the Right
[90:1:0] - Preamble terms: **transparency of information**, **revelation of information**, **informed citizenry**, **paramountcy of the democratic ideal** (all four).
[90:1:1] - Objectives: transparency and accountability, **answerability**, **containing corruption**, empowering citizens, making democracy work for the people – **NOT** "empowering women and weaker sections".
[90:1:2] - RTI **mandates a timely response** to citizens' requests for government information (not NeGP, Aadhaar or RTE).
[90:1:3] - Nature: a **statutory (legal) right** under the 2005 Act; the **right to know** is also read into **Article 19(1)(a)** (State of U.P. v. Raj Narain, 1975) – hence "both" a legal and a fundamental right in most keys.
[90:1:4] - **Namit Sharma v. Union of India (2012)** – RTI case on Information Commissions.
[90:1:5] - Impact: raised the **sense of responsibility in bureaucracy**, but "miles to go" (both true, R does not explain A); the Act is **misused by both** applicants and public authorities.
[90:1:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Rocket Polity Part 1 p.54 (legal right; Namit Sharma 2012); app's current notes 2:90 sub 1, 11
## SUB 2 | Key Sections – Who May Ask, What Is Covered
[90:2:0] TABLE head: Section | Subject
  [90:2:0.0] 2(f) | "Information": records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, samples, models, electronic data
  [90:2:0.1] 2(h) | "Public authority": bodies under the Constitution, a law or notification; bodies and NGOs substantially financed by government
  [90:2:0.2] 2(j) | Right to: inspection of work, documents, records; notes, extracts, certified copies; certified samples; information in diskettes, floppies, tapes, video cassettes or electronic form – not taking files out of the office
  [90:2:0.3] 3 | All citizens have the right (not "any person" or companies)
  [90:2:0.4] 4 | Proactive (suo motu) disclosure; 4(1)(b) must publish organisation, functions, procedure followed in decision-making, norms, budgets, PIOs
  [90:2:0.5] 5 | PIOs / APIOs designated by each public authority
  [90:2:0.6] 6 | Request in English, Hindi or the official language of the area; 6(2) no reason need be given
  [90:2:0.7] 7 | Disposal – 30 days / 48 hours; 7(5) no fee for BPL applicants
  [90:2:0.8] 11 | Third-party information
  [90:2:0.9] 12 / 15 | Constitute CIC / SIC
  [90:2:0.10] 18 | Complaints and inquiry by the Commission
  [90:2:0.11] 19 | Appeals; 19(8)(b) compensation
  [90:2:0.12] 20 | Penalties on PIOs
  [90:2:0.13] 22 | Overrides the Official Secrets Act, 1923
  [90:2:0.14] 24 | Second Schedule intelligence/security bodies excluded – except corruption and human-rights information (CBI added 2011)
  [90:2:0.15] 25 | Annual report, laid before Parliament/Legislature
[90:2:1] - "Obtaining security information" is **not** part of the right to information.
[90:2:2] ~~ Sources: RTI Act 2005 – important sections (mkc.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/RTI-Act-2005.pdf), s.2(f), 2(h), 2(j), 3, 4, 6, 7, 24, 25; app's current notes 2:90 sub 2
[90:2:3] - The **Central Information Commission** is **not** a Second Schedule (Section 24) body – it is the appellate authority under the Act.
## SUB 3 | Time Limits
[90:3:0] TABLE head: Stage | Limit
  [90:3:0.0] Normal reply by PIO (Sec. 7(1)) | 30 days
  [90:3:0.1] Life or liberty | 48 hours
  [90:3:0.2] Through APIO | 35 days (30 + 5)
  [90:3:0.3] Third-party (Sec. 11) | 40 days
  [90:3:0.4] Human-rights allegations vs Section 24 bodies | 45 days (with Commission approval)
  [90:3:0.5] First appeal | Filed within 30 days; decided in 30 days, extendable to 45 with reasons recorded (Sec. 19(6))
  [90:3:0.6] Second appeal to CIC/SIC | Within 90 days
[90:3:1] - "Normal reply in 45 days" and "second appeal in 180 days" are the standard wrong pairs.
[90:3:2] ~~ Sources: RTI Act 2005 – important sections (mkc.ac.in PDF), s.5(2), 7(1), 11(3), 19(1), 19(3), 19(6), 24(1)
## SUB 4 | Exemptions – Sections 8, 9 and 24
[90:4:0] TABLE head: Clause 8(1) | Exempt information
  [90:4:0.0] (a) | Sovereignty, security, foreign relations, incitement of an offence
  [90:4:0.1] (b) | Forbidden by a court / contempt of court
  [90:4:0.2] (c) | Breach of privilege of Parliament or State Legislature
  [90:4:0.3] (d) | Commercial confidence, trade secrets, intellectual property – unless larger public interest warrants disclosure (conditional)
  [90:4:0.4] (e) | Fiduciary relationship
  [90:4:0.5] (f) | Information received in confidence from a foreign Government
  [90:4:0.6] (i) | Cabinet papers incl. deliberations of the Council of Ministers (decisions made public once complete)
  [90:4:0.7] (j) | Personal information (rewritten as a blanket exemption by DPDP Act 2023, s.44(3))
[90:4:1] - **Procedure followed in decision-making** is **not exempt** – Section 4(1)(b) requires its publication.
[90:4:2] - **8(2)** public-interest override; **8(3)** most exemptions lapse after **20 years**; **Section 9**: copyright of a person other than the State.
[90:4:3] - Information that cannot be denied to Parliament cannot be denied to any person.
[90:4:4] - **Second ARC**: maximum information in the public domain; read Section 8 **narrowly**; link RTI with **whistle-blower protection**.
[90:4:5] ~~ Sources: RTI Act 2005 – important sections (mkc.ac.in PDF), s.8(1), 9; app's current notes 2:90 sub 4, 7
## SUB 5 | Information Commissions and Penalties
[90:5:0] TABLE head: Item | CIC | SIC
  [90:5:0.0] Composition | Chief IC + up to 10 ICs | State Chief IC + up to 10 SICs
  [90:5:0.1] Appointed by | President | Governor
  [90:5:0.2] Committee | PM (chair), LoP in Lok Sabha, Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM | CM (chair), LoP in the Assembly, State Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM
  [90:5:0.3] Removal for misbehaviour | President, after Supreme Court inquiry | Governor, after Supreme Court inquiry
[90:5:1] - **No Chief Justice** (CJI or High Court CJ) on either committee.
[90:5:2] - Eligibility: eminence in law, S&T, social service, management, **journalism**, mass media, administration; **cannot be an MP or a member of any State Legislature**, hold office of profit or be linked to a party.
[90:5:3] - Statutory bodies with **civil-court powers**; term now **prescribed by the Centre (3 years)** or 65 (RTI Amendment Act 2019; earlier 5 years).
[90:5:4] - **Section 20 penalty**: imposed by the **CIC or SIC** (not courts) – **₹250 per day, max ₹25,000**; burden of proof on the PIO; Commission can also recommend disciplinary action.
[90:5:5] - **AP SIC**: **Vajji (Vajja) Srinivasa Rao** appointed Chief Information Commissioner (Jan 2026) with four ICs; 2026 inspection of 258 offices found Section 4(1)(b) violations.
[90:5:6] - Before 2019: CIC's salary = **Chief Election Commissioner**, IC = Election Commissioner; State CIC = Election Commissioner, State IC = **Chief Secretary**; term was **5 years or 65**.
[90:5:7] - Contrast **CVC**: CVC + up to 2 Vigilance Commissioners; **4 years or 65**.
[90:5:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.62-63 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-02.txt p.252-257); RTI Act 2005 – important sections (mkc.ac.in PDF) s.20; Praveen CA360 Jan 2026 magazine (src/current-affairs/praveen-ca360-2026-01-magazine.txt, AP SIC appointments)
[90:5:9] - **Removal grounds** (CIC/SIC): insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude, paid outside employment, infirmity of mind or body, prejudicial financial interest, and proved misbehaviour/incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry – **not** disagreement with the Government.
## SUB 6 | Public Authority, Judgements and Issues
[90:6:0] TABLE head: Case / order | Held
  [90:6:0.0] CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019) | Office of the CJI is a public authority (Constitution Bench)
  [90:6:0.1] CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011) | Evaluated answer sheets = information
  [90:6:0.2] Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v CIC (2012) | Service records, assets, tax returns = personal information, 8(1)(j)
  [90:6:0.3] DAV College Trust (2019) | NGOs substantially financed by government are public authorities
  [90:6:0.4] CIC, June 2013 | Six national parties (INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP, BSP) declared public authorities – not complied with
  [90:6:0.5] Zee Telefilms (2005) / CIC 2026 | BCCI not "State"; not a public authority
[90:6:1] - Issues: **pendency** (over 4 lakh appeals, Jul 2026), **vacancies**, 2019 amendment weakening autonomy, DPDP 8(1)(j) change (Constitution Bench, 2026), attacks on activists; **Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014** not operationalised.
[90:6:2] - RTI Online portal (DoPT, 2013); AP HC (Nov 2023) directed an online RTI portal; SIC website sic.ap.gov.in (8 Sep 2025).
[90:6:3] - Political parties: inclusion meant to check **corruption, crony capitalism** and illegal **foreign contributions**; the RTI (Amendment) Bill 2013 to exclude them **lapsed**.
[90:6:4] - MPLADS works are covered and tracked on **eSAKSHI**; Madras HC's 2014 remark that applicants state reasons was **withdrawn** (Sec. 6(2)).
[90:6:5] - DPDP change: notified Nov 2025 → Constitution Bench reference **Feb 2026** → SC to examine the "en bloc embargo" (7 Aug 2026).
[90:6:6] - **Economic Survey 2025-26**: re-examine RTI – exempt **confidential service records and draft policy discussions**; **Satark Nagrik Sangathan** 2025 report card found gaps; **more than 100** RTI activists killed (Jul 2026); AP secretariat publishes ATRs on seven sector white papers (22 June 2026).
[90:6:7] ~~ Sources: app's current notes 2:90 sub 8-11

=== NOTES 2:92 | Accountability and Transparency Mechanisms – Whistle Blowers Protection Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, Citizens' Oversight
## SUB 0 | Money Laundering, Benami Property and Offshore Leaks
[92:0:0] # PMLA 2002
[92:0:1] - **Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002**: India's principal anti-money-laundering law; **in force 1 July 2005** (with its Rules).
[92:0:2] - **Section 3:** money laundering = concealing, possessing, acquiring, using, projecting or claiming **"proceeds of crime"** as untainted property; punishment **3 to 7 years** RI (up to 10 in some cases) + fine.
[92:0:3] - **Director of the Enforcement Directorate** can **attach property** believed to be proceeds of crime (APPSC Group 1).
[92:0:4] - Machinery: **Adjudicating Authority**, **Appellate Tribunal** and **Special Courts** for the trial of money-laundering offences.
[92:0:5] - **Schedule:** **Part A** = listed offences (IPC/BNS, NDPS, etc.) with no money limit; Part B = Customs false declaration; **Part C = offences with cross-border implications** (so "Part A = trans-border crimes" is **wrong**).
[92:0:6] - **"Proceeds of crime" definition (Sec 2(1)(u)) amended by the Finance Act, 2015** (w.e.f. 14 May 2015): added property taken or held **outside the country** → equivalent value within India (APPSC AEE 2016); widened again in **2018** and **2019** (Explanation).
[92:0:7] - **Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022):** SC upheld the main PMLA provisions; ED works under the **Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance** (ED set up 1956).
[92:0:8] # Benami and fugitive offenders
[92:0:9] TABLE head: Law | Key point
  [92:0:9.0] Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 | Sec 3(2): up to 3 years' imprisonment, or fine, or both for entering into a benami transaction
  [92:0:9.1] Benami (Amendment) Act, 2016 | Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act; bans proxy holdings; confiscation + RI 1 to 7 years (not ten)
  [92:0:9.2] Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 | Warrant + offence of ₹100 crore or more + flight from India; Special Court (on ED application) may confiscate even before conviction; e.g. Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi
[92:0:10] - **Ganpati Dealcom (23 Aug 2022):** SC held **Sec 3(2)** (3-year punishment) **unconstitutional** and the 2016 Act **prospective** (APSLPRB SI 2023). **⚠ Recalled in Oct 2024** when the SC allowed the Union's review petition.
[92:0:11] # Offshore leaks
[92:0:12] - **Paradise Papers (5 Nov 2017, ICIJ):** leaked records mainly of offshore law firm **Appleby**; **714 Indians** named. (Panama Papers = the earlier 2016 leak.)
[92:0:13] ~~ Sources: PMF Internal Security & DM Part 1 p.78-79 (PMLA, Benami, FEOA, ED); bcajonline.org (Finance Act 2015, proceeds of crime); verdictum.in (Ganpati Dealcom, 23 Aug 2022); taxmann.com (recall, Oct 2024); indiankanoon.org (Benami 1988 Sec 3 text quoted in Rajasthan HC 1997); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise_Papers; app notes 2:92 sub 6
## SUB 1 | UN Conventions against Corruption and Organised Crime
[92:1:0] TABLE head: Feature | UNCAC | UNTOC (Palermo)
  [92:1:0.0] Adopted | 2003 (Merida) | 2000
  [92:1:0.1] Signature | only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument | Organised crime, money laundering, extradition
  [92:1:0.2] Special chapter | Chapter V – asset recovery (return of assets to rightful owners) | —
  [92:1:0.3] Protocols | none | 3 Protocols – trafficking in persons, smuggling of migrants by land, sea and air, firearms
  [92:1:0.4] India | signed 2005, ratified 2011 | party, with its three Protocols
[92:1:1] - **UNODC** (Vienna) is mandated to assist States in implementing **both UNCAC and UNTOC** (secretariat).
[92:1:2] > UPSC 2019 statements: smuggling-of-migrants protocol belongs to UNTOC (✗ for UNCAC); asset-recovery chapter is UNCAC's (✗ for UNTOC) → **B and D only**.
[92:1:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Internal Security & DM Part 1 p.71, p.78; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Convention_against_Corruption; app notes 2:92 sub 0
## SUB 2 | Corruption Perceptions Index
[92:2:0] - **Transparency International (Berlin)**, yearly since **1995**; measures **perceived public-sector corruption** (APPSC 2017) from expert and business surveys.
[92:2:1] - Scale **0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean)**.
[92:2:2] TABLE head: Edition | India's rank | Score
  [92:2:2.0] CPI 2016 (Jan 2017) | 79th of 176 (2015: 76th) | 40
  [92:2:2.1] CPI 2024 | 96th | 38
  [92:2:2.2] CPI 2025 (10 Feb 2026) | 91st of 182 | 39

[92:2:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket Current Affairs 2026 Part 1 p.26 (CPI 2025); businesstoday.in (CPI 2016, 27 Jan 2017); app notes 2:92 sub 7
## SUB 3 | Prevention of Corruption Act and Sanction for Prosecution
[92:3:0] - **PCA 1988**: consolidated anti-bribery law after the **Santhanam Committee**'s push.
[92:3:1] - **Public servant (Sec 2(c))**: any government or **local-authority** employee, any **Judge**, anyone whose office requires a **public duty** – not only permanent Union employees.
[92:3:2] # PC (Amendment) Act 2018
[92:3:3] TABLE head: Change | Detail
  [92:3:3.0] Purpose | Align with UNCAC

## SUB 4 | Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014
[92:4:0] - **Whistle-blower**: **any public servant or other person, including an NGO**, making a **public interest disclosure** on corruption, wilful misuse of power or a criminal offence to the **Competent Authority** (CVC by default).
[92:4:1] TABLE head: Complained against | Competent authority
  [92:4:1.0] Central employees | CVC
  [92:4:1.1] State employees | State Vigilance Commission
  [92:4:1.2] Union Minister | Prime Minister
  [92:4:1.3] State Minister | Chief Minister
  [92:4:1.4] MPs | Rajya Sabha Chairman / Lok Sabha Speaker
  [92:4:1.5] MLAs | Presiding officer of the House
[92:4:2] - **Identity** kept **confidential**; protection against **victimisation**; **no anonymous** complaints; complaint within **7 years**.
[92:4:3] - Penalties: revealing identity = up to **3 years + ₹50,000**; knowingly false complaint = up to **2 years + ₹30,000**.
[92:4:4] - **SPG** excluded. Bill passed the Lok Sabha in 2011; **Act of 2014**, still **not brought into force** (CVC uses the 2004 PIDPI resolution).
[92:4:5] - **Amendment Bill 2015** (Lok Sabha, May 2015) would bar disclosures in **RTI Sec 8(1)-type** categories; **lapsed in 2019** with the 16th Lok Sabha.

## SUB 6 | Lokpal and Lokayuktas
[92:6:0] - **Lokpal (2013 Act)**: **Chairperson + up to 8 members**; **50% judicial**; at least 50% from **SC, ST, OBC, minorities, women**.
[92:6:1] - **Selection committee**: **PM** (chair), **Speaker**, **LoP**, **CJI** or nominated SC judge, an **eminent jurist** (not the Cabinet Secretary).
[92:6:2] - **First Lokpal**: **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose** (March 2019); **Justice A.M. Khanwilkar** chairperson from **Feb 2024**.
[92:6:3] - The Act obliged every State to set up a **Lokayukta within one year**.
[92:6:4] - **AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983**; Lokayukta = **higher functionaries**, Upa-Lokayukta = the rest; **2024 amendment**: retired HC CJ or Judge, chosen by a committee **chaired by the CM**, term **5 years**.
[92:6:5] - **Aug 2026**: **Justice Tallapragada Mallikarjuna Rao** selected and sworn in (25 Aug) as AP Lokayukta; oath by Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer**.

  x: At least 50% of Lokpal members must be from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women; 50% must be judicial.

=== NOTES 2:93 | Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation – the 1991 Reforms
## SUB 0 | Capital Account Convertibility and Reform-era Committees
[93:0:0] # Reform committees – who looked at what
[93:0:1] TABLE head: Committee | Year | Subject
  [93:0:1.0] S.S. Tarapore (I), set up by RBI | 1997 | Roadmap to capital account convertibility (CAC)
  [93:0:1.1] S.S. Tarapore (II), RBI | 2006 (report Sept 2006) | Fuller capital account convertibility (FCAC)
  [93:0:1.2] C. Rangarajan | 1993 | Disinvestment of PSUs – up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector
  [93:0:1.3] Raja J. Chelliah ("father of Indian tax reforms") | 1991 | Tax reforms – MODVAT towards a full VAT
  [93:0:1.4] M. Narasimham (I 1991; II 1998) | 1991, 1998 | Financial sector / banking reforms
  [93:0:1.5] R.N. Malhotra | 1993 | Insurance sector reforms
  [93:0:1.6] Vijay Kelkar | 2002 task forces; 2015 | Direct and indirect taxes; PPP model
  [93:0:1.7] C. Rangarajan (High Level Committee on BoP) | 1993 | Market-determined exchange rate
[93:0:2] - **Distractors:** Kelkar = tax / PPP, not disinvestment; Gadgil = planning formula; Usha Thorat and S.A. Dara are not the CAC committees.
[93:0:3] # Capital account convertibility
[93:0:4] - **Meaning:** freedom to convert rupees into any major currency (and back) for **trading financial assets** – investment, loans, portfolio flows (UPSC 1998). Conversion for trade in goods and services = **current account** convertibility.
[93:0:5] - **Current account:** fully convertible since **August 1994** (IMF Article VIII obligation).
[93:0:6] - **Capital account:** never fully convertible; India allows **partial** CAC with limits (e.g. individuals up to **$2,50,000 a year** under LRS).
[93:0:7] - **Tarapore I (1997) preconditions:** fiscal consolidation – Centre's gross fiscal deficit cut from **4.5% to 3.5% of GDP** over three years (by 1999-2000); a mandated inflation target; a strong financial system; a phased move over three years from 1997-98.
[93:0:8] - **Capital account convertibility was not part of the 1991 LPG package.**
[93:0:9] > Recall angle: "Tarapore" → capital account convertibility (asked as "framework for full CAC", "fuller CAC" and "3.5% fiscal deficit precondition").
[93:0:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC Exams Part 3.2 p.10 (Tarapore); NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 4 p.21 (Rangarajan BoP 1993), p.27 (Chelliah), p.29 (Rangarajan disinvestment 49%); Rocket Indian Economy p.95 (Sheet #66 committees); Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (file 05) p.170-171, §15.8-15.9 (CAC, Tarapore 1997/2006); chronicleindia.in Tarapore committee page (4.5% → 3.5% fiscal deficit)
## SUB 1 | The 1991 Crisis and the New Economic Policy
[93:1:0] - **Trigger:** **flight of NRI deposits**; forex reserves fell to about **$975 million (June 1991)** = about **two weeks of imports**.
[93:1:1] - **Gold:** **67 tonnes** pledged with the **Bank of England and UBS**.
[93:1:2] - **IMF:** approached for about **$7 billion**, with **structural-adjustment conditions**.
[93:1:3] - **Other 1991 numbers:** fiscal deficit about **9.4%** of GDP, inflation about **12%**, GDP growth only about **1.3%**.
[93:1:4] - **NEP (LPG) announced:** the New Industrial Policy on **24 July 1991** – so economic reforms were formally introduced in **July 1991**.
[93:1:5] - **Leaders:** PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao**, FM **Dr. Manmohan Singh** (UPPSC 2013); the earlier Janata (1977), Indira (1980) and Rajiv (1985) governments did not launch it.
[93:1:6] - **Components:** **Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation**, with **disinvestment** as the main form of privatisation; **nationalisation** is the opposite of the NEP (APPSC 2018).
[93:1:7] # Stabilisation vs structural adjustment
[93:1:8] TABLE head: Aspect | Stabilisation | Structural adjustment
  [93:1:8.0] Time frame | Short-term, demand side | Medium/long-term, supply side
  [93:1:8.1] Aim | BoP, inflation, fiscal deficit | Efficiency, competitiveness
  [93:1:8.2] Measures | Devaluation, deficit cuts | Delicensing, trade, financial, tax, PSU reforms
[93:1:9] > Trap: devaluation = stabilisation; delicensing = structural adjustment.
[93:1:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 4 p.25 (24 July 1991), p.29 (1991 numbers); Rocket Indian Economy p.58 (NEP, stabilisation vs structural adjustment); NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC Part 8.2 p.6-9; app notes 2:93 (sub 0)
## SUB 2 | 1991 Measures – Delicensing, De-reservation, FDI and the Rupee
[93:2:0] TABLE head: Measure | Part of 1991 LPG?
  [93:2:0.0] Industrial de-licensing | Yes – licensing first kept for 18 industries, now only 5 (alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronic aerospace and defence; drugs since delicensed)
  [93:2:0.1] Public-sector reservation | Cut 17 → 8 → 3 (atomic energy, railways, specified minerals); now only atomic energy and railway operations
  [93:2:0.2] FDI automatic route | Yes – up to 51% in 34 priority industries; later up to 100% in hotels, infrastructure, software
  [93:2:0.3] PSU autonomy | MoUs; Navratnas (1997)
  [93:2:0.4] Current account convertibility | Yes, 1994
  [93:2:0.5] Capital account convertibility | No; never fully adopted (Tarapore)
  [93:2:0.6] FERA → FEMA | 1999, not 1991
  [93:2:0.7] Foreign Investment Promotion Board | Set up to promote FDI
[93:2:1] - **Defence opened to the private sector:** **May 2001** (Press Note 4 of 2001, 21 May 2001) – Indian private firms allowed to make **arms and ammunition** (100% Indian private, FDI up to 26%), under licence (APPSC G2 Mains).
[93:2:2] - **Rupee:** devalued about **18-20% on 1 and 3 July 1991**; LERMS dual rate 1992, unified **market-determined** rate from **March 1993** – today the rupee's rate is **market determined** (managed float), not pegged to the dollar, the euro or a basket.
[93:2:3] - **Financial sector:** RBI's role moved from **regulator to facilitator**; private Indian and foreign banks allowed.
[93:2:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC Part 8.2 p.6-10 (reserved sectors, licensing, FDI, MRTP, 17 → 8 → 3); Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (file 05) p.171 (LERMS March 1993, devaluation); Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (file 05) p.15, §9.15 (strategic PSEs: arms and ammunition); web: DPIIT Press Note 4 (2001) as summarised in search results (taxtmi.com, idsa.in)
## SUB 3 | LPG Terms
[93:3:0] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [93:3:0.0] Liberalisation | Removing controls: licences, quotas, entry curbs; freedom to fix prices, expand, import
  [93:3:0.1] Privatisation | Government leaves ownership/management – withdrawal or outright sale of PSUs; narrow sense = private ownership in a PSU, broad sense = bigger role for the private sector
  [93:3:0.2] Disinvestment | Sale of part of PSU equity to the public; above 51% private stake transfers control
  [93:3:0.3] Globalisation | Joining the world economy; the outcome (not precondition) of L and P
[93:3:1] - **Navratnas:** nine PSUs given greater autonomy in **1997** (NextGen NCERT summary says 1996 – the scheme was launched July 1997); **Miniratnas: 97**; Maharatna from 2010.
[93:3:2] - **New PSE Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat (2021):** favours **strategic disinvestment**.
[93:3:3] - **Private sector** = engine of growth after 1991 (before: size of the public sector measured "socialisation").
[93:3:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 3 p.41 (privatisation, disinvestment, globalisation as outcome, Navratna, 97 Miniratnas); NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC Part 8.2 p.10; Rocket Indian Economy p.94 (Navratna 1997, Maharatna 2010)
## SUB 4 | Industrial Policies, Licence Raj and MRTP
[93:4:0] TABLE head: Year | Thrust
  [93:4:0.0] 1948 IPR | Mixed economy; four categories (6 April 1948, S.P. Mukherjee)
  [93:4:0.1] 1956 IPR | Schedule A (17 public), B (12 mixed), C (private); "economic constitution of India"
  [93:4:0.2] 1977 IPS (Janata) | Small/cottage industries; District Industries Centres
  [93:4:0.3] 1980 IPS | Technology upgrading, export orientation, backward areas; MRTP firms 25% expansion
  [93:4:0.4] 1991 IPS | De-licensing, MRTP restructured, FDI, PSU autonomy via MoUs; did not expand licensing
[93:4:1] - **MRTP Act 1969** (Dutt Committee recommended it); relaxed 1980; in 1991 asset limits and pre-entry curbs on expansion, mergers and acquisitions **abolished**.
[93:4:2] - Replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002 (CCI)**.
[93:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 4 p.25 (1948, 1956), p.29 (Dutt Committee, Competition Act); NextGen Indian Economy - APPSC Part 8.2 p.6, p.9 (MRTP 1991); app notes 2:93 (sub 3-4)
## SUB 5 | Trade Reforms, Sequencing and the Washington Consensus
[93:5:0] - Import licensing abolished except hazardous/environmentally sensitive items; peak customs duty cut from about **130% to 30%**.
[93:5:1] TABLE head: Generation | Content
  [93:5:1.0] First (1991-2000) | Trade and industrial delicensing; tariffs ~125% → ~30%; FDI; financial reform
  [93:5:1.1] Second (2000s) | Factor markets (labour, land, power), fiscal rules, disinvestment, governance
[93:5:2] - **Washington Consensus:** **John Williamson, 1989**; 10 prescriptions (fiscal discipline, tax reform, trade and FDI liberalisation, privatisation, deregulation, property rights).
[93:5:3] - **Foreign Trade Policy 2023:** announced 31 March 2023, in force from **1 April 2023**; unlike the earlier five-year EXIM/trade policies it has **no end date** and is updated when needed; target **$2 trillion** exports by 2030.
[93:5:4] > Trap: factor-market reforms are **second-generation**; globalisation is the outcome, not the first step.
[93:5:5] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh Indian Economy (file 05) p.171-172, §15.9-15.10 (IMF conditions: customs 130% → 30%); app notes 2:93 (sub 6)

=== NOTES 2:95 | Impact of Lpg on Administration – Downsizing, Contractualisation, Npm
## SUB 0 | Contractualisation and Outsourcing
[95:0:0] - **Outsourcing:** hiring outside sources (legal, IT, advertising, security) for regular work once done in-house; an outcome of globalisation, spread by IT – the method that "became popular in the recent past" for staffing jobs in both public and private sectors (APPSC G1).
[95:0:1]   - Distractors: contract appointments (a form of it, narrower), emergency recruitment, on-line recruitment (a channel, not a method of employing).
[95:0:2] - **Contract labour:** **20% (1999) → 40.7%** of manufacturing workforce (2022-23, ASI); such firms **31% lower productivity** (Aug 2025).
[95:0:3] - Weaker direct employer relation → weaker unions; **Industrial Relations Code 2020**: 10% or 100 workers to form a union.
[95:0:4] # AP angle
[95:0:5] - **APCOS** (2020): recruits outsourced staff and **pays directly**, cutting contractor middlemen.
[95:0:6] - **APSRTC:** about 8,000 outsourced staff paid via contractors; wage, PF, ESI irregularities (28 Jul 2026).
[95:0:7] - **Civil Services Board:** curbs political interference in postings.
[95:0:8] - Upper age limit for non-uniform direct recruitment raised **42 → 44** till 30 Sep 2027 (G.O. Ms. No. 187).
[95:0:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 3 p.41 (outsourcing); app notes 2:95 (sub 4)
## SUB 1 | Downsizing the State and Pay Commissions
[95:1:0] - **Downsizing, disinvestment, privatisation** shrink the State; **FDI promotion** is a growth/external-sector measure, **not** a cut in State size.
[95:1:1] - Keyed set: downsizing, disinvestment, privatising higher education (UPSC 2010).
[95:1:2] - **Disinvestment:** sale of part of PSU equity to the public; need not transfer ownership or management. **Privatisation:** withdrawal or outright sale.
[95:1:3] - **Economic Survey 2025-26:** redefine "Government Company" so the State may hold **less than 51%**.
[95:1:4] # Pay Commissions and staff strength
[95:1:5] TABLE head: Commission | Chair / year | Key change
  [95:1:5.0] Fifth | Justice S. Ratnavel Pandian, 1997 | Staff cut about 30%; freeze on new posts
  [95:1:5.1] Sixth | Justice B.N. Srikrishna, 2008 | Group D merged into Group C; running pay bands; PRIS
  [95:1:5.2] Seventh | Justice A.K. Mathur, 2015 (effective 2016) | Pay matrix replaced pay bands; performance-linked pay
[95:1:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy Part 1 - APPSC Part 3 p.41 (disinvestment vs privatisation); app notes 2:95 (sub 0)
## SUB 2 | New Public Management
[95:2:0] - Private-sector techniques in government (Phase 4 of Indian public administration after 1991); term popularised by **Christopher Hood (1991)**.
[95:2:1] - **Hood's doctrines:** hands-on professional management, explicit standards and performance measures, **output controls**, competition.
[95:2:2] - **Features:** performance auditing, **contracting out non-core services**, citizen as customer; it does **not** reject performance measures.
[95:2:3] - **Pioneers:** **UK (Thatcher), New Zealand, Australia, USA**.
[95:2:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:95 (sub 1)
## SUB 3 | Reinventing Government (Osborne and Gaebler, 1992)
[95:3:0] - "**Steering, not rowing**." Ten principles:
[95:3:1] TABLE head: Principle | Meaning
  [95:3:1.0] Catalytic | Steer rather than row
  [95:3:1.1] Community-owned | Empower rather than serve
  [95:3:1.2] Competitive | Inject competition
  [95:3:1.3] Mission-driven | Rules → mission
  [95:3:1.4] Results-oriented | Fund outcomes
  [95:3:1.5] Customer-driven | Meet customer needs
  [95:3:1.6] Enterprising | Earn rather than spend
  [95:3:1.7] Anticipatory | Prevent rather than cure
  [95:3:1.8] Decentralised | Hierarchy → participation and teamwork
  [95:3:1.9] Market-oriented | Change through the market
[95:3:2] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:95 (sub 2)
[95:3:3] - **Authors:** David **Osborne** and Ted **Gaebler**, *Reinventing Government* (1992).
## SUB 4 | Critiques of NPM and Citizen as Customer
[95:4:0] TABLE head: Thinker | Work | Idea
  [95:4:0.0] Denhardt & Denhardt | New Public Service (2000) | "Serve, not steer"; citizenship, public interest
  [95:4:0.1] Mark Moore | Creating Public Value (1995) | Value includes legitimacy and trust, not only efficiency
[95:4:1] - Both reject citizen → customer and State → service seller.
[95:4:2] - **Citizen-as-customer instruments:** Citizens' Charters, service standards, grievance redressal.
[95:4:3] - **Criticism:** citizen has **rights, not just purchasing power**; equity and accountability suffer.
[95:4:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:95 (sub 3, 7)
## SUB 5 | Lateral Entry and Performance Management
[95:5:0] - **Normal route:** JS/Director posts by tenure deputation (**Central Staffing Scheme, DoPT**).
[95:5:1] - **Second ARC:** lateral entry at **Joint Secretary** level; performance-based appraisal and promotion; performance incentives.
[95:5:2] - **NITI Aayog Action Agenda:** wider entry at middle/senior levels; longer, stable tenures.
[95:5:3] - First lateral JS joined **2019**; **Aug 2024**: UPSC told to cancel advertisement for **45** posts.
[95:5:4] - **Debate:** domain expertise vs no reservation in single posts, conflict of interest, demotivated career officers.
[95:5:5] # Performance tools
[95:5:6] - **RFD (2009)**, PMES, Cabinet Secretariat: objectives, success indicators, targets = **Key Result Areas**.
[95:5:7] - **Referral Board** reviews adverse ACR remarks; **360-degree** multi-source feedback.
[95:5:8] - **Good Governance Index:** uniform framework for States/UTs. **NeSDA** (2019; 2025 portal June 2026). **GRAI:** **11 indicators, 4 dimensions** on CPGRAMS.
[95:5:9] - India **97th** in UN EGDI 2024.
[95:5:10] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:95 (sub 5, 6)
