=== NOTES 2:100 | Sectoral Regulators – Trai, Cci, Fssai, Cerc/sercs, Pngrb, Aera, Data Protection Board
## SUB 0 | Competition Commission of India
[100:0:0] - Statutory body under the **Competition Act, 2002**, as amended by the **Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007**; **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**.
[100:0:1] - The Act **replaced the MRTP Act, 1969** and its **MRTP Commission** – shift from curbing monopolies to **promoting competition**.
[100:0:2] - **Established:** notified **14 October 2003**, but legal challenges delayed it; **fully constituted / functional in March 2009** (MCA: "established in March 2009").
[100:0:3] - **Function:** to **ensure fair competition in markets**, prevent practices with adverse effect on competition, protect consumers – not registering competitors or monitoring capital markets.
[100:0:4] - **Composition:** **Chairperson + 2 to 6 other members** appointed by the **Central Government** (original 2002 Act: up to 10) – so "chairperson and five members" is wrong.
[100:0:5] TABLE head: CCI area | What it does
  [100:0:5.0] Anti-competitive agreements | Cartels, bid-rigging
  [100:0:5.1] Abuse of dominant position | e.g. WhatsApp 2021 privacy policy – Meta fined ₹213.14 crore
  [100:0:5.2] Combinations | Mergers and acquisitions; ₹2,000 crore deal-value threshold for start-up "killer acquisitions"
[100:0:6] - Appeals: **NCLAT from 26 May 2017** (earlier **COMPAT**) → Supreme Court. CCI's **Digital Markets Division**; proposed **Digital Competition Bill** for **Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises**.
[100:0:7] - Market forms: many sellers of differentiated brands (e.g. **toothpaste**) = **monopolistic competition**; identical product = perfect competition.
[100:0:8] ~~ Sources: web search snippets – mca.gov.in CCI page and ies.gov.in Arthapedia (CCI established March 2009; set up 2003); NextGen Indian Economy P1 - APPSC 01 p.54, 04 p.29; app notes 2:100 (CCI)
## SUB 1 | TRAI and TDSAT
[100:1:0] - **TRAI** = **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India**, set up **20 February 1997** under the **TRAI Act, 1997**; regulates **tariffs, interconnection, quality of service**.
[100:1:1] - **TDSAT** (May 2000), created by the **TRAI (Amendment) Act, 2000**, to **separate adjudication** from regulation; also hears appeals under the **IT Act, 2000** and the **DPDP Act**. No separate "TDSAT Act".
[100:1:2] - **TRAI MyCall** app revamped for call-quality rating (Aug 2026), after **DND** and **MySpeed**.
[100:1:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:100 (TRAI, TDSAT)
## SUB 2 | FSSAI – Food Regulator
[100:2:0] - **FSSAI**: under the **Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006**; set up **2008**; administered by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** (not DGHS). It is the agency that enforces food safety laws (not FDA, WHO or FAO).
[100:2:1] - The Act consolidated **eight** laws and orders incl. the **Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954**.
[100:2:2] - From **1 July 2019** (Packaging Regulations, 2018): **no recycled plastics or newspaper** to wrap food.
[100:2:3] - **Eat Right India** (2018). **2026 reforms**: perpetual validity of licences; registration up to **₹1.5 crore** turnover, State licence ₹1.5-50 crore, Central licence above **₹50 crore**.
[100:2:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:100 (FSSAI)
## SUB 3 | Regulators at a Glance; Appointment, Removal and Appeals
[100:3:0] TABLE head: Regulator | Parent Act | Set up | Ministry
  [100:3:0.0] TRAI | TRAI Act, 1997 | 20 Feb 1997 | Telecom
  [100:3:0.1] CCI | Competition Act, 2002 | 2003 / functional 2009 | Corporate Affairs
  [100:3:0.2] FSSAI | FSS Act, 2006 | 2008 | Health
  [100:3:0.3] PNGRB | PNGRB Act, 2006 | 1 Oct 2007 | Petroleum
  [100:3:0.4] AERA | AERA Act, 2008 | 2009 | Civil Aviation
  [100:3:0.5] CEA, CERC, APTEL | Electricity Act, 2003 | APTEL 2004 | Power
[100:3:1] - Chairpersons are **appointed by the Central Government** on a search-cum-selection committee's recommendation (CCI's headed by the **CJI or nominee**); removed by the Centre only on grounds in the Act (insolvency, moral turpitude, incapacity, abuse of position) after a hearing – not by a Parliament resolution.
[100:3:2] TABLE head: Order of | Appeal to
  [100:3:2.0] TRAI | TDSAT → SC
  [100:3:2.1] CCI | NCLAT → SC
  [100:3:2.2] CERC / SERC / PNGRB | APTEL → SC
  [100:3:2.3] DPBI | TDSAT (60 days) → SC
[100:3:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:100 (regulators table, appointment, appeals)
## SUB 4 | Energy and Airport Regulators – CERC, SERCs, PNGRB, AERA
[100:4:0] - **CERC** = inter-State electricity; regulator of carbon trading under the **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme**. **SERCs** = intra-State tariffs. **APTEL** hears appeals from CERC, SERCs and PNGRB.
[100:4:1] - **APERC** constituted **1999** under the **AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998**; under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 it stayed joint regulator for **not more than six months**.
[100:4:2] - **PNGRB** regulates **City Gas Distribution** and authorises pipelines; not electricity. **Jul 2026**: **10 Geographical Areas** in AP approved for CGD; **East Godavari** has the most connections.
[100:4:3] - **Kakinada–Srikakulam natural gas pipeline** (about 271 km): authorised by PNGRB (16 Jul 2014) to **AP Gas Distribution Corporation (APGDC)**; APGDC later surrendered it and PNGRB **terminated the authorisation on 1 Dec 2023**.
[100:4:4] - **AERA** regulates **aeronautical charges** at major airports.
[100:4:5] ~~ Sources: web search snippets – Lok Sabha answer eparlib.nic.in AU647 (July 2024) and acuite.in rating report on APGDC / Kakinada-Srikakulam pipeline; app notes 2:100 (electricity, PNGRB, AERA)
## SUB 5 | Data Protection Board of India
[100:5:0] - **DPDP Act, 2023** (Aug 2023): consent-based processing. **DPBI**: adjudicatory body, **4 members** (DPDP Rules 2025), appointed by the Centre on a Selection Committee's advice.
[100:5:1] - Penalty up to **₹250 crore**, **no imprisonment**; appeal to **TDSAT within 60 days** → Supreme Court.
[100:5:2] - DPDP Act amended **RTI Sec. 8(1)(j)** (wider personal-information exemption).
[100:5:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:100 (Data Protection Board)
## SUB 6 | Education, Film and Other Regulators
[100:6:0] - **Education** is in the **Concurrent List** (moved from the State List by the **42nd Amendment, 1976**) – regulated by both Union and States; UGC, AICTE, NCTE are central regulators.
[100:6:1] - **NCTE and NAAC** signed the MoU (2002) for **accreditation of teacher education institutions**.
[100:6:2] - **CBFC** (Central Board of Film Certification), under the **Ministry of I&B** (Cinematograph Act, 1952), regulates **public exhibition of films**.
[100:6:3] - **Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025** (HECI idea): introduced in **Lok Sabha, Dec 2025** → **Joint Committee**; not passed. Would repeal **UGC Act 1956, AICTE Act 1987, NCTE Act 1993** (not the NMC Act 2019); three councils – **Regulatory, Accreditation, Standards** (no **Funding Council**).
[100:6:4] ~~ Sources: PMF Lens 2026-01 part 2 p.50 (education in Concurrent List); app notes 2:100 (VBSA Bill); NCTE-NAAC MoU and CBFC – general knowledge (not checked)

=== NOTES 2:103 | Civil Society, Ngos, Shgs and Pressure Groups in Governance; Fcra Regulation
## SUB 0 | Pressure Groups – Meaning, Types and Techniques
[103:0:0] - **Pressure group**: an **organised group** that seeks to influence public policy **without contesting elections or seeking office**; also called **interest groups, lobby groups**; labelled the **"Anonymous Empire"**.
[103:0:1] - Test: seeks to form the government → political party. **Members of a trade union** = pressure group; members of the Lok Sabha, a panchayat or the Cabinet are not (MPPSC 2017). The **Election Commission** is a constitutional authority, not a pressure group.
[103:0:2] - **Almond and Powell**: **institutional, associational, non-associational, anomic**.
[103:0:3] TABLE head: Type | Indian examples
  [103:0:3.0] Business – most powerful and largest | FICCI, CII, ASSOCHAM – work for commerce and industry interests
  [103:0:3.1] Trade union | AITUC, INTUC, CITU, BMS, HMS
  [103:0:3.2] Agrarian | Bharatiya Kisan Union, All India Kisan Sabha (oldest), Shetkari Sanghatana (Maharashtra); Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana = farmers' union, Maharashtra, founder Raju Shetti
  [103:0:3.3] Professional | Indian Medical Association, Bar associations
  [103:0:3.4] Women / feminist, caste, religious, student | Feminist groups are organised social (interest) groups pressing for women's rights
[103:0:4] # Techniques
[103:0:5] TABLE head: Technique | Meaning
  [103:0:5.0] Lobbying | Dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation and regulation
  [103:0:5.1] Propagandising | Shaping public opinion
  [103:0:5.2] Electioneering | Helping sympathetic candidates win
  [103:0:5.3] Petitioning; strikes, bandhs, dharnas | Memoranda; direct disruption
  [103:0:5.4] Litigation | PILs (e.g. ADR on candidates' backgrounds)
[103:0:6] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth Indian Polity 8th ed. part 2 p.397-398 (pressure groups: FICCI, agrarian groups, lobbying); NextGen Polity full p.1 ("Anonymous Empire"); app notes 2:103 (pressure groups)
## SUB 1 | Media, Press Freedom and the Press Council of India
[103:1:0] - **Fourth Estate** = **the Press** (media) – watchdog and **agenda-setter**: media sets the public agenda **because** it selectively filters news (A and R true, R explains A).
[103:1:1] - **Freedom of the press** is not named in the Constitution; it is read into **Article 19(1)(a)** (Art. 19), not Arts. 14, 21 or 32.
[103:1:2] - **Press Council of India**: first set up **1966** (Press Council Act, 1965); now under the **Press Council Act, 1978**; **statutory, quasi-judicial**; **Chairman + 28 members**; **print media only**; can warn, admonish, censure – no punitive powers. Chairman by custom a **retired SC judge**, chosen by the RS Chairman, LS Speaker and a PCI member.
[103:1:3] TABLE head: PCI Chairman | Term
  [103:1:3.0] Markandey Katju | 2011-2014
  [103:1:3.1] Justice C.K. (Chandramauli Kumar) Prasad | 2014-2022
  [103:1:3.2] Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai | 17 Jun 2022 – Dec 2025; again from 24 April 2026 (three years) – current, as of Nov 2026
[103:1:4] - Problems: paid news, fake news, concentrated ownership. RSF index (May 2026): India **"very serious"**.
[103:1:5] ~~ Sources: Daily EM CA 17 Oct 2026 (src/current-affairs/octlatest-daily-em-ca-2026-10-17.txt) p.6 (PCI reconstituted; Ranjana Prakash Desai from 24 Apr 2026; Art. 19(1)(a)); web search snippets – counterview.net / ukhrultimes.com (Desai's first term 2022-25); app notes 2:103 (media)
## SUB 2 | SHGs and Women's Microfinance – DWCRA, SERP, Velugu
[103:2:0] - SHGs in AP are popularly called **DWCRA groups**; a **self-help group** has **10 to 20 members** (NABARD / national norm).
[103:2:1] - **Velugu** (AP District Poverty Initiatives Project) was launched in **2000** to organise and federate women's SHGs; run by **SERP** (autonomous society of the Rural Development Dept); renamed **Indira Kranthi Patham** (Velugu + DWCRA merged) under Congress; Velugu name restored after 2014.
[103:2:2] - **SAPAP** (1995, UNDP): base for Velugu. **Pavala Vaddi** (2004) for SHGs. **Mana Kirana**: general stores run by DWCRA groups supplying quality goods.
[103:2:3] - **MEPMA** (urban): G.O. Ms 414 of 4 Jun 2007, launched **1 Sep 2007**; SHG → Slum Level Federation → Town Level Federation.
[103:2:4] TABLE head: National body | Year | Feature
  [103:2:4.0] Rashtriya Mahila Kosh | 1993 | Society (Societies Registration Act 1860), Ministry of WCD; lends to NGOs/MFIs who on-lend to poor women
  [103:2:4.1] SHG-Bank Linkage | 1992 (NABARD) | Banks lend to SHGs
  [103:2:4.2] DAY-NRLM | — | Rural Development; Pashu, Krishi, Bank, Bima, Poshan Sakhis
[103:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP Economy static 1-01 p.14-15 (Velugu 2000; Pavala Vaddi 2004; IKP); web search snippet – Rajya Sabha answer 05.08.2014 (SHGs of 10-20 members); app notes 2:103 (SHGs)

## SUB 4 | NGOs, CBOs and Social Service
[103:4:0] - NGOs are to be treated as **partners of government in development** (National Policy on the Voluntary Sector, **2007**, Planning Commission: partnership, not subordination). The APPSC key printed "**people's representatives**".
[103:4:1] - **Social service** is provided by **both government and private individuals**, profit and non-profit organisations.
[103:4:2] - **Community Based Organisations (CBOs)**: non-profit groups that **extend social services locally**.
[103:4:3] - Civil society = the **"third sector"** beside State and market; shift from welfare delivery to **rights, advocacy and watchdog** work.
[103:4:4] TABLE head: Legal form | Law
  [103:4:4.0] Society | Societies Registration Act, 1860
  [103:4:4.1] Private trust | Indian Trusts Act, 1882
  [103:4:4.2] Public charitable trust | State laws (e.g. Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950)
  [103:4:4.3] Not-for-profit company | Section 8, Companies Act, 2013
[103:4:5] - **Bhagavatula Charitable Trust** (Yellamanchili, Visakhapatnam) – founded by **B.V. Parameswara Rao**.
[103:4:6] - **Amaravati farmers' agitation**: Dec 2019 – June 2024 (**1,631 days**), led by **Amaravati Parirakshana Samithi**.
[103:4:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:103 (civil society, NGOs, AP examples); BCT founder – general knowledge (not checked)
## SUB 5 | FCRA Regulation
[103:5:0] TABLE head: Year | Change
  [103:5:0.0] 1976 | First FCRA
  [103:5:0.1] 2010 | FCRA 2010 replaced it
  [103:5:0.2] 2016 | Retrospective: Indian subsidiaries of foreign firms not "foreign source" (after Delhi HC 2014)
  [103:5:0.3] 2020 | Designated account at SBI, New Delhi; admin cap 50% → 20%; sub-granting banned
  [103:5:0.4] 25 Mar 2026 | Amendment Bill (asset takeover of cancelled NGOs) – deferred
  [103:5:0.5] 22 Jun 2026 | Amendment Rules notified
[103:5:1] - Administered by the **MHA** (FEMA by RBI and ED). Registration valid **5 years**; **14,538** active (15 Apr 2026). Cancellation grounds: breach, **non-functioning**, defaults – not office location.
[103:5:2] - **Public Health Foundation of India**: FCRA licence suspended/cancelled (April 2017) for using foreign funds for **lobbying with parliamentarians** (on tobacco control).
[103:5:3] - **Rules 2026**: foreign citizens other than **PIOs** as key functionaries make an NGO ineligible; renewal needs **₹10 lakh** spent over two years.
[103:5:4] - Every NGO receiving foreign contributions must register (or get prior permission) under the **FCRA**, besides its registration as a society, trust or Section 8 company.
[103:5:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:103 (FCRA, PHFI)

=== NOTES 2:105 | Indian Society – Salient Features, Unity in Diversity, Continuity and Change
## SUB 0 | Founders and Classical Theorists
[105:0:0] # Founders of sociology
[105:0:1] TABLE head: Thinker | Key ideas (exam answer words)
  [105:0:1.0] Auguste Comte (1798–1857) | Father of Sociology; coined "sociology" (1838) after first calling it "social physics"; positivism; motto "Order and Progress"; sociology an encyclopaedic (synthetic) science
  [105:0:1.1] Herbert Spencer | Social evolution (Social Statics, 1851); society like a biological organism; "survival of the fittest"
  [105:0:1.2] Emile Durkheim | Father of Modern Sociology; social facts, collective conscience, anomie, sacred-profane; religion builds solidarity
  [105:0:1.3] Karl Marx | Scientific socialism; historical materialism; surplus value; alienation; class struggle; class fixed by relations of production; Asiatic mode of production (India)
  [105:0:1.4] Max Weber | Verstehen; ideal type; class, status and power; 3 authorities; 4 social actions; bureaucracy; *Protestant Ethic*, *The Religion of India*
  [105:0:1.5] C. Wright Mills | *The Sociological Imagination* (1959); power elite (political, military, corporate)
  [105:0:1.6] Georg Simmel | formal sociology; society exists because individuals interact; studied social interaction and city life; dyad = 2, triad = 3
  [105:0:1.7] Manuel Castells | network society (1996)
[105:0:2] - **Comte's three stages:** **theological** (rain = God's will), **metaphysical** (abstract forces of nature), **positive** (rain explained by atmospheric processes); positivism rests on **observation, experiment, evidence**, never on divine forces.
[105:0:3] - **Durkheim:** **social facts** = laws, customs, religion, traditions existing **outside** the individual and shaping behaviour; **anomie** = normlessness from rapid change (crime, suicide); books *The Division of Labour in Society*, *The Rules of Sociological Method*, *Suicide* ("Collective Conscience" is a concept, not a book).
[105:0:4] - **Marx:** **historical materialism** = the economic base shapes society, politics, culture; **surplus value** = value workers produce beyond their wages; founder of the **conflict perspective**.
[105:0:5]   - Alienation from the **product**, from the **production process** (forced, monotonous work), from **fellow humans**, from **oneself** (one's human nature).
[105:0:6]   - **Communist Manifesto (1848)** – written **jointly by Marx and Engels**; central theme = **class struggle**; *Das Kapital* 1867.
[105:0:7]   - **Religion:** "the **opium (intoxicant)** of the people", "the **heart of a heartless world**" – Marx (1844).
[105:0:8]   - **Asiatic mode of production:** Marx's label for India – village communities, no private landed property, despotic state (not Weber).
[105:0:9] - **Weber's authority:** **traditional** (custom, sanctity of tradition – a tribal chief), **charismatic** (personality), **legal-rational** (rules). Bureaucracy: hierarchy, **impersonality**, written rules, **merit** appointment.
[105:0:10] - **Weber's social action:** **instrumentally rational** (goals), **value-rational** (values, ethics), **affective** (emotions), **traditional** (customs).
[105:0:11] - **Mills' sociological imagination:** link **biography** (one's own life and troubles) with **history**; one person's unemployment (trouble) ↔ **economic slowdown** (public issue).
[105:0:12] - **Malinowski** (functionalist): **strong personal attachments and death** are the main sources of religious belief.
[105:0:13] # Other names asked
[105:0:14] TABLE head: Concept / book | Scholar

## SUB 1 | Basic Concepts – Society, Community, Culture, Groups and Roles
[105:1:0] # Society and community
[105:1:1] - **Main purpose of the sociologist:** to **study society** scientifically; sociology = **the scientific study of society**.
[105:1:2] - **Human society is unique** because it rests on **culture**; culture (not language alone) separates human from animal society.
[105:1:3] - **Community (MacIver):** a group sharing "the basic conditions of a common life"; its **bases = locality (territory) + community sentiment (we-feeling, solidarity)**.
[105:1:4] - **Coercion:** a person or group **forcibly imposes its opinion/will** on another.
[105:1:5] - **Institutionalisation:** the process by which **conventions and rules develop** and become stable in social forms.
[105:1:6] - **Reference group:** the group whose standards we **compare ourselves with** and emulate, without belonging to it.
[105:1:7] - **Social system:** social structure + culture + personality (Parsons).
[105:1:8] # Culture
[105:1:9] - **Language** is a product of **culture**; **language, literature, art** = **non-material culture** (tools, buildings = material).
[105:1:10] - **Not an essential component of culture:** the **economy** (tradition, language, customs are).
[105:1:11] - **Cultural lag:** non-material culture trails material change (Ogburn).
[105:1:12] # Beliefs, values, roles
[105:1:13] - "**Men are stronger than women**" = a **belief** (a proposition held true; "trust" in translation), not a value, oath or approval.
[105:1:14] - **Independently defined role:** **painter**; father, teacher, officer need a counter-role.
[105:1:15] - **Sex vs gender:** sex = **biological** difference; gender = **social** role assigned to each sex.
[105:1:16] # Measuring attitudes
[105:1:17] - **Social distance scale:** **Emory Bogardus** (1925).
[105:1:18] - **Equal-appearing interval scale:** **L.L. Thurstone** (1928); Guttman = cumulative scale.
[105:1:19] ~~ Sources: OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 1 l.464, l.1039; Part 2 l.816, l.1562-1703; web: sociology.institute (MacIver); general knowledge (scales, roles)
## SUB 2 | Social Psychology and Sociology of Education
[105:2:0] # Education and society
[105:2:1] - **Educational sociology** = **application of the principles of sociology to education** (F.J. Brown); sociology of education = sociological analysis of education as an institution.
[105:2:2] - **Education as a result of social change:** social change creates a **demand for education** (new knowledge and skills).
[105:2:3] - **Pragmatism** (Dewey): ideas without action are meaningless; truth verified by **experiment**; useful knowledge only. "Develop the individual and society develops automatically" is **not** pragmatist.
[105:2:4] - **Humanistic realism:** classics studied to **cultivate the intellect** and make man rational and practical.
[105:2:5] - **Character formation:** best through **good character models** (example), not sermons.
[105:2:6] - **J. Krishnamurti:** knowledge is **scientific, collective, individual**.
[105:2:7] # Psychology terms
[105:2:8] - **Personality** (APPSC key): the **behaviour** of the individual (sum of behaviour patterns); Allport stresses inner systems.
[105:2:9] - **Leadership:** ability to **influence others' attitudes or behaviour** in a desired way.
[105:2:10] - **Role play:** best method to **re-examine one's own and others' views, feelings and behaviour**.
[105:2:11] - **Rorschach inkblot test** (1921): detects **thought disorder**.
[105:2:12] - *Theories of Motivation* (1959): **K.B. Madsen**; Maslow – *A Theory of Human Motivation* (1943).
[105:2:13] - **Life stages:** **adolescence** = rapid change, identity search ("storm and stress"); relative **social stability** comes in **adulthood**.
[105:2:14] ~~ Sources: general knowledge, not checked; web: TAMU catalogue (F.J. Brown, Educational Sociology 1947); WSU lifespan text (stability in early adulthood)
## SUB 3 | Unity in Diversity and National Integration
[105:3:0] # Diversity
[105:3:1] - **Salient features:** **multi-ethnic, multi-lingual, multi-class, broadly patriarchal**; matrilineal exceptions **Khasi, Jaintia, Garo**.
[105:3:2] - **Structural features (UPPSC 2014):** excess village population, **various religions, various castes**; **poverty** is an economic condition, not a feature.
[105:3:3] - **Languages:** about **122** major languages (Census 2011) vs **22** in the **Eighth Schedule**; **4** language families.
[105:3:4] - **Religions:** 6 major religions; Hindus a minority in **8** States/UTs.
[105:3:5]   - **Dakhma** (Tower of Silence) = **Parsi/Zoroastrian** exposure of the dead to vultures.
[105:3:6]   - **Sallekhana/Santhara** = **Jain** fast unto death; **Rajasthan HC** banned it (2015), SC stayed the ruling.
[105:3:7]   - **Durkheim:** religion = beliefs and practices about **sacred things**; it strengthens **social solidarity**.
[105:3:8] - **Festivals:** **Pongal** = harvest festival of **Tamil Nadu** (Sankranti in AP).
[105:3:9] - **Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya** (Museum of Mankind, story of human evolution) – **Bhopal**.
[105:3:10] - **International Mother Language Day: 21 February** (UNESCO, 1999).
[105:3:11] # Bonds of unity
[105:3:12] - **Shankaracharya** sent priests from southern temples to the north and vice versa; Onam; Bhakti-Sufi blending. Linguistic homogeneity is **not** a bond.
[105:3:13] - **Linguistic reorganisation** = a **"safety valve"** accommodating linguistic aspirations, making India a **"State-Nation"**; **Andhra (1953)** began it, the first linguistic State.
[105:3:14] # National integration
[105:3:15] - **Dimensions:** **political, economic, social, cultural, psychological** – inter-related.
[105:3:16] - **National Integration Council:** constituted **1961** (after the National Integration Conference, chaired by **Nehru**/PM; first met **1962**) to fight **communalism, casteism, regionalism**.
[105:3:17] - **Emotional Integration Committee (1961):** chaired by **Dr Sampurnanand**.
[105:3:18] - **Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (2015):** pairs States/UTs to promote **national integration**.
[105:3:19] - **Art. 350-B:** Special Officer for **Linguistic Minorities** (not a Finance Commission).
[105:3:20] - **Social stability:** society keeps **peace, order, harmony, continuity and effective functioning of institutions** despite change; key feature **inclusive development**; promoted by **family** (primary agent of socialisation), education, **welfare and social justice**, tolerance; threatened by **regionalism**, poverty, extremism. Tolerance does not threaten it.
[105:3:21] > A-R (UPPCS 2025): "integration is multi-dimensional" ✓; "NIC constituted 1961 on unity in diversity" ✓; but R does not explain A → **both true, R not the correct explanation**.
[105:3:22] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.5-7, p.17; NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.1-8; Laxmikanth Part 2 (Eighth Schedule); app notes 2:105 sub 0-1; web: Drishti IAS UPPCS 2025 key Q99
[105:3:23] - **Women and culture:** the place of women in a society is the main symbol (index) of its culture – credited to **K.M. Panikkar** (APPSC 2000 key; A.S. Altekar made the same point).
## SUB 4 | Indian Sociologists and Approaches
[105:4:0] # Who's who
[105:4:1] TABLE head: Sociologist | Idea / work
  [105:4:1.0] G.S. Ghurye | Father of Indian Sociology; Bombay School; *Caste and Race in India* (1932); caste grew out of Indo-Aryan culture
  [105:4:1.1] M.N. Srinivas | Father of Modern Indian Sociology; Sanskritisation, Westernisation, dominant caste; *Religion and Society among the Coorgs*; joint family modified, not eliminated
  [105:4:1.2] Irawati Karve | first woman sociologist; first to study Indian kinship systematically; *Kinship Organization in India* (1953); four kinship zones; kinship = backbone of Indian social organisation
  [105:4:1.3] Yogendra Singh | *Modernization of Indian Tradition* (1973); orthogenetic vs heterogenetic change
  [105:4:1.4] Andre Beteille | *Caste, Class and Power* (1965, Sripuram, TN); caste = cumulative, class = dispersed inequality
  [105:4:1.5] Louis Dumont | *Homo Hierarchicus* (1966): purity-pollution, encompassing Brahmin; with D. Pocock founded *Contributions to Indian Sociology* (1957)
  [105:4:1.6] Henry Maine | status to contract; *Ancient Law* (1861); *Village Communities in the East and West* (1871); studied the joint family by the Indological (textual) approach
  [105:4:1.7] A.R. Desai | *Social Background of Indian Nationalism*: nationalism from socio-economic change under colonialism
  [105:4:1.8] K.M. Kapadia | marriage and family = central institutions of Indian society
  [105:4:1.9] N.K. Bose | change in India through adjustment, not conflict
  [105:4:1.10] D.P. Mukerji | tradition essential to understand Indian society
  [105:4:1.11] J.H. Hutton | caste from social and religious disabilities
  [105:4:1.12] Verrier Elwin | tribes should develop by their own culture
  [105:4:1.13] B.R. Ambedkar | caste = division of labourers, not only of labour
[105:4:2] - **Indological approach:** relies on **texts** (Smritis, Puranas, epics such as the **Mahabharata**); **field-view** approach relies on contemporary surveys.
[105:4:3] - **Chronology:** Ancient Law 1861 → Village Communities 1871 → Caste and Race 1932 → Kinship Organization 1953 → Village India 1955 → Homo Hierarchicus 1966.
[105:4:4] - **Note:** *Family and Kin in Indo-European Culture* (1955) is by **Ghurye** (the Rocket table credits Karve) – general knowledge, not checked.
[105:4:5] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.3, p.13-16; NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.15; app notes 2:105 sub 2, 6
## SUB 5 | Continuity and Change
[105:5:0] # Forces of change
[105:5:1] TABLE head: Force | Effect
  [105:5:1.0] Education | individualism, rights; questions joint-family customs
  [105:5:1.1] Urbanisation | nuclear households; family a consumption unit; more individualism, competition and social distance
  [105:5:1.2] Law | Caste Disabilities Removal Act 1850 (no loss of inheritance on conversion); Art. 17; Hindu Code; RTE Act 2009 (in force 2010, Art. 21A)
  [105:5:1.3] Technology | digital citizenship; DPDP Act 2023
[105:5:2] - **Nuclear households** do not reject the **joint-family ideal**; continuity survives structural change.
[105:5:3] - **A.M. Shah:** the joint family **changes in structure but continues in function**.
[105:5:4] - **Harappan continuity** is limited: the **script is undeciphered**.
[105:5:5] - **Feb 2026:** a Mother Language Day report proposed a **National Mission for Mother-Tongue-Based Multilingual Education**.
[105:5:6] # Terms of change
[105:5:7] TABLE head: Term | Originator | Meaning
  [105:5:7.0] Great / Little Tradition | Robert Redfield; applied to India by Milton Singer (*When a Great Tradition Modernizes*, Madras) and McKim Marriott | elite-Sanskritic vs local-folk
  [105:5:7.1] Universalisation | McKim Marriott (*Village India*, 1955) | little → great (upward)
  [105:5:7.2] Parochialisation | McKim Marriott | great → localised (downward)
  [105:5:7.3] Cultural lag | W.F. Ogburn (*Social Change*, 1922) | non-material lags behind material
  [105:5:7.4] Orthogenetic / heterogenetic | Yogendra Singh | internal / external sources of change
[105:5:8] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:105 sub 3-4; Rocket Indian Society p.14, p.16

=== NOTES 2:106 | Family – Types, Functions and Changing Structure in India
## SUB 0 | Types of Family – Residence, Descent, Authority, Orientation
[106:0:0] # Family as an institution
[106:0:1] - **Family** (Latin *familia*, household) = the **basic, primary** social institution and the child's **first school** (language, customs, values).
[106:0:2] - **Murdock's definition:** a group marked by **common residence, economic co-operation and reproduction**.
[106:0:3] - **Consanguine family** ("united blood family"): built on **blood ties**; **conjugal** family: built on the marriage bond.
[106:0:4] - **Family of orientation** = the family one is **born into** and socialised in (parents, siblings); **family of procreation** = set up by one's **marriage** (spouse, children). The **spouse** does not belong to the family of orientation.
[106:0:5] - **Siblings** = children of the same parents.
[106:0:6] # Classification
[106:0:7] TABLE head: Basis | Types
  [106:0:7.0] Size / structure | nuclear (husband, wife, unmarried children); joint/extended (two or more generations)
  [106:0:7.1] Residence | patrilocal (husband's family), matrilocal/uxorilocal (wife's family), ambilocal/bilocal (either or both alternately), neolocal (new home), duolocal (each spouse in own natal home), avunculocal (with the husband's maternal uncle, "matula")
  [106:0:7.2] Descent / inheritance | patrilineal (father to son), matrilineal (mother to daughter)
  [106:0:7.3] Authority | patriarchal (oldest male; male-dominated), matriarchal (woman holds authority – more theoretical than real)
  [106:0:7.4] Marriage | monogamous; polygamous (polygyny, polyandry)
  [106:0:7.5] Centre | affection-centred (filiocentric) family run around the children's wishes
[106:0:8] - **Neolocal residence** does not support an extended family and speeds the decline of joint families.
[106:0:9] - **Biological vs social father:** separated in **polyandrous (polygamous)** families, e.g. the Toda.
[106:0:10] - **Okka** (Coorgs, Srinivas) = **patrilineal, patrilocal joint family**.
[106:0:11] - **⚠ Trap:** matriliny ≠ matriarchy; duolocal ≠ bilocal.
[106:0:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.9-10; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 2 p.3; Rocket Indian Society p.18; app notes 2:106 sub 0-1
## SUB 1 | Functions of the Family and Socialisation
[106:1:0] # Functions
[106:1:1] - **Primary functions (NextGen):** reproduction and rearing, **culture transmission**, home, **agent of socialisation**, **status ascription**, social control.
[106:1:2] - **Secondary:** economic (now **consumption** more than production), educational, religious, recreational.
[106:1:3] - Family **protects** members from social and economic risks; approved sex relations **prevent social disorder**; gives caste, religion, language and **national identity**.
[106:1:4] - **Inheritance** = passing on property (not consumption of goods).
[106:1:5] - **Dysfunction** = persistent failure of functions (abuse, alcoholism).
[106:1:6] TABLE head: Scholar | Number | Functions
  [106:1:6.0] Murdock | 4 universal | sexual, reproductive (birth of children), economic, educational
  [106:1:6.1] MacIver | essential / non-essential | essential: sex need, procreation and rearing, home; non-essential: religious, educational, economic, health, recreation
  [106:1:6.2] Ogburn (and Nimkoff) | 7 | incl. status-giving, affectional; all but affection pass to outside agencies – "loss of functions"
  [106:1:6.3] Talcott Parsons | 2 irreducible | primary socialisation; stabilisation of adult personality
[106:1:7] - **Why the family emerged:** sexual, economic and reproductive needs – **all these**.
[106:1:8] - **Family today** is no longer the main unit of production and has **lost many traditional functions** – both statements correct.
[106:1:9] - **First and most important agency of socialisation:** the **family** (then school, peer group, community).
[106:1:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.10; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 2 l.1758; app notes 2:106 sub 0, 2; general knowledge (MacIver)
## SUB 2 | Joint Family – Features and Scholars
[106:2:0] # Features
[106:2:1] - **Joint family:** **co-residence**, one hearth, **joint ownership of property**, **common worship**, pooled income; members are **kin** – private property and "unrelated members" are not features.
[106:2:2] - **Karve's definition:** people under one roof, one hearth, common property, common worship, related as kindred – an **extended kinship group**; jointness = functional unity and obligations, may hold common property.
[106:2:3] # Scholars
[106:2:4] TABLE head: Scholar | Statement
  [106:2:4.0] Henry Maine | studied the joint family from Hindu law texts – Indological approach
  [106:2:4.1] K.M. Kapadia | *Marriage and Family in India* (1955); pioneer of family studies
  [106:2:4.2] I.P. Desai | Mahuva study; five degrees of jointness; 61% nuclear, 39% joint
  [106:2:4.3] A.M. Shah | *The Household Dimension of the Family in India* (1973); family ≠ household; developmental cycle; Indians mostly lived in small and simple households; changes in structure, continues in function
  [106:2:4.4] Milton Singer | industrialists of Madras – traditional family and values resilient; with Orenstein: joint family not dissolved
  [106:2:4.5] Ramkrishna Mukherjee | joint families over-represented in trade and higher occupations
  [106:2:4.6] M.S. Gore | nuclear rises, emotional bonds persist
  [106:2:4.7] Leela Dube | family reproduces patriarchy
  [106:2:4.8] M.N. Srinivas | joint family modified, not eliminated
[106:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.13-17; Rocket Indian Society p.15-16; app notes 2:106 sub 3
## SUB 3 | Changing Structure and Urban Families
[106:3:0] # Causes of change
[106:3:1] TABLE head: Factor | Effect
  [106:3:1.0] Industrialisation and urbanisation | the main factors behind joint-family disintegration; family: production → consumption unit; youth economically independent
  [106:3:1.1] Migration, housing | rural-urban migration and small housing break up joint families
  [106:3:1.2] Women's employment | more female-headed households
  [106:3:1.3] Law, education | Hindu Succession Act, labour laws, rational education
[106:3:2] - **Modern family:** financial independence, **decline of religious control**, **more freedom for women**; increased religious feeling is **not** a trait.
[106:3:3] - Urbanisation does **not** eliminate all emotional bonds of joint families.
[106:3:4] - **T.K. Oommen:** urban families by livelihood, **authority structure**, social milieu, value pattern; **proprietary class** = joint, strong elder-male authority.
[106:3:5] - **Single-parent / female-headed rise:** widowhood, marital instability, male migration (not joint-family expansion).
[106:3:6] - **High-risk families:** severe social, economic, health, psychological or environmental challenges; causes economic (poverty, **debt** – economic, not psychological), social (**exclusion**), psychological (stress, addiction); elderly care rests on **filial piety**.
[106:3:7] # Data
[106:3:8] TABLE head: Census 2001 → 2011 | Nuclear | Joint
  [106:3:8.0] Rural | 50.7 → 52.1% (rose) | 20.1 → 16.8%
  [106:3:8.1] Urban | 54.3 → 52.3% (fell) | 16.5 → 14.6%
[106:3:9] - **NFHS-6** (2023–24): MoHFW, nodal **IIPS Mumbai**; TFR **2.0**. NFHS-5: urban TFR **1.6**; household size 4.6 → **4.4**.
[106:3:10] - **Jun 2026:** AP CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu** urged a return to the **joint family** and incentives for families with two or more children.
[106:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.9-18; app notes 2:106 sub 4, 7, 8
## SUB 4 | Matrilineal Systems and Family Theories
[106:4:0] # Matrilineal communities
[106:4:1] TABLE head: Community | Region | Feature
  [106:4:1.0] Nair – tharavad (tharwad) | Kerala | Marumakkathayam; abolished by Kerala Joint Family System (Abolition) Act 1975
  [106:4:1.1] Tiyans, some Moplas, Bants | Malabar/Kanara | tharawad = a woman, her siblings, her sisters' children
  [106:4:1.2] Khasi | Meghalaya | matrilocal; youngest daughter inherits (ultimogeniture)
  [106:4:1.3] Garo | Meghalaya | Machong = matrilineage; heiress's husband Nokma heads
[106:4:2] - In matrilineal systems power usually stays with **men** (maternal uncles).
[106:4:3] - **Yakö of Nigeria:** **double (dual) descent**.
[106:4:4] # Evolution and critique of the family
[106:4:5] - **L.H. Morgan** (*Ancient Society*, 1877), five forms in order: **consanguine → punaluan → syndyasmian → patriarchal → monogamian**.
[106:4:6] - **Engels** (*Origin of the Family*, 1884): the monogamous family arose with private property.
[106:4:7] - **David Cooper** (*The Death of the Family*, 1971): the family is the **ideal (ideological conditioning) instrument of an exploitative society**.
[106:4:8] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:106 sub 5; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 2 p.3; web: Millan 1974 review of Cooper (opus4.kobv.de); general knowledge (Morgan)
## SUB 5 | Family Laws – Inheritance, Adoption, Family Courts
[106:5:0] TABLE head: Mitakshara | Dayabhaga
  [106:5:0.0] Vijnaneshwara on Yajnavalkya Smriti (Kalyani Chalukya court) | Jimutavahana; Bengal (West Bengal), Assam
  [106:5:0.1] son's right by birth | right only on the father's death
[106:5:1] # Family legislation
[106:5:2] TABLE head: Law / case | Provides
  [106:5:2.0] Hindu Succession Act 1956 | part of the Hindu Code (advocate Ambedkar); 2005 amendment, Sec. 6: daughters coparceners by birth
  [106:5:2.1] Vineeta Sharma (2020) | applies whether or not the father was alive in 2005
  [106:5:2.2] AP amendment 1985 | 20 years before the central one
  [106:5:2.3] Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956 | guardianship; an amendment bill (equal guardianship) introduced 2016
  [106:5:2.4] Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 | adoption among Hindus
  [106:5:2.5] Family Courts Act 1984 | after the 59th Law Commission Report (1974); set up by the State Government with the High Court's concurrence
  [106:5:2.6] BNSS 2023 | maintenance: wives, children, indigent parents, divorced wives

=== NOTES 2:107 | Marriage – Forms, Rules of Endogamy and Exogamy, Changing Trends and Legislation
## SUB 0 | Marriage Laws – Acts, Ages, Registration, Personal Law
[107:0:0] # Acts – year and key point
[107:0:1] TABLE head: Act | Key point (exam answer words)
  [107:0:1.0] Special (Civil) Marriage Act 1872 (the Native Marriage Act) | first legislative provision for inter-caste (civil) marriage; monogamous civil marriage; ages 14 (girl), 18 (boy)
  [107:0:1.1] Indian Divorce Act 1869 + Christian Marriage Act 1872 | Christians; adultery, bigamy, conversion; mutual consent added 2001
  [107:0:1.2] Age of Consent Act 1891 | B.M. Malabari's effort; girls below 12 – an early measure, not a restraint law
  [107:0:1.3] Sharda (Sarda) Act 1929 = Child Marriage Restraint Act | first child marriage restraint law; curbed marriage of young girls; fixed minimum age 14 for girls, 18 for boys (raised to 15 in 1949, 18/21 in 1978)
  [107:0:1.4] Anand Marriage Act 1909 | Sikh; registration added 2012
  [107:0:1.5] Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1936 | re-enacted the 1865 Parsi law; registration compulsory
  [107:0:1.6] Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act 1939 | wife's grounds for divorce
  [107:0:1.7] Special Marriage Act 1954 | inter-religious civil marriage before a Marriage Officer; ages 21/18; registration compulsory; divorce Sec. 27
  [107:0:1.8] Hindu Marriage Act 1955 | first codified Hindu marriage law after Independence; Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs; STs only if notified; registration (Sec. 8) optional
  [107:0:1.9] Foreign Marriage Act 1969 | –
  [107:0:1.10] PCMA 2006 (Prohibition of Child Marriage Act) | ages 18 (women) / 21 (men); child marriage voidable at the child's option; punishes an adult male who marries a child (Sec. 9), whoever performs or abets it (Sec. 10), and parents/guardians who promote it or fail to stop it (Sec. 11)
  [107:0:1.11] Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019 | instant triple talaq void and illegal; up to 3 years' jail + fine; Parliament passed it 30 July 2019 (Rajya Sabha)
[107:0:2] - **Sarda Act statements (TSPSC 2023):** "known as Sharda Act" and "to curb child marriage" are correct; "fixed girls' age at **15**" is wrong (it was **14**) and "minimum three years' RI" is wrong (only simple imprisonment/fine).
[107:0:3] - **Registration compulsory:** under the **Special Marriage Act** (the marriage certificate is the registration); not under the HMA.
[107:0:4] - **Muslim law:** marriage (Nikah) is a **contract**, solemnised by a **Kazi** (Kazis Act 1880) through a *nikahnama*; **Mehr** = the sum fixed at marriage and **payable to the bride** (prompt or on divorce/death); **khula** = divorce at the wife's instance by mutual consent.
[107:0:5] - **Talaq-e-Hasan:** talaq once a month over **three months**; challenged in the SC after the 2017 triple-talaq verdict; **Talaq-e-Ahsan** = a single pronouncement + iddat.
[107:0:6] - **Sikh Anand Karaj** is solemnised in a **gurdwara**.
[107:0:7] # Goa and the Uniform Civil Code
[107:0:8] - **Goa**: long the **only State with a common civil code** – the **Portuguese Civil Code 1867**, brought into Goa in **1870**.
[107:0:9] - **Uttarakhand UCC** in force since **27 January 2025** – the first State to enforce a UCC after Independence; live-in registration mandatory.
[107:0:10] - 2026 (app notes): Amit Shah said a UCC will cover all **21 NDA States by 2029**; Assam, Gujarat, MP UCC Bills await assent.
[107:0:11] > Exam angle: "only State with a common civil code" = Goa in older papers; add Uttarakhand (2025) for current questions.
[107:0:12] ~~ Sources: Spectrum Modern India (src/indian-history/spectrum-modern-india.txt) l.9292-9301; Rocket Indian Society p.2 (Sharda Act first restraint law); NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.20; web: newsonair.gov.in (Uttarakhand UCC 27 Jan 2025); app notes 2:107 sub 5
## SUB 1 | Forms of Marriage – Monogamy, Polygamy, Levirate, Sororate
[107:1:0] # Forms by number of spouses
[107:1:1] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [107:1:1.0] Monogamy | one man – one woman (the most common form)
  [107:1:1.1] Polygamy | more than one spouse at a time: polygyny (one man, many wives) or polyandry (one woman, many husbands)
  [107:1:1.2] Sororal polygyny | a man marries several sisters
  [107:1:1.3] Fraternal (adelphic) polyandry | a woman's husbands are brothers (Toda, Khasa)
  [107:1:1.4] Group marriage | several men with several women
  [107:1:1.5] Serial monogamy | remarriage after death/divorce, one spouse at a time
[107:1:2] # Preferential widow/widower marriage
[107:1:3] TABLE head: Term | Telugu term in APPSC papers | Meaning
  [107:1:3.0] Levirate | Devara Nyayam ("divine justice") | a widow marries her deceased husband's (younger) brother (Gond, Munda)
  [107:1:3.1] Sororate | Bharya Bhagini Nyayam ("justice for spouses / wife's sister") | a widower marries his deceased wife's sister
[107:1:4] - **Levirate = husband's brother; Sororate = wife's sister** – both after the spouse's death.
[107:1:5] - **Toda (Nilgiris):** fraternal **polyandry → polygyny (polyandry with several wives) → monogamy** – the order asked by UPSC 1997.
[107:1:6] - Polyandry tends to arise where one man cannot support a family (extreme poverty).
[107:1:7] - **Legal position today:** polygamy and polygyny are prohibited for Hindus (HMA Sec. 11 – bigamous marriage void); monogamy prevails.
[107:1:8] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.19 (marriage terms); NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.19-20, p.43 (Toda, Khasa polyandry); OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 2 (src/society/onlyias-ncert-indian-society-02.txt) l.177-189; app notes 2:107 sub 0
## SUB 2 | Endogamy, Exogamy, Hypergamy and Incest Taboo
[107:2:0] # Rules of mate selection
[107:2:1] TABLE head: Rule | Meaning
  [107:2:1.0] Endogamy (Telugu *antar-vivaham*, "intermarriage" in translated papers) | marriage within one's own caste, tribe, religion – keeps caste boundaries
  [107:2:1.1] Exogamy (*bahir-vivaham*, "extramarriage") | marriage outside a group: sapinda exogamy, sagotra exogamy, village exogamy
  [107:2:1.2] Hypergamy = Anuloma | higher-caste man + lower-caste woman (woman marries up) – tolerated
  [107:2:1.3] Hypogamy = Pratiloma | lower-caste man + higher-caste woman (woman marries down) – condemned
[107:2:2] - **Ghurye**: endogamy is the **defining feature of caste**.
[107:2:3] - **North India**: caste endogamy + gotra exogamy + **village exogamy**; daughters marry into distant villages.
[107:2:4] - **Incest taboo**: a social prohibition that **forbids sexual contact between certain relatives** (parents–children, siblings) – the basis of exogamy.
[107:2:5] - **Irawati Karve** analysed sapinda and gotra.
[107:2:6] # Sapinda and prohibited degrees (HMA)
[107:2:7] - **Sec. 3(f)** sapinda: **3 generations** on the mother's side, **5** on the father's.
[107:2:8] - **Sec. 5(iv)** bars prohibited degrees; **Sec. 5(v)** bars **sapinda** marriage – both unless **custom** allows.
[107:2:9] - **Delhi High Court (Jan 2024)** upheld **Sec. 5(v)** (sapinda bar).
[107:2:10] - **⚠ Trap:** anuloma ≠ pratiloma – in both terms the direction is the **woman's** marriage relative to her own caste.
[107:2:11] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.18-19, p.51; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 1 (src/society/onlyias-ncert-indian-society-01.txt) l.1419-1425; OnlyIAS Part 2 l.205-218; NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.20, p.27; app notes 2:107 sub 3
[107:2:12] - **HMA Sec. 5 conditions:** no living spouse, sound mind, ages **21/18**, not within prohibited degrees, not sapindas – belonging to the **same sub-caste is not a condition**.
## SUB 3 | Hindu Marriage – Aims, Manu's Eight Forms, Ancient Customs
[107:3:0] # Definitions and aims
[107:3:1] - **Malinowski**: marriage is a **contract for the production and maintenance of children** ("a covenant to bear and nurture children").
[107:3:2] - **Lowie**: a relatively permanent bond between permissible mates; **Leach**: a **bundle of rights** (legitimating offspring, access to the spouse, affinal ties, domestic rights).
[107:3:3] - Hindu marriage = a **sacrament** (homa, panigrahana, saptapadi); Muslim marriage = a **contract**.
[107:3:4] - **Aims (K.M. Kapadia)** in descending order: **Dharma** (religious duty) → **Praja** (progeny) → **Rati** (pleasure).
[107:3:5] # Manu Smriti – 8 forms (4 approved, 4 disapproved)
[107:3:6] TABLE head: Form | Meaning | Status
  [107:3:6.0] Brahma | daughter given to a learned, virtuous groom; no dowry or bride price | approved; highest
  [107:3:6.1] Daiva | daughter given to a priest officiating at a sacrifice | approved
  [107:3:6.2] Arsha | after symbolic gifts (cow and bull) from the groom | approved
  [107:3:6.3] Prajapatya | duty, family welfare, procreation | approved
  [107:3:6.4] Gandharva | love, mutual consent (Shakuntala–Dushyanta) | disapproved but conditionally accepted
  [107:3:6.5] Asura | purchase of the bride – groom pays bride price | disapproved
  [107:3:6.6] Rakshasa | forcible abduction; linked with Kshatriyas, seen in the epics | disapproved
  [107:3:6.7] Paisacha | deceit, intoxication, no consent | most condemned
[107:3:7] # Other customary unions
[107:3:8] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [107:3:8.0] Niyoga | a wife cohabits with a designated man to beget a child when her husband is impotent or dead
  [107:3:8.1] Sambandham | consensual, informal union of Namboothiris and Nairs under Kerala's matrilineal system
[107:3:9] - **Later Vedic** changes: child marriage began, **Swayamvara** declined, widow remarriage discouraged, same-gotra marriage banned.
[107:3:10] - **Satyashodhak marriage** (started by **Savitribai Phule**): no dowry, no Brahmin priest.
[107:3:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.19-20; app notes 2:107 sub 1-2; general knowledge, not checked (Malinowski, Kapadia)
## SUB 4 | Divorce and Marriage Offences
[107:4:0] # Divorce
[107:4:1] - **Divorce** = the **legal dissolution of a marriage by a court**; **W.P. Scott**: "an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage relationship and allowing each partner the right to remarry". Living apart is only separation.
[107:4:2] - **Desertion** (husband leaving the family to fend for itself) = **"the poor man's divorce"**.
[107:4:3] - First divorce laws: **Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1865**, **Indian Divorce Act 1869** (Christians) – not "Parsi Act 1869".
[107:4:4] - **HMA Sec. 13** grounds: adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, unsoundness of mind, renunciation, not heard of for **7 years**; **13B** mutual consent; **Sec. 11** bigamous marriage void; **Sec. 12** voidable marriages.
[107:4:5] - **Irretrievable breakdown** is not an HMA ground; **May 2023 (Shilpa Sailesh)**: the SC can dissolve such a marriage under **Art. 142(1)** even if one party opposes.
[107:4:6] - **Muslim law:** 1939 Act grounds – no maintenance for **2 years**, imprisonment of 7+ years, cruelty; 2019 Act gives subsistence allowance and custody of minor children.
[107:4:7] # Offences (IPC → BNS)
[107:4:8] - **IPC Chapter XX (Sec. 493–498)** = **offences relating to marriage** = **BNS 81–84**; bigamy IPC **494** = **BNS 82**.
[107:4:9] - **Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill 2025** (app notes): cognizable, non-bailable; up to **7 years'** RI.
[107:4:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.19 (divorce and desertion rising); app notes 2:107 sub 6-7; general knowledge, not checked (Scott, Art. 142)
## SUB 5 | Landmark Cases and Changing Trends
[107:5:0] # Cases
[107:5:1] TABLE head: Case | Year | Ruling
  [107:5:1.0] Naveen Kohli | 2006 | urged irretrievable breakdown as a ground
  [107:5:1.1] Live-in case | 2010 | live-in relationship protected under Art. 21
  [107:5:1.2] Narendra v. K. Meena | 2016 | forcing the husband to separate from his parents = cruelty (divorce ground)
  [107:5:1.3] Shayara Bano | 2017 | instant triple talaq unconstitutional
  [107:5:1.4] Navtej Singh Johar | 6 Sep 2018 | 5-judge bench decriminalised consensual same-sex relations (Sec. 377)
  [107:5:1.5] Self-respect marriages | Aug 2023 | SC overruled a 2014 Madras HC ruling: advocates can solemnise marriages under HMA Sec. 7-A (Periyar; Tamil Nadu amendment 1967)
  [107:5:1.6] Supriyo | Oct 2023 | no same-sex marriage under the SMA; CJI Chandrachud in the minority
  [107:5:1.7] SC | Jun 2026 | dissolved a marriage of a couple separated 15 years (app notes)
  [107:5:1.8] Allahabad HC | 1 Jul 2026 | PCMA overrides the personal-law "puberty" rule for all religions (app notes)
[107:5:2] # Trends
[107:5:3] - Aim shifts from **dharma to companionship**; age at marriage rising; more divorce and desertion; **live-in** and **cohabitation** (unmarried partners sharing an intimate, committed daily life) gaining acceptance.
[107:5:4] - **Patricia Uberoi**: companionate marriage, serial monogamy.
[107:5:5] - **Inter-caste** marriages only about **5%**; **Dr Ambedkar Scheme**: Rs **2.5 lakh** to inter-caste couples; Ambedkar: intermarriage the real remedy for caste.
[107:5:6] - **Nepal**: **first South Asian** nation to register a same-sex marriage (2023).
[107:5:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.13, p.19, p.23, p.35; app notes 2:107 sub 8-9; general knowledge, not checked (Narendra 2016)
## SUB 6 | Child Marriage – Causes, Data, Campaigns
[107:6:0] - **Causes:** **poverty**, **low education of girls**, **social customs and traditions**, dowry, safety of girls, the old belief in pre-puberty marriage – "status symbol" is not a cause.
[107:6:1] - More prevalent in **lower castes, poorer classes** and **joint families**.
[107:6:2] - **International Day of the Girl Child**: 11 October; first observed **2012**, theme **"Ending Child Marriage"**.
[107:6:3] TABLE head: Data | Fact
  [107:6:3.0] NCRB 2021 (PCMA cases) | Karnataka 273, Tamil Nadu 169, Assam 155 – the top three
  [107:6:3.1] NCRB 2023 | 6,038 cases (about six times 1,002 of 2022); Assam nearly 90%
  [107:6:3.2] NFHS-6 | 20.1% of women aged 20–24 married before 18 (app notes)
[107:6:4] - **PCM (Amendment) Bill 2025** (app notes): women's age to **21**; **Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat**: cut child marriage **10% by 2026**, eliminate by **2030**; AP adolescent-education programme in **9,675 schools**.
[107:6:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.24-25; web: factly.in (NCRB 2021 state figures), assamtribune.com (NCRB 2023); app notes 2:107 sub 9
## SUB 7 | Tribal Ways of Acquiring a Mate
[107:7:0] - Ways: probation, **capture**, trial, **purchase** (bride price), **service**, **exchange**, mutual consent, intrusion.
[107:7:1] TABLE head: Way | Tribe / example
  [107:7:1.0] Capture | Naga, Ho, Bhil, Gond
  [107:7:1.1] Service (groom works at the bride's home) | Gonds
  [107:7:1.2] Exchange | Atta Satta (bride exchange) in Rajasthan
  [107:7:1.3] Purchase | parallels the Asura form
[107:7:2] # Ho tribe terms

  [107:7:3.1] Diku Andi | marriage by negotiation, borrowed from Hindus ("diku" = outsider)
  [107:7:3.2] Oportipi | marriage by capture
  [107:7:3.3] Raji-khushi | elopement by mutual consent
  [107:7:3.4] Anader | intrusion – the girl forces herself into the lover's home

=== NOTES 2:108 | Kinship – Descent, Lineage, Clan, Kinship Terminology; North-south Indian Kinship Contrast
## SUB 0 | Kinship – Meaning, Consanguineal, Affinal and Ritual Kin
[108:0:0] # Meaning
[108:0:1] - **Kinship**: a system of social relationships based on **blood (consanguineal) and marriage (affinal)** – the set of relationships among **consanguineous and marital relatives**.
[108:0:2] - **Radcliffe-Brown**: kinship = a system of **dynamic relations** between persons, regulated by **social usage**; a field of rights and obligations.
[108:0:3] - **Murdock**: a structured system of relationships binding individuals by complex interlocking ties.
[108:0:4] - Best short definition (UPSC 1994 key): kinship = **social identity expressing genealogical relationship**.
[108:0:5] - **Marriage creates kinship** (Westermarck, APPSC 2000 key): when two people marry they become kin to one another.
[108:0:6] # Types
[108:0:7] TABLE head: Type | Basis | Example
  [108:0:7.0] Consanguineal (blood) | birth / descent | parent–child, siblings, uncle–nephew; an adopted son is treated as consanguineous kin
  [108:0:7.1] Affinal ("relatives by marriage", affines; "matrimonial kinship") | marriage | husband–wife (ego's wife), son-in-law–father-in-law, brothers-in-law
  [108:0:7.2] Ritual / fictive | functional social relationship, not biology | godparenthood, dharam bhai/behen, rakhi ties
[108:0:8] - **Genetic traits** pass only through **blood relatives**, never through affines.
[108:0:9] - A father–son tie by birth is consanguineal, not fictive; husband–wife is the classic **non-consanguineous** pair.
[108:0:10] - **Inheritance** = transfer of property (immovable) from a dead person to heirs.
[108:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.25, p.31; Rocket Indian Society p.18, p.31; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society Part 2 l.175-176; app notes 2:108 sub 0; general knowledge, not checked (Westermarck, adopted son)
## SUB 1 | Kinship Usages and Terminology
[108:1:0] # Usages
[108:1:1] TABLE head: Usage | Meaning
  [108:1:1.0] Avoidance | restraint, e.g. daughter-in-law and father-in-law
  [108:1:1.1] Joking relationship | licensed teasing, e.g. brother-in-law – sister-in-law (a man and his wife's younger sister)
  [108:1:1.2] Teknonymy | referring to a person through a child ("father of Ramu")
  [108:1:1.3] Avunculate | special authority of the maternal uncle (matrilineal societies)
  [108:1:1.4] Amitate (Telugu translation "patriarchal relationship") | special respect/authority of the father's sister (patrilineal societies)
  [108:1:1.5] Couvade (*Kuhana prasuti*) | the husband simulates pregnancy / observes his wife's birth taboos – Khasi, Toda
  [108:1:1.6] Complementary filiation (Meyer Fortes) | in a patrilineal society, the ritual and social role of the mother's brother and mother's kin
[108:1:2] - **Match (UPSC 2002):** avoidance – kinship practice; joint family – kinship group; gotra – exogamy; sororate – marriage.
[108:1:3] # Terminology
[108:1:4] TABLE head: Basis | Types
  [108:1:4.0] Meaning | classificatory (one word for many kin: "uncle") vs descriptive (one kin: "father")
  [108:1:4.1] Use | terms of address vs terms of reference
[108:1:5] - **Hawaiian** system (fewest terms, all cousins = siblings) goes with **bilateral (cognatic)** descent.
[108:1:6] - **Kinship diagrams:** **circle (O) = female**, **triangle = male**, "=" = marriage.
[108:1:7] - **L.H. Morgan**: classificatory–descriptive distinction, *Systems of Consanguinity and Affinity* (**1871**); *Ancient Society* (1877): **savagery → barbarism → civilisation**.
[108:1:8] - **K.M. Kapadia** linked kinship terms to marriage and inheritance rules.
[108:1:9] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:108 sub 5-6, sub 11 (couvade Khasi, Toda); general knowledge, not checked (Fortes, Hawaiian, symbols, Ancient Society)
## SUB 2 | Descent, Residence and Descent Groups
[108:2:0] # Descent rules
[108:2:1] TABLE head: Rule | Meaning | Example
  [108:2:1.0] Patrilineal | through the father | most of North India; Kondhs, Santhals, Bhils
  [108:2:1.1] Matrilineal | through the mother | Khasi, Garo, Nair, Lakshadweep Muslims
  [108:2:1.2] Bilateral / cognatic | both sides equal | –
  [108:2:1.3] Double (bilineal) | movable via mother, immovable via father | –
  [108:2:1.4] Parallel / cross | women → daughters, men → sons / mother → son, father → daughter | –
[108:2:2] # Residence after marriage
[108:2:3] TABLE head: Term | Couple lives with
  [108:2:3.0] Patrilocal = virilocal | the husband's (groom's) parents
  [108:2:3.1] Matrilocal = uxorilocal | the wife's family
  [108:2:3.2] Avunculocal (Telugu *matula-sthanika*) | the groom's mother's brother
  [108:2:3.3] Neolocal | a new, separate home
  [108:2:3.4] Duolocal | each spouse in own natal home; husband visits at night – Lakshadweep matrilineal Muslims, old Nayars
  [108:2:3.5] Bilocal / ambilocal | either family, alternately
[108:2:4] # Descent groups
[108:2:5] TABLE head: Group | Definition
  [108:2:5.0] Lineage | unilineal group from a known ancestor; exogamous
  [108:2:5.1] Clan | believes in a common ancestor; link not demonstrated
  [108:2:5.2] Gotra | exogamous Hindu clan; common male ancestor; same-gotra bar from the Later Vedic period
  [108:2:5.3] Phratry | two or more related clans
  [108:2:5.4] Moiety | society divided into two halves
[108:2:6] - Order (small to large): **lineage → clan → phratry → moiety**.
[108:2:7] - **Corporate group** (tribal societies): a **durable, property-holding group based on kinship**.
[108:2:8] - **Sapinda**: kin within the prohibited degrees of blood relationship – not a large unilineal group.
[108:2:9] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.18; NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.9; web: scribd.com/document/475097194 (Lakshadweep matriliny: husband visits at night, duolocal); app notes 2:108 sub 2-4
## SUB 3 | Matrilineal Kinship – Nair Tharavad, Khasi
[108:3:0] - Matrilineal communities: **Nairs** (Kerala), **Khasis** and **Garos** (Meghalaya); "pro-matriarchal" pair asked: **Nairs and Khasis**.
[108:3:1] - **Tharavad (Nayar)**: a **matrilineal, matrilocal** joint family of a woman, her brothers and sisters, and her own and her sisters' **sons and daughters** (and daughters' children); husbands do not live in it – no husband–wife or father–child relation inside.
[108:3:2] - **Nayar marriage**: the husband had **no legal paternity** – children have no legal genitor/father in the tharavad (Gough's test case of marriage).
[108:3:3] - **Khasi**: matrilineal; women free; children go to the mother after divorce; clan exogamy, parallel cousins barred.
[108:3:4] - In matrilineal societies the **maternal uncle** holds authority (avunculate).
[108:3:5] - **⚠ Trap:** Namboodiris are patrilineal Brahmins (they joined Nair women only in **sambandham**); Coorgs are patrilineal.
[108:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.28, p.30; app notes 2:108 sub 8; general knowledge, not checked (Gough)
## SUB 4 | Degrees of Kinship
[108:4:0] TABLE head: Degree | Meaning | Number
  [108:4:0.0] Primary | directly related: parents, siblings, spouse, children | 8
  [108:4:0.1] Secondary | primary kin of primary kin (father's father, wife's brother, brother's wife, sister's husband) | 33
  [108:4:0.2] Tertiary | primary kin of secondary kin (father's brother's wife) | 151
[108:4:1] - **Uncle** is not a primary relative (he is secondary).
[108:4:2] - **Family scenario (APPSC 2025):** Krishna (son) – Jyothi (sister's daughter) = **consanguineous**; spouses and in-laws = affinal.
[108:4:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:108 sub 1
[108:4:4] - **Joint family** = several (two or more) generations living together; **nuclear family** = parents and unmarried children.
## SUB 5 | North–South Kinship Contrast (Karve)
[108:5:0] - **Irawati Karve**, *Kinship Organization in India* (**1953**): **4 zones – North, Central, South, East**; basis = language, caste, family organisation; "Mother of Indian Kinship Studies".
[108:5:1] TABLE head: North | South
  [108:5:1.0] caste endogamy, gotra and village exogamy; sasan/sapinda bars; four-gotra rule | cross-cousin marriage preferred; parallel cousins barred
  [108:5:1.1] brides go to higher-status families | marriage with the elder sister's daughter (Telugu menarikam), FZD or MBD
  [108:5:1.2] distinct terms for blood and affinal kin; by generation | terms by older/younger
  [108:5:1.3] bride breaks with the natal family | continuity with the natal family
[108:5:2] - **Cross-cousin** = child of the **mother's brother** or father's sister; **parallel cousin** = child of the father's brother or mother's sister.
[108:5:3] - Uncle–niece (elder sister's daughter) marriage is allowed among **Marathas of south Maharashtra and Vokkaligas of Karnataka** (Karve).
[108:5:4] - **Dumont** on the South: **immediate exchange**; kin clustered in a narrow area; **no sharp consanguine–affine line**; more freedom for women.
[108:5:5] - **Pauline Kolenda**: *Regional Variations in Hindu Kinship* (**1968**).
[108:5:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.26-31; Rocket Indian Society p.4; app notes 2:108 sub 7
## SUB 6 | Family Planning and Other Facts
[108:6:0] - **National Family Planning Programme (1952)**: India's, the first national programme in the world.
[108:6:1] - Family welfare in the DPSP: **Articles 39 and 42** (app notes).

=== NOTES 2:109 | Caste – Features, Theories of Origin, Varna-jati Distinction
## SUB 0 | Jajmani System and Village Service Relations
[109:0:0] - **Jajmani system** = a **socio-economic and ritual** arrangement in which one caste secures the services of another; everyone works for a family or group to which he is **hereditarily** linked – so it is at once economic, political and socio-cultural.
[109:0:1] - **Jajman** = the **landholding** patron caste; **kamin** = the castes rendering hereditary services; paid in kind (grain share) at harvest.
[109:0:2] - Features: **functional interdependence** of castes, **hereditary** ties, **inequality** of status between groups; critics (Beidelman) call it exploitative, but "feudalism" is not a defining feature.
[109:0:3] - Pre-independence rural inter-caste relations rested on **dominance and reciprocity** (patron dominance + exchange of services).
[109:0:4] - **William H. Wiser**, ***The Hindu Jajmani System*** (**1936**); with Charlotte Wiser *Behind Mud Walls*. (*India's Villages* – Srinivas ed.; *Caste in Modern India* – Srinivas; *Hindu Social Organization* – P.H. Prabhu.)
[109:0:5] - **⚠ Trap:** jajmani is a **caste-village** system; economic exchange **between tribes** is mainly **barter**.
[109:0:6] TABLE head: System | Region
  [109:0:6.0] Jajmani | North India

## SUB 1 | Theories of Origin and Scholars of Caste
[109:1:0] TABLE head: Theory | Proponent | Idea
  [109:1:0.0] Traditional / Divine | Purusha Sukta (Rig Veda 10.90) | varnas from head, arms, thighs, feet
  [109:1:0.1] Racial | Herbert Risley | racial difference; Aryans kept apart
  [109:1:0.2] Occupational | Nesfield | hereditary occupations → guilds → castes
  [109:1:0.3] Brahminical / Political | Abbé Dubois | a Brahmin device for purity
  [109:1:0.4] Cultural | S.C. Roy | commensality and marriage bars
[109:1:1] - **Abbé J.A. Dubois** (*Hindu Manners, Customs and Ceremonies*, 19th c.): caste **saved Hindu society from barbarism**; also wrote that a Hindu woman could go anywhere alone without fear of insult.
[109:1:2] - **J.C. Nesfield** is credited (APPSC key) with first using the word **"untouchable"** for these castes.
[109:1:3] - Early Vedic: no rigid varna; **Later Vedic**: four hereditary varnas crystallise; **post-Maurya/Gupta**: Manu Smriti, rigid caste.
[109:1:4] TABLE head: Scholar | Definition / idea
  [109:1:4.0] S.V. Ketkar | *History of Caste in India* (1909): membership by birth + bar on marrying outside
  [109:1:4.1] Risley | common name, claimed mythical ancestor, same hereditary calling; ranked castes in the 1901 Census; first to define caste scientifically
  [109:1:4.2] C. Bouglé | hereditary specialisation, hierarchy, repulsion
  [109:1:4.3] A.W. Green | ideally no mobility up or down
  [109:1:4.4] J.H. Hutton | caste developed through social and religious disabilities
  [109:1:4.5] Louis Dumont | *Homo Hierarchicus* (1966): pure vs impure
  [109:1:4.6] McKim Marriott | ranking by exchange of "coded substances" (food, water, services)
[109:1:5] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.5, p.15; NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.32; app notes 2:109 sub 1, 3, 4; general knowledge, not checked (Dubois quotations, Nesfield)
## SUB 2 | Varna and Jati; Features of Caste
[109:2:0] - "Caste" from **Portuguese casta** (race, breed).
[109:2:1] TABLE head: Varna | Jati
  [109:2:1.0] theoretical 4-fold scheme of the Vedas | real local groups; thousands of sub-castes
  [109:2:1.1] excludes "untouchables" | regional variations
  [109:2:1.2] almost no mobility | mobility possible, esp. middle castes
[109:2:2] - **Ghurye** (*Caste and Race in India*, **1932**), **six features**: segmental division; hierarchy; restrictions on feeding and social intercourse; civil and religious disabilities and privileges; **lack of free choice of occupation**; restrictions on marriage (endogamy).
[109:2:3] - Two dimensions: **vertical** (ranking) and **horizontal** (grouping).
[109:2:4] - Cultural traits: pollution by touch, untouchability, Sanskritic rituals, commensal taboos (not universal inter-caste commensality).
[109:2:5] - **1931 Census**: **4,147** castes; caste enumeration began with the **1871** Census.
[109:2:6] - **Telugu dependent castes:** the **Viramushtis** are bards/beggars dependent on the **Komatis (Vaishyas)**.
[109:2:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society G2 Part 1 p.32-34; NextGen Society G2 Part 3 p.33, p.36; app notes 2:109 sub 0, 2; general knowledge, not checked (Viramushti)
## SUB 3 | Caste Among Non-Hindus; Tribe–Caste Continuum
[109:3:0] - **Muslims**: **Ashraf** (foreign descent, upper-caste converts), **Ajlaf** (clean occupational groups), **Arzal** (lowest; converts from untouchable castes).
[109:3:1] - **Christians**: from St Thomas (52 AD); about 74% identify with lower castes. **Sikhs**: **Mazhabi Sikhs** = largest SC component.
[109:3:2] TABLE head: SC Order | Covers
  [109:3:2.0] 1950 | Hindus only
  [109:3:2.1] 1956 | Sikhs added
  [109:3:2.2] 1990 | Buddhists added
[109:3:3] - **F.G. Bailey**: tribe and caste as poles of a **continuum** (*Tribe, Caste and Nation*, 1960); **Surajit Sinha**: **secondary state formation** (chiefs take Raja titles); **N.K. Bose**: *The Hindu Method of Tribal Absorption* (1941); **Ghurye**: tribes as **"backward Hindus"**; **Nicholas Dirks, Susan Bayly**: caste as a colonial construct.
[109:3:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.16 (backward Hindus); app notes 2:109 sub 6-7

## SUB 3 | Ethnicity – Concept, Identity and Minority
[112:3:0] # Concept
[112:3:1] - **Ethnic group** = people who identify with each other on a common **language/dialect, history, society, culture or nation**; markers – language, religion, race, region, culture.
[112:3:2] - **Consensus approach:** groups **coexist** with separate identities; **conflict approach:** ethnic groups are **interest groups competing unequally** for power and resources (South Africa, Sri Lankan Tamils).
[112:3:3] - **Xenocentrism** = preferring another group's culture and **rejecting one's own**; opposite of **ethnocentrism**.
[112:3:4] # Views on ethnic identity
[112:3:5] TABLE head: View | Core idea | Scholars
  [112:3:5.0] Primordialist | Identity given by birth; "primordial attachments" | Clifford Geertz, Edward Shils
  [112:3:5.1] Instrumentalist | Elites mobilise identity for power | Paul Brass; Rajni Kothari (*Politics in India*); Christophe Jaffrelot (*India's Silent Revolution*)
  [112:3:5.2] Constructivist | Identity socially made, kept by boundaries | Fredrik Barth (*Ethnic Groups and Boundaries*); Benedict Anderson (*Imagined Communities*)
[112:3:6] # Minority
[112:3:7] TABLE head: Scholar | Contribution
  [112:3:7.0] T.K. Oommen | Separates nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship
  [112:3:7.1] Arnold Rose | Minority = group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language, regarded as different by itself and others
  [112:3:7.2] Giddens | Minority marked by disadvantage, group solidarity, isolation
[112:3:8] - **National minority:** non-dominant citizen group with its own ethnic, religious or linguistic identity; term from **European minority-rights law**.
[112:3:9] - Abroad: **Rohingya** – Sunni Muslim minority of **Rakhine State, Myanmar**; China recognises **55** minority groups, **Hui** = largest Muslim group (Uyghurs too); China's "ethnic unity and progress" law (Mar 2026); Sri Lanka Tamil-Muslim common platform (Jul 2026).
