=== NOTES 2:130 | Crimes Against Women – Trafficking, Honour Crimes, Acid Attacks; Criminal Law Amendments 2013 and 2018
## SUB 0 | Andhra Pradesh – Disha and Women-Safety Initiatives
[130:0:0] # AP Disha Bill (December 2019)
[130:0:1] - **Passed:** the AP Legislative Assembly passed the **AP Disha Bill** (AP Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2019) on **13 December 2019** – response to the **2019 Hyderabad veterinarian** rape-murder.
[130:0:2] - **Death** for rape and gang rape; verdict in **21 days** = **7 days investigation + 14 days trial** (vs CLA 2018: 2-month probe).
[130:0:3] - **Special court in every district** (not only the capital); forensic evidence; cyber-stalking penalties.
[130:0:4] - Needs **President's assent** (criminal law is in the **Concurrent List**); **never got assent – not in force**.
[130:0:5] # Initiatives → Purpose
[130:0:6] TABLE head: Initiative | Purpose
  [130:0:6.0] Disha App | SOS app; alerts police and shares location (APPSC G1 2022)
  [130:0:6.1] Disha police stations | 18 women's police stations
  [130:0:6.2] Abhayam | Chittoor police awareness campaign for women and children (Dec 2019, SP S. Senthil Kumar)
  [130:0:6.3] Abhay | Prakasam (Ongole) pilot, 4 Dec 2019: free pick-up and drop for stranded women, 9 pm-5 am
  [130:0:6.4] Shakti Teams | AP Police teams for prevention of crimes against women and children (164 teams); patrolling, awareness
  [130:0:6.5] Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi | Women-protection functionaries in village/ward secretariats
  [130:0:6.6] Trishul committees | State/district: zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women, zero road accidents (Sep 2026)
[130:0:7] > **Abhayam** = Chittoor campaign; **Abhay** = Ongole pick-up. **SOS** = Disha SOS app and also **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
[130:0:8] # AP data
[130:0:9] - Cases: **25,503** (2022) → **22,418** (2023, **11th** in India) → **19,952** (2024); further **4.4%** fall credited to **Shakti Teams**, Women's Safety Week rallies, **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
[130:0:10] - **Conviction rate** (crimes against women, 2021): AP only **5.6%** (pendency 86.7%) vs India 26.5%.
[130:0:11] - **District-wise** (2022): **Visakhapatnam** most rape cases (69), then NTR district (51).
[130:0:12] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:130 sub 9; web: inkl.com (The Hindu) "Chittoor police launch Abhayam"; web search results (Prakasam 'Abhay', 4 Dec 2019); CARE APPSC CA Mar 2026 p.5 (Shakti Teams)
## SUB 1 | Nirbhaya Case, Verma Committee and CLA 2013
[130:1:0] # Nirbhaya case (Delhi, December 2012) → outcomes
[130:1:1] - 1. **Justice J.S. Verma Committee** (report **January 2013**)
[130:1:2] - 2. **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013** = popularly the **"Nirbhaya Act"** (amended IPC, CrPC, Evidence Act)
[130:1:3] - 3. **Nirbhaya Fund** (2013) – non-lapsable corpus for **safety and security of women**
[130:1:4] - 4. **JJ Act 2015** – 16-18-year-olds may be tried as adults for **heinous crimes**
[130:1:5] - Not an outcome: the BNS. **Nirbhay Raho**: Panchayati Raj + MWCD + **NLSIU** under the Nirbhaya Fund.
[130:1:6] # Dates of the Nirbhaya Act
[130:1:7] TABLE head: Step | Date
  [130:1:7.0] Ordinance | 3 February 2013
  [130:1:7.1] President's assent | 2 April 2013
  [130:1:7.2] Notified / "came into existence" (most books) | 3 April 2013
  [130:1:7.3] Legally deemed in force | 3 February 2013 (s.1(2))
[130:1:8] # Verma Committee
[130:1:9] - Members: **J.S. Verma, Leila Seth, Gopal Subramanium**.
[130:1:10] - Recommended: **criminalise marital rape**, **no death penalty for rape**, police reforms, **age of consent kept at 16** → Parliament chose **18**.
[130:1:11] # CLA 2013 – new offences
[130:1:12] TABLE head: IPC 2013 | Offence | Now BNS
  [130:1:12.0] 326A | Acid attack (min 10 years-life) | 124(1)
  [130:1:12.1] 326B | Attempted acid attack (5-7 years) | 124(2)
  [130:1:12.2] 354A | Sexual harassment | 75
  [130:1:12.3] 354B | Disrobing | 76
  [130:1:12.4] 354C | Voyeurism | 77
  [130:1:12.5] 354D | Stalking | 78
  [130:1:12.6] 370 | Trafficking redefined | 143
  [130:1:12.7] 376D | Gang rape (revised) | 70
  [130:1:12.8] 376E | Death for repeat rapists | 71
[130:1:13] - Rape definition widened (objects, body parts, oral acts); **minimum 7 years**; age of consent **18**.
[130:1:14] - **Two-finger test** struck down in **Lillu v State (2013)**.
[130:1:15] - **Soumya case (Kerala):** Justice **Markandeya Katju** apologised to the Supreme Court (Jan 2017) for criticising its 2016 verdict in this **rape-and-murder** case.
[130:1:16] ~~ Sources: Spectrum Modern India p.799; web: latestlaws.com bare Act (assent 2 Apr 2013, deemed 3 Feb 2013); app notes 2:130 sub 3; general knowledge (376D, Soumya case), not checked
## SUB 2 | Institutions, IT Systems and Fast-track Courts
[130:2:0] TABLE head: Mechanism | Key fact | Funded by
  [130:2:0.0] Nirbhaya Fund | Set up 2013 for women's safety schemes | Government of India
  [130:2:0.1] One Stop Centres (Sakhi) | Since 2015; police, medical, legal help, shelter | Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.2] Women Helpline 181 | Universalised 2015; being integrated with ERSS-112 | Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.3] ERSS 112 | Single emergency number | Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.4] Safe City projects | CCTV and AI safety in 8 major cities | Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.5] Central Victim Compensation Fund | Supports State schemes (MHA, 2015) | One-time grant from Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.6] Mahila Police Volunteers | MWCD-MHA | Nirbhaya Fund
  [130:2:0.7] AHTUs | District task forces: trafficking intelligence, rescue, prosecution | MHA
[130:2:1] - **SHe-Box** = Sexual Harassment electronic Box; online POSH complaints go **directly to the Internal / Local Committee** with jurisdiction.
[130:2:2] - **Damini (Daamini):** helpline of the **UP State Road Transport Corporation** for women passengers (Dec 2019, Nirbhaya scheme).
[130:2:3] # IT systems → purpose
[130:2:4] TABLE head: System | Body | Purpose
  [130:2:4.0] Cri-MAC | Crime Multi-Agency Centre (MHA) | Real-time sharing of major crimes incl. human trafficking; inter-State coordination
  [130:2:4.1] NDSO | National Database on Sexual Offenders (NCRB, 2018) | Database of convicted sexual offenders; police-only
  [130:2:4.2] ITSSO | Investigation Tracking System for Sexual Offences | Tracks the 2-month investigation deadline
  [130:2:4.3] CCTNS | NCRB | Links police stations nationwide
  [130:2:4.4] Cyber Crime Portal + 1930 | I4C (MHA) | Report CSAM, non-consensual images, financial fraud
[130:2:5] # Fast-track and special courts
[130:2:6] - Fast-track courts are **administrative**, not created by CLA 2013; **FTSC scheme (2019)** follows CLA 2018; centrally sponsored, **Nirbhaya Fund**; **rape and POCSO** cases.
[130:2:7] - **POCSO:** a **Court of Session** designated Special Court in each district.
[130:2:8] - **Odisha** announced **45** fast-track courts for sexual crimes (**December 2019**).

## SUB 3 | CLA 2018, BNS 2023 and Victim Identity
[130:3:0] # CLA 2018
[130:3:1] - Context: **Kathua and Unnao** cases (2018); led to the FTSC scheme.
[130:3:2] - Minimum for rape: **7 → 10 years**.
[130:3:3] TABLE head: Victim | Punishment
  [130:3:3.0] Girl under 16 | Minimum 20 years
  [130:3:3.1] Girl under 12 | 20 years to life or death
  [130:3:3.2] Gang rape, girl under 12 | Life or death
[130:3:4] - Investigation **2 months** + trial 2 months + appeals 6 months; **no anticipatory bail** for rape of a girl under 16.
[130:3:5] # BNS 2023 (in force 1 July 2024)
[130:3:6] - **Gang-rape age raised 16 → 18**; **s.69**: intercourse by **deceitful means / false promise of marriage or job**; **s.103**: honour killing prosecuted as **murder**.
[130:3:7] - **Cheating** and dishonestly inducing delivery of property: **IPC 420** → now **BNS 318(4)**.
[130:3:8] # Identity of rape victims
[130:3:9] - **IPC 228A (now BNS 72):** victim's name cannot be published except by or under the written order of the **officer in charge of the police station / investigating police officer**, or with the victim's (next of kin's) written authorisation to a recognised welfare organisation.
[130:3:10] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:130 sub 4; general knowledge (IPC 420/BNS 318, 228A/BNS 72), not checked
## SUB 4 | Trafficking
[130:4:0] - **UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons 2016:** victims and traffickers often have the **same ethnic background** / place of origin (APPSC G1 2017).
[130:4:1] - **Palermo Protocol (2000):** prevents trafficking in persons, especially **women and children**; supplements **UNTOC**; ratified by India.
[130:4:2] TABLE head: Law / Bill | Provision
  [130:4:2.0] Art. 23(1) | Prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour
  [130:4:2.1] BNS s.143 | Defines trafficking; victim's consent immaterial
  [130:4:2.2] ITPA 1956 | Prostitution not a crime per se; punishes brothel-keeping, pimping, soliciting, living on earnings
  [130:4:2.3] Trafficking of Persons Bill 2018 | Passed Lok Sabha, lapsed
  [130:4:2.4] 2021 draft Bill | NIA as national investigating agency
[130:4:3] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:130 sub 6
## SUB 5 | Acid Attacks and Honour Crimes
[130:5:0] - **Laxmi v. Union of India (2013):** acid sold only against **photo ID** and stated purpose, with a register; no sale under 18; minimum compensation ₹3 lakh.
[130:5:1] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [130:5:1.0] Shakti Vahini v UOI (2018) | Khap interference in marriages of consenting adults illegal
  [130:5:1.1] Law Commission 242nd Report (2012) | Draft law against interference in marriages "in the name of honour"
  [130:5:1.2] Constitutional angle | Honour killings violate Arts 14, 15, 19, 21
  [130:5:1.3] Witness Protection Scheme 2018 | Enforced under Art. 141 till a law is made
[130:5:2] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:130 sub 5

  [130:6:0.0] Crimes against women, 2024 | 4,41,534 (down 1.5%)

  [130:6:0.2] Top State by number (2023) | Uttar Pradesh
  [130:6:0.3] Top State by rate (2023) | Telangana (124.9 per lakh women)

[130:6:2] - Cyber crimes against women rose **239%** (2017-22).
[130:6:3] - **Heads:** IPC/BNS (rape, dowry death, cruelty, kidnapping, assault on modesty) vs **SLL** (Dowry Prohibition Act, **Domestic Violence Act 2005**, ITPA, POCSO, **Indecent Representation of Women Act**).
[130:6:4] - **Causes:** patriarchy, **dowry (can grow into bride burning)**; under-reporting (stigma, **economic dependence**); women only **11.7%** of police.
[130:6:5] - **Firsts:** first all-women police station **Kozhikode, Kerala (1973)**; first women's court **West Bengal**.

## SUB 1 | 73rd/74th Amendments – Women in Local Bodies
[131:1:0] # Article 243D (panchayats) / 243T (municipalities)
[131:1:1] - **243D(2):** not less than **one-third of SC/ST seats** for SC/ST women (not 1/4, not 50%).
[131:1:2] - **243D(3):** not less than **one-third of total seats** in every Panchayat; rotated.
[131:1:3] - **243D(4):** not less than one-third of **Chairperson** offices (Pradhan, Pramukh, Adhyaksha).
[131:1:4] - **243D(5) sunset:** SC/ST reservation tied to **Art. 334** (to 2030); **women's reservation has no sunset**.
[131:1:5] - **243T** gives the same for municipalities; ST seats in municipalities = **243T(1)**. **BC reservation** is left to States (optional).
[131:1:6] - Tenure **5 years** from first meeting (**243E**); minimum age to contest **21** (243F, 243V). **73rd in force 24 April 1993**.
[131:1:7] # States at 50%
[131:1:8] - One-third is a **floor, not a ceiling**. **Bihar** first with **50% (2006)**; MP, Uttarakhand, HP followed.
[131:1:9] - **MoPR (April 2026): 21 States and 2 UTs** have 50% for women (about 20 when APPSC asked); **Haryana** moved to 50% in **2020**. Women are **49.75%** of 25 lakh+ elected panchayat representatives.
[131:1:10] - Earlier one-third-only States (APPSC flashcard): **UP, Haryana (till 2020), Goa, J&K**. **UP Panchayat Laws (Amendment) Act 1994:** **one-third** for women.
[131:1:11] - **Andhra Pradesh:** **50%** in panchayats and municipalities. AP 2026: 34% BC (rural) and 33.33% (urban) approved.
[131:1:12] - **Nagaland (2017):** violent protests against **33% reservation for women in urban local bodies** (claimed to violate Art. 371A).
[131:1:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity APPSC 24 p.5; web: static.pib.gov.in MoPR Highlights, National Panchayati Raj Day 24 Apr 2026; web search results (MoPR table: Haryana 2020); app notes 2:131 sub 1; general knowledge (Nagaland 2017), not checked
[131:1:14] - **Rotation:** reserved seats and chairpersons' offices rotate among constituencies (243D(3)-(4)); rotation of legislative women's seats after each delimitation is Art. 334A, not 243D.
## SUB 2 | Gender Indices

  [131:2:0.1] GDI | UNDP | Female/male HDI ratio (health, education, income)
  [131:2:0.2] GII | UNDP | Reproductive health (MMR, adolescent births), empowerment, labour (LFPR); 0-1, 1 = worst
  [131:2:0.3] WPS Index | Georgetown Institute + PRIO (Oslo) | Inclusion, justice, security; India 131st (2025/26)

## SUB 3 | 106th Amendment and the Women's Reservation Bill
[131:3:0] - **Constitution (106th Amendment) Act 2023 = Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam:** **one-third** of Lok Sabha, State Assembly and Delhi Assembly seats for women, incl. one-third of SC/ST seats; **no OBC sub-quota**; **not** Rajya Sabha or Councils.
[131:3:1] - Before it, Arts 330-334 had **no provision for women**, so a **constitutional amendment** was needed (party ticket quotas need none).
[131:3:2] TABLE head: Article | Content
  [131:3:2.0] 330A / 332A / 239AA(2)(ba) | Lok Sabha / State Assemblies / Delhi Assembly
  [131:3:2.1] 334A | Starts after the first Census after the Act + delimitation (2027 Census); 15 years, extendable; seats rotate after each delimitation
[131:3:3] - **Assent 28 September 2023**; brought into force **16 April 2026**; stated in force for **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from 17 April 2026 (app notes).
[131:3:4] # Bill history
[131:3:5] TABLE head: Year | Bill | Fate
  [131:3:5.0] 1996 | 81st Amendment Bill (Deve Gowda) | Lapsed
  [131:3:5.1] 2008 | 108th Bill (Rajya Sabha) | Referred to the Law and Justice Standing Committee (chair E.M. Sudarsana Natchiappan; report Dec 2009 signed by Jayanti Natarajan); passed RS 9 March 2010; lapsed 2014
  [131:3:5.2] 2023 | 128th Bill | Passed 21 Sept 2023 → 106th Amendment
  [131:3:5.3] 2026 | 131st Bill (Lok Sabha 550 → 850, delimitation on 2011 Census) | Defeated 17 April 2026: 298-230, short of 352 (Art. 368)
[131:3:6] - Women's groups demand removing the **Census-delimitation condition**.
[131:3:7] - **Arts 325-326** = equal franchise; **Arts 84/173** = women can contest.
[131:3:8] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.77; Praveen CA360 Apr 2026 p.10; PMF LENS Apr 2026 Part 1 p.9; web: prsindia.org Women's Reservation Bill 2008 brief (search results); app notes 2:131 subs 0, 2, 3
[131:3:9] - **Piloted by:** the Ministry of **Law and Justice** (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 33% of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats).
## SUB 4 | Women in Legislatures and As Voters

## SUB 5 | Grassroots Initiatives, Studies and Proxy Representation
[131:5:0] TABLE head: Initiative | Body / place | Purpose
  [131:5:0.0] Balika Panchayat | Kutch, Gujarat (June 2022) | India's first girls' panchayat
  [131:5:0.1] Mahila Sabha | e.g. Maharashtra | Women-only meeting before the Gram Sabha
  [131:5:0.2] Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan | MoPR | Trains women representatives
  [131:5:0.3] Nirbhay Raho – Nirbhay Chetna | MoPR | Sensitises male representatives
  [131:5:0.4] Model Women-Friendly GPs | MoPR | At least one per district
[131:5:1] - **Bokkasam Palem** (Srikalahasti, Tirupati): **1st** among women-friendly panchayats (2026).
[131:5:2] - **NCW** set up **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**. Reserving seats in **local bodies came first** among political empowerment measures.
[131:5:3] - **Reservation of chairperson posts brought a distinct change** in working – **Chattopadhyay-Duflo (2004)**, **West Bengal and Rajasthan**: women leaders invested more in **drinking water, roads**. It came from the 73rd Amendment, not a long rural demand.
[131:5:4] - **Proxy ("sarpanch-pati"):** male relative runs the office informally; does not legally replace her.
[131:5:5] - Dalit/tribal representatives: **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** and **PCR Act 1955**; **Therku Thittai** (Cuddalore, TN, 2020): Dalit woman president made to **sit on the floor**.

=== NOTES 2:132 | Women's Welfare Schemes – Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Mission Shakti, Pmmvy, Ujjwala
## SUB 0 | Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
[132:0:0] - **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**; launched **1 May 2016**, **Ballia (UP)**.
[132:0:1] - **Free LPG connections in women's names** for **BPL households** – **clean cooking fuel**, ends indoor smoke, improves health (APPSC 2017, 2025). Meant for **women**, not students or BCs.
[132:0:2] - **Ujjwala 2.0 (August 2021, Mahoba):** **free first refill + hotplate**; **migrants self-declare address**. Reach: over **10.5 crore** households (2026).
[132:0:3] - **Abroad:** **Ghana** (National Petroleum Authority) signed an MoU with **Indian Oil** (Jan 2020) to replicate the Ujjwala model.
[132:0:4] - **AP's own LPG scheme:** **Deepam** (1999) – LPG connections to women of BPL/DWCRA families; Deepam-2 (2024) – three free cylinders a year.
[132:0:5] > **Ujjawala (2007)** = anti-trafficking (now Shakti Sadan); **Ujjwala (2016)** = LPG – not an anti-trafficking scheme.
[132:0:6] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.77; Ramesh Singh Indian Economy 07 p.7; Spectrum Modern India p.820; web: business-standard.com (PTI, 22 Jan 2020) Ujjwala inspires Ghana; app notes 2:132 sub 4; general knowledge (Deepam), not checked
## SUB 1 | Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Gender Mainstreaming
[132:1:0] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [132:1:0.0] Launch | 22 January 2015, Panipat (Haryana)
  [132:1:0.1] Nodal ministry | Women and Child Development
  [132:1:0.2] Joint ministries | Health & Family Welfare + Education (then HRD)
  [132:1:0.3] Not involved | Social Justice & Empowerment (APPSC 2023)
  [132:1:0.4] Funding | 100% central
  [132:1:0.5] Coverage | 100 gender-critical districts (low CSR) → now all districts
  [132:1:0.6] Vertical | Sambal of Mission Shakti
[132:1:1] - **Objectives:** arrest the decline in **Child Sex Ratio**; prevent gender-biased sex-selective elimination (**female infanticide/foeticide**); ensure girls' survival, protection and **education** (female illiteracy); women's empowerment, gender equality – **not legal aid**, not child marriage or honour killing.
[132:1:2] - BBBP is a **PM flagship** with **Make in India** and **Digital India**; **Antyodaya Yojana is not**.
[132:1:3] # Gender mainstreaming
[132:1:4] - **Gender budgeting** = allocating resources to gender-sensitive programmes; Ministry of Finance mandated **Gender Budgeting Cells** in all Ministries in **2004-05** (Dec 2004); GBC Charter 2007; Gender Budget Statement since 2005-06.
[132:1:5] - **UN – five components of women's empowerment:** sense of self-worth; right to have and determine choices; right to **access** opportunities and resources; right to control their own lives; ability to influence social change (**"restrictions on access"** is not one).
[132:1:6] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:132 sub 2; OnlyIAS NCERT Indian Society 03 p.69; Rocket Indian Society p.10; web search results (MWCD Gender Budgeting Handbook: Dec 2004 instructions); general knowledge (UN components), not checked

  [132:3:1.2] Sambal | BBBP; Nari Adalat | Girl child; alternative redressal of petty cases

=== NOTES 2:135 | Reservation – Constitutional Basis, Indra Sawhney, Creamy Layer, Ews, Promotion
## SUB 0 | Backward Classes Commissions – Kalelkar, Mandal, Rohini
[135:0:0] # The three commissions (all under Article 340)
[135:0:1] TABLE head: Feature | First – Kaka Kalelkar | Second – B.P. Mandal | Justice G. Rohini
  [135:0:1.0] Set up | 29 January 1953 by the President (Nehru Govt); opened 18 March 1953 | Decided 1978 (Janata Govt of Morarji Desai), commission constituted 1979; through the Ministry of Home Affairs | October 2017, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
  [135:0:1.1] Report | 30 March 1955 | 1980 | 31 July 2023 to the President
  [135:0:1.2] Castes | 2,399 backward castes (837 "most backward") | 3,743 backward castes | ~3,000 Central-list OBC castes examined
  [135:0:1.3] Key point | First to use social and educational criteria; recommended a caste-based census and reservations | 11 indicators (4 social, 3 educational, 4 economic); OBCs = 52%; 27% quota | Sub-categorisation of OBCs into 3-4 sub-groups
  [135:0:1.4] Outcome | Not implemented (rejected 1961) | Implemented by the V.P. Singh (National Front) Govt, August 1990; 27% central posts from 1993 | Report not public
[135:0:2] - **First Backward Classes Commission** chairman = **Kaka Kalelkar** (D.B. = Dattatreya Balkrishna Kalelkar), 1953 – asked 7 times; distractors B.P. Mandal, B.R. Ambedkar, Jagjivan Ram.
[135:0:3] - **Second Backward Classes Commission** (report 1980) chairman = **B.P. Mandal** (**Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal**, an MP) – the "Mandal Commission"; set up by the **Janata** Government under **Morarji Desai** (not Janata Dal, not V.P. Singh, who only implemented it).
[135:0:4] - **Year set up:** NextGen and most keys say **1978** (the Janata Govt's decision, December 1978); Laxmikanth says "in 1979" (formal constitution). An exam offering only 1978 → **1978**.
[135:0:5] - **Mandal criteria** (examples): castes **considered socially backward by others**; castes **mainly dependent on manual labour**; castes where **women's work participation is at least 25% above the State average** – "stimulus stigma or impact" is **not** a criterion.
[135:0:6] - Mandal **mandate**: identify the socially and educationally backward; dealt with **reservation in government employment** → basis of the **27% OBC quota**.
[135:0:7] - **Rohini findings:** ~**97%** of benefits taken by **25%** of sub-castes; ~**1,000** communities with zero representation; 14 extensions. It examined **OBCs**, not STs.
[135:0:8] # Other bodies
[135:0:9] TABLE head: Body | Fact
  [135:0:9.0] Justice R.N. (Ram Nandan) Prasad Expert Committee | First laid down the creamy-layer criteria (report 1993, accepted → DoPT OM, September 1993)
  [135:0:9.1] M. Veerappa Moily Oversight Committee (2006) | OBC quota through expansion of seats (~54%, phased) so general seats did not shrink
  [135:0:9.2] NCBC | Statutory under the NCBC Act, 1993 (repealed 2018); now constitutional (Art. 338B); examines inclusion/exclusion requests; chairperson Niranjan Jyoti (appointed 2026)
  [135:0:9.3] Ranganath Misra Commission | 15% reservation for minorities
[135:0:10] > Trap: Mandal was set up through **Home Affairs**, Rohini through **Social Justice**; Kalelkar's report was never implemented, Mandal's was (1990).
[135:0:11] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.139; NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 p.36, p.41; Rocket Indian Society p.5-6, p.42, p.90; app notes 2:135 sub 3
## SUB 1 | Constitutional Amendments on Reservation
[135:1:0] TABLE head: Amendment | Content
  [135:1:0.0] 1st (1951) | Inserted Art. 15(4) (to undo Champakam Dorairajan) – first amendment on reservation
  [135:1:0.1] 76th (1994) | Tamil Nadu's 69% reservation law placed in the Ninth Schedule
  [135:1:0.2] 77th (1995) | Art. 16(4A) – reservation in promotion for SCs/STs (answer to Indra Sawhney)
  [135:1:0.3] 81st (2000) | Art. 16(4B) – unfilled backlog vacancies carried forward as a separate class (outside the 50% ceiling)
  [135:1:0.4] 82nd (2000) | Proviso to Art. 335 – relaxation of qualifying marks / lowering standards for SCs/STs in promotion
  [135:1:0.5] 85th (2001) | Consequential seniority in promotion for SC/ST government servants (from June 1995)
  [135:1:0.6] 89th (2003) | Split of the SC/ST Commission (Art. 338A NCST) – not relaxed marks
  [135:1:0.7] 93rd (2005) | Art. 15(5) – reservation in admission incl. private unaided institutions (minority institutions excluded); undid P.A. Inamdar; base of the 27% OBC quota in central educational institutions
  [135:1:0.8] 102nd (2018) | NCBC constitutional (Art. 338B), Art. 342A, 366(26C)
  [135:1:0.9] 103rd (2019) | 10% EWS: Arts. 15(6), 16(6); in force 14 January 2019
  [135:1:0.10] 105th (2021) | Restored the States' power to identify and list SEBCs; assent by President Ram Nath Kovind on 18 August 2021 – answer to Jaishri Patil
[135:1:1] # Bill numbers
[135:1:2] TABLE head: Amendment Act | Bill
  [135:1:2.0] 102nd | 123rd Bill (NCBC constitutional status)
  [135:1:2.1] 103rd | 124th Bill, 2019 (passed by the Lok Sabha; APPSC G1)
  [135:1:2.2] 105th | 127th Bill
[135:1:3] - **77th / 81st / 82nd** all concern reservation in **public employment** (promotion, backlog, relaxed marks); reservation in **admissions** comes from the **93rd** (Art. 15(5)).
[135:1:4] > Trap: relaxed marks in promotion = **82nd**, not 89th; promotion quota = **77th**, consequential seniority = **85th**; Bill number ≠ Act number (124th Bill → 103rd Act).
[135:1:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.135, p.139-140; app notes 2:135 sub 2
## SUB 2 | Constitutional Basis – Articles 15, 16, 335, 338, 340
[135:2:0] TABLE head: Article | Content | Added by
  [135:2:0.0] 15(4) | Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs, STs | 1st CAA, 1951
  [135:2:0.1] 15(5) | Reservation in admission incl. private aided/unaided; minority institutions excluded | 93rd CAA, 2005
  [135:2:0.2] 15(6) / 16(6) | EWS in education / posts | 103rd CAA, 2019
  [135:2:0.3] 16(4) | Reservation of posts for backward classes | Original Constitution
  [135:2:0.4] 16(4A) | Reservation in promotion for SCs/STs | 77th CAA, 1995
  [135:2:0.5] 16(4B) | Backlog vacancies as a separate class | 81st CAA, 2000
  [135:2:0.6] 335 proviso | Relaxed marks for SCs/STs in promotion | 82nd CAA, 2000
  [135:2:0.7] 338B | National Commission for Backward Classes | 102nd CAA, 2018
  [135:2:0.8] 342A | SEBC lists | 102nd CAA, 2018
  [135:2:0.9] 366(26C) | Defines SEBCs by reference to Art. 342A | 102nd CAA, 2018
  [135:2:0.10] 340 | President appoints a commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes and recommend remedies | Original
  [135:2:0.11] 341 / 342 | SC / ST lists | Original
[135:2:1] - **"Backward Classes" is NOT defined** in the Constitution (APPSC G2: the "defined" statement is the wrong one).
[135:2:2] - Correct term: **Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC)** – not "Socially and Economically".
[135:2:3] - **Art. 16(4)** backward classes are **mainly social**; they need not be both socially and educationally backward (Indra Sawhney) – identified mainly by **caste and social backwardness**.
[135:2:4] - **Art. 338(10)** (before 2018): references to SCs included such backward classes as the **President** specified – BC complaints went to the SC Commission.
[135:2:5] - For the CEI Act, OBCs are the classes "so determined by the **Central Government**".
[135:2:6] - **Protective discrimination** = e.g. **reservation of posts for STs**; SHG aid or minority scholarships are welfare schemes; one-region-only jobs would be plain discrimination.
[135:2:7] - **First reservation in India:** **Kolhapur State, 1902**, under **Shahu Maharaj** (for non-Brahmins and backward classes).
[135:2:8] > Number game: Art. 340 = commission (Kalelkar, Mandal, Rohini all under it); 338B = NCBC; 342A = SEBC list; NHRC is statutory, not constitutional.
[135:2:9] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.139-140; Rocket Indian Society p.3, p.5-6 (Kolhapur 1902); app notes 2:135 sub 0, 1
## SUB 3 | Landmark Cases – Indra Sawhney to Janhit Abhiyan
[135:3:0] # Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992, "Mandal case")
[135:3:1] - **Caste** can be the main criterion of backwardness (overruled Balaji on this); **upheld 27%** OBC quota.
[135:3:2] - Total reservation **not above 50%** except in **extraordinary cases**; applied **year by year**; **carry-forward** allowed within 50%.
[135:3:3] - **Creamy layer** excluded from OBCs (the concept originates here).
[135:3:4] - Reservation only at **initial appointment, not promotion** → answered by the **77th** Amendment.
[135:3:5] - Directed a **permanent statutory body** for OBC lists → **NCBC** (1993).
[135:3:6] TABLE head: Case | Year | Issue decided
  [135:3:6.0] State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan | 1951 | Caste-based quota struck down → 1st Amendment, Art. 15(4)
  [135:3:6.1] M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore | 1962 | Reservation generally within 50%; caste not the sole test
  [135:3:6.2] P.A. Inamdar | 2005 | No quota in private unaided institutions → undone by 93rd
  [135:3:6.3] M. Nagaraj | 2006 | Upheld 77th/81st/82nd/85th; promotion quota needs data on backwardness, inadequacy and efficiency
  [135:3:6.4] Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. UoI | 2008 | Upheld the 93rd Amendment and 27% OBC quota in central educational institutions (CEI Act); creamy layer applies to OBCs
  [135:3:6.5] Ram Singh v. UoI | 2015 | Jats struck out of the Central OBC list
  [135:3:6.6] Jarnail Singh | 2018 | Creamy layer can apply to SC/ST promotions
  [135:3:6.7] Jaishri Patil (Maratha case) | 5 May 2021 | Maratha SEBC quota struck down (breach of 50%); only Centre identifies SEBCs → reversed by 105th
  [135:3:6.8] Janhit Abhiyan | 7 Nov 2022 | EWS upheld
  [135:3:6.9] Union of India v. Rohith Nathan | 11 March 2026 | Parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer
[135:3:7] - **OBC quota timeline:** 27% central jobs from **1993**; **CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006** – 27% OBC seats, in force **2007**.
[135:3:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.139-140; Rocket Indian Society p.94; app notes 2:135 sub 4, 7
## SUB 4 | Creamy Layer and EWS Reservation
[135:4:0] # Creamy layer
[135:4:1] - **Status-based exclusions**: children of constitutional post-holders, **Class-I officers**, parents **both Class-II** officers, senior armed-forces officers, large landowners, high earners – **not all OBC children** are excluded.
[135:4:2] TABLE head: Year | Income limit (per annum)
  [135:4:2.0] 1993 | ₹1 lakh
  [135:4:2.1] 2004 | ₹2.5 lakh
  [135:4:2.2] 2008 | ₹4.5 lakh
  [135:4:2.3] 2013 | ₹6 lakh
  [135:4:2.4] 2017 | ₹8 lakh (still current)
[135:4:3] - **SC/ST creamy layer debate:** the Union Government opposed it (August 2026) – SC/ST status flows from **Arts. 341 and 342**.
[135:4:4] # EWS – 103rd Amendment (2019)
[135:4:5] - **Up to 10%** for economically weaker sections **not covered** by SC/ST/OBC quotas; **over and above** existing reservation (outside the 50% cap).
[135:4:6] - In jobs and education, including **private** institutions; **enabling, not mandatory** for States.
[135:4:7] - Criteria: family income **below ₹8 lakh**; agricultural land below **5 acres**; flat below **1,000 sq ft**.
[135:4:8] - **First State to implement** the 10% EWS quota: **Gujarat**, from **14 January 2019**.
[135:4:9] - **Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022):** upheld **3:2** by a **five-judge** bench; dissent: **CJI U.U. Lalit** and **Justice S. Ravindra Bhat**.
[135:4:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.140; https://www.outlookindia.com/national/india-news-gujarat-becomes-first-state-to-implement-10-per-cent-general-category-reservation-news-323522 (Gujarat, 14 Jan 2019); app notes 2:135 sub 5, 6
## SUB 5 | Andhra Pradesh – BC Groups and Muslim Quota
[135:5:0] TABLE head: Group | Who | Quota
  [135:5:0.0] BC-A | Aboriginal tribes, vimukta jatis, nomadic groups | 7%
  [135:5:0.1] BC-B | Vocational / occupational groups | 10%
  [135:5:0.2] BC-C | SC converts to Christianity | 1%
  [135:5:0.3] BC-D | Other classes | 7%
  [135:5:0.4] BC-E | Socially and educationally backward Muslims (2007 Act) | 4%
[135:5:1] - Combined BC-A to BC-E = **29%**.
[135:5:2] - **Muslim quota:** AP was the State that **proposed/ordered Muslim reservation**: **5%** (2004, 2005) struck down by the AP HC; **2007 Act – 4%** struck down by the AP HC in 2010, but the **Supreme Court's interim order** lets it continue pending a Constitution Bench.
[135:5:3] - **Sukhdev case** (AP HC): caste alone cannot be the basis → **112 classes** listed on poverty, residence and occupation.
[135:5:4] - **Anantharaman Commission**: **first AP BC Commission**, report **1970**; framed the **A-D grouping** and a **25%** quota. **Muralidhara Rao Commission**: took charge 27 Jan 1982; reviewed BC reservation and inclusion of minorities.
[135:5:5] - **Kapus**: Justice **Manjunatha Commission (2016)** → 2017 Bill giving **5% as BC-F**; never approved by the Centre.
[135:5:6] - **Local bodies:** **NTR** introduced a **20%** BC quota in **1984**; raised to 34%; cut to **24.15%** under GOs **176, 559, 560**. Supreme Court **triple test**: dedicated commission + local-body-wise proportion + total within **50%** (no NCBC approval needed).
[135:5:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:135 sub 8 (AP BC groups, Muslim quota, local-body quota)

=== NOTES 2:136 | Scheduled Tribes – Fra 2006, Fifth Schedule, Pesa, Tsp, Eklavya Schools
## SUB 0 | Forest Rights Act, 2006
[136:0:0] # The Act
[136:0:1] - Full name: **Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006** – aims at **redressal of the historical injustice** done to forest-dwelling STs and other traditional forest dwellers.
[136:0:2] - **Parliament passed it in December 2006**: Lok Sabha **15 Dec**, Rajya Sabha **18 Dec 2006** (passage complete); President's assent **29 Dec 2006**; in force **31 Dec 2007**; Rules **1 Jan 2008**.
[136:0:3] - **Nodal ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs** (not MoEFCC) (UPSC 2021). The Act **overrides** inconsistent laws.
[136:0:4] # Who decides
[136:0:5] - **Sec. 6(1): the Gram Sabha** is the authority to **initiate** the process of determining the nature and extent of individual or community forest rights (UPSC 2013) – not the Forest Department, Collector or Tahsildar.
[136:0:6] - Claims go up to the six-member **Sub-Divisional** and **District Level Committees**; the **District Level Committee's decision on the record of forest rights is final** (Sec. 6(6)).
[136:0:7] TABLE head: Category | Eligibility (cut-off 13 Dec 2005)
  [136:0:7.0] Forest-dwelling STs | Occupying forest land before the cut-off
  [136:0:7.1] Other Traditional Forest Dwellers | 3 generations (75 years) of residence
[136:0:8] - Ceiling **4 ha** per family; rights **heritable but not alienable**.
[136:0:9] TABLE head: Right | Type
  [136:0:9.0] Habitation, self-cultivation | Individual
  [136:0:9.1] Nistar, grazing, fishing | Community
  [136:0:9.2] Ownership of minor forest produce | Community
  [136:0:9.3] CFR management, PVTG habitat | Community
[136:0:10] # Bamboo, habitat, CWH
[136:0:11] - **Bamboo is a minor forest produce** under the FRA, and the FRA gives **ownership of MFP** to forest dwellers. The **Indian Forest (Amendment) Act, 2017** only removed bamboo grown **outside forests** from "tree" – it gave **no right to fell bamboo in forests** (UPSC 2019: 2 and 3 only). **No ownership of minerals.**
[136:0:12] - **Critical Wildlife Habitat** is defined **only in the FRA**: areas of national parks and sanctuaries to be **kept inviolate**, notified after an **open process of consultation**.
[136:0:13] - **Habitat rights** for PVTGs are decided under the FRA by the State machinery with the Ministry of **Tribal Affairs** guidelines – **not by MoEFCC**. **First habitat rights in India: the Baiga** (Baigachak, Dindori, Madhya Pradesh, 2015-16); later the **Bharia** (Patalkot, MP, 2022) and Kamar and Baiga (Chhattisgarh). UPSC 2018 key: statements 1 and 2.
[136:0:14] - **Protecting reserve forests:** allowing **limited rights** (e.g. grazing) to locals works better than keeping them out or giving unlimited rights or privatising.
[136:0:15] - **Niyamgiri (2013):** Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas rejected bauxite mining under the FRA.
[136:0:16] - **Implementation gaps:** focus on individual titles over **CFR**, Gram Sabhas bypassed, MFP transit permits, **weak MoTA capacity**. **MoEF circular (3 Aug 2009):** no diversion until FRA rights are settled and Gram Sabha consent obtained (no public-importance exception).
[136:0:17] - **Forest Conservation Rules 2022** dropped the consent clause (NCST vs MoEFCC); **Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023** exempts strategic projects within **100 km** of borders. **31 Aug 2026:** MoTA said the FRA has no provision for Gram Sabha consent for Stage-II clearance; MoTA sought CFR funds from **MoEFCC**.
[136:0:18] - Data (2025-26): 23.92 lakh individual + 1.22 lakh community titles; **AP: 2,26,651** titles.
[136:0:19] - **RFCTLARR 2013**: SIA **mandatory**; consent **80%** (private), **70%** (PPP); in Scheduled Areas acquisition is a last resort with consent of the **Gram Sabha / Panchayat / Autonomous Council**.
[136:0:20] ~~ Sources: PMF Environment (src/environment/pmf-environment-06.txt) p.84-87; https://ncst.nic.in/page/forest-rights-act-2006 (passage dates); https://www.downtoearth.org.in/news/governance/baiga-tribals-become-india-s-first-community-to-get-habitat-rights-52452; Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-03.txt) p.242; app notes 2:136 sub 3
## SUB 1 | Scheduled Tribe Identification and Committees
[136:1:0] - **Art. 366(25)** defines STs; **Art. 342(1)**: the **President**, after **consultation with the Governor**, notifies STs **State/UT-wise** by public notification; **Art. 342(2)**: later inclusion or exclusion **only by Parliament by law** (amending the Constitution (ST) Order, 1950).
[136:1:1]   - ST status is **State/UT-specific** – a tribe scheduled in one State does not get ST benefits everywhere; the President cannot alter the list later.
[136:1:2] - **Procedure:** State proposal → **Registrar General of India** (must agree) → NCST → Union Cabinet → Parliament.
[136:1:3] - ST status is **religiously neutral** (unlike SCs, limited to Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists).
[136:1:4] - **Criteria (Lokur Committee, 1965):** **primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness** – all five (not in the Constitution; no religion criterion).
[136:1:5] - **September 2022 Cabinet decision:** ST lists revised for **Himachal Pradesh (Hattee), Chhattisgarh, Karnataka (Betta-Kuruba), Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh** – not AP or Bihar.
[136:1:6] TABLE head: Body | Chair / year | Mandate
  [136:1:6.0] Dhebar Commission (Art. 339) | U.N. Dhebar, 1960-61 | Scheduled Areas and ST welfare
  [136:1:6.1] Lokur Committee | 1965 | 5 ST criteria
  [136:1:6.2] Bhuria Committee | Dilip Singh Bhuria | Basis for PESA
  [136:1:6.3] High-Level Committee | Virginius Xaxa, 2013 | Socio-economic, health, educational status of tribes
[136:1:7] - **Art. 244(1)** = Fifth Schedule; **Art. 338A** = NCST (89th CAA, 2003).
[136:1:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society Group 2 Part 1 (src/society/nextgen-society-group2-01.txt) p.42; OnlyIAS NCERT Polity Part 4 p.9 (Lokur); https://theprint.in/india/union-cabinet-approves-inclusion-of-tribes-of-five-states-in-st-category/1128927/; app notes 2:136 sub 0
## SUB 2 | Tribal Sub-Plan, ITDA and Institutions
[136:2:0] - **TSP**: Expert Committee **1972** (S.C. Dube); adopted in the **Fifth Plan (1974)**; now **DAPST**; funds at least **in proportion to the ST population**, over and above normal flows. Planning unit = **ITDP/ITDA**, with Panchayat members on its advisory committee – a decentralised, **bottom-up** approach (APPSC key). Grants: **Art. 275(1)** + SCA. Monitoring moved to MoTA in **Jan 2017**.
[136:2:1] - **SCP**: **1979** → SCSP → DAPSC. **AP SC/TSP Act 2013**: the **first State law** on planning, allocation and utilisation of the SC and Tribal Sub-Plans.
[136:2:2] - **TADP/ITDA objectives** (all correct): raise farm output with **improved seeds and fertilisers**, plant **fruit trees**, credit and marketing, freedom from **indebtedness**, wean tribals from **shifting cultivation**, and education, health and drinking water.
[136:2:3] TABLE head: Body | Year | Note
  [136:2:3.0] Ministry of Tribal Affairs | 1999 | Split from MoSJE
  [136:2:3.1] NCST | 89th CAA 2003; from 19 Feb 2004 | Civil-court powers
  [136:2:3.2] TRIFED | 1987 | Tribes India; MSP for MFP
  [136:2:3.3] NSTFDC | 2001 | STs up to double the poverty line
  [136:2:3.4] NSKFDC | 1997 | Implements NAMASTE
  [136:2:3.5] Girijan Cooperative Corporation (AP) | 1956 | MFP at fair prices, PDS depots, credit – tribal upliftment PSU
[136:2:4] - **AP data:** STs **27.39 lakh (5.53%)**, **34** communities; Scheduled Areas **10.15%**; tribal MMR and IMR **above** the State average. **APSCCFC**: self-employment, Jogin rehabilitation.
[136:2:5] - STs ≈ **9%** of the population but **over 50%** of the development-displaced.

## SUB 3 | Tribal Schemes – PVTGs, PM-JANMAN, Dharti Aaba, Van Dhan
[136:3:0] - **PVTGs: 75** in 18 States + 1 UT; criteria **pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness, stagnant/declining population**. **AP – 12** (Chenchu, Bondo Poroja, Dongria Khond, Konda Reddi, Kolam, Thoti, etc.).

  [136:3:1.1] Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan | Sept 2024; 63,000 villages; 17 ministries; nodal MoTA
  [136:3:1.2] Aadi Karmayogi Abhiyan | Under it Patalkot (Chhindwara, MP) got its first functional health centre (Sept 2025)
  [136:3:1.3] PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission | 2021-22, MoTA/TRIFED: buys MFP at MSP, value addition, GI tags; AP named a top-performing State (APPSC FSO key, not verified)

## SUB 4 | Education and SC/ST Empowerment – EMRS, Sports School, DACE
[136:4:0] - **Ekalavya (Eklavya) Model Residential Schools**: the model residential schools for **ST students** (also in AP); 1997-98; MoTA Central Sector via **NESTS**; modelled on **Navodaya**; block with **>50% ST and ≥20,000** tribals; target **740**; **Odisha** has the most.
[136:4:1] - **APTWR Sports School, Araku Valley** (2016): special sports school for tribal (SC/ST) children in AP.
[136:4:2] - **Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence (DACE):** free Civil Services coaching for **SC students** in 31 Central Universities; launched **22 April 2022** from **Banaras Hindu University** by the Social Justice Minister.
[136:4:3] - **SHRESHTA:** seats for meritorious **SC students** in top **private residential schools** (NETS by NTA).
[136:4:4] - Scholarships: SC Post-Matric **60:40**; National Overseas **20** awards for STs. **Stand-Up India** (5 April 2016): **greenfield** units, ₹10 lakh-₹1 crore, ≥1 SC/ST and 1 woman per branch. **VCF-SC**: 2014-15, ₹10 lakh-₹15 crore.

## SUB 5 | Tribal Problems, Approaches and Revolts
[136:5:0] - Colonial **moneylenders, traders and revenue farmers** → **indebtedness, land alienation**; the **common factor** of 19th-century tribal revolts = **complete disruption of the old agrarian order** of tribal communities (UPSC 2011).
[136:5:1] - **Diku** = outsider-exploiter (moneylender, trader, landlord, contractor); **Marang Buru** = Parasnath Hills revered by Santhals.
[136:5:2] TABLE head: Approach | Idea | Proponent
  [136:5:2.0] Isolation | Keep apart ("national park") | Early Verrier Elwin
  [136:5:2.1] Assimilation | "Backward Hindus", to be absorbed | G.S. Ghurye
  [136:5:2.2] Integration | Develop while keeping identity | Nehru
[136:5:3] - **Panchsheel** (Nehru's foreword to Elwin's **A Philosophy for NEFA**): develop along their **own genius**; respect land and forest rights; train tribals for own administration; avoid over-administration; judge by **quality of human character**, not money spent. **T.K. Oommen**: modern tribal movements seek autonomy, identity, control over resources.
[136:5:4] TABLE head: Revolt | Years | Leader / issue
  [136:5:4.0] Santhal Hul | 1855-56 | Sidhu and Kanhu; against dikus
  [136:5:4.1] Birsa's Ulgulan | 1899-1900 | Birsa Munda (Dharti Aaba); Abua Raj; against British land-grabbing and dikus → Chotanagpur Tenancy Act 1908
  [136:5:4.2] Rampa | 1922-24 | Alluri Sitarama Raju; forest curbs on podu
  [136:5:4.3] Srikakulam Girijan | 1967-70 | Vempatapu Satyanarayana, Adibhatla Kailasam
[136:5:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 (src/society/nextgen-society-group2-03.txt) p.40; app notes 2:136 sub 1, 2
## SUB 6 | PESA and AP Scheduled Area Laws
[136:6:0] - **PESA 1996** extends Part IX (Panchayats) to **Fifth Schedule** areas; ≥**50%** seats + all chairpersons STs. **10** PESA States; **Odisha** has only draft rules. AP: **2,038** PESA Gram Sabhas (AP PESA Rules 2011).

  [136:6:1.0] Regulation 1 of 1959 | Bars land transfer in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
  [136:6:1.1] Regulation 1 of 1970 ("1/70") | Presumption that land is tribal; bars transfer even between non-tribals
  [136:6:1.2] Samatha (1997) | Leases of tribal/government land to non-tribals or private mining companies void; mining only by State undertakings or tribal cooperatives
  [136:6:1.3] G.O. No. 3 (2000) | 100% Scheduled Area teacher posts for local STs; struck down 2020

  *B, D, C, A | D, B, C, A | B, C, D, A | A, B, D, C
  x: The correct sequence is Santhal Hul (1855–56), Birsa’s Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa rebellion (1922–24), and Srikakulam Girijan movement (1967–70).

=== NOTES 2:137 | Child Rights – Articles 21A, 24, 39(e)(f); Uncrc; Rte Act 2009
## SUB 0 | Universalisation of Education – NPE, SSA, RMSA, Samagra Shiksha
[137:0:0] # National Policy on Education
[137:0:1] - First NPE: **1968** (Kothari Commission); second NPE: **1986** (revised 1992).
[137:0:2] - **NPE 1986 vs 1968:** to universalisation of elementary education it **added the goal of minimum levels of learning (MLL)** – quality, not just enrolment.
[137:0:3] - NPE priority areas: **universal elementary education, adult literacy, education for women's equality** – "**compulsory nutrition education to all**" is **NOT** a priority area (APPSC G2, 2018).
[137:0:4] # Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001) → Samagra Shiksha (2018)
[137:0:5] - **Samagra Shiksha (2018)** merged **SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education**; funding **60:40**, **90:10** for North-Eastern and hill States; KGBVs up to **Class 12**.
[137:0:6] - **Component of SSA:** **NPEGEL** – National Programme for Education of Girls at Elementary Level; also **KGBV**.
[137:0:7] - **Wrong statements on SSA after RTE:** "GoI bears the **whole expense** of SSA" (it is shared); "it is **mandatory** on GoI to bring **early childhood care and education** under SSA" (ECCE below 6 is Art. 45, a DPSP, outside RTE).
[137:0:8] - **Interventions for universal elementary education:** mid-day meals, free books and uniforms, SSA, KGBV – **not free laptops** (code a, b, d, e).
[137:0:9] - **Tamil Nadu** pioneered the Mid-Day Meal; ICDS 1975.
[137:0:10] # RMSA (2009) and RUSA (2013)
[137:0:11] - **RMSA** = universal access to **secondary** education (Classes 9-10); **SEMIS** (Secondary Education Management Information System) = a **database system mapping schools** at national, State, district, block and village level.
[137:0:12] - **Not associated with RMSA:** "universal education for all children aged **6-16**" (6-14 is RTE); "access to quality secondary education is a **constitutional commitment**" (only 6-14 is, under Art. 21A).
[137:0:13] - **RUSA** (Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan) = funding of State **higher** education institutions; the wrong statement: "it is recommended by the National Education Commission".
[137:0:14] - Teacher education is regulated by the **NCTE** (National Council for Teacher Education).
[137:0:15] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:137 sub 3; general knowledge, not checked (RMSA, RUSA, SEMIS, NPEGEL details)
## SUB 1 | RTE Act, 2009 – Provisions
[137:1:0] - Full name: **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009**; gives effect to **Art. 21A**; free and compulsory **elementary** education for **6–14** years (Classes 1–8); in force **1 April 2010** – the Art. 51A(k) duty became a statutory right then.
[137:1:1] TABLE head: Section | Provision
  [137:1:1.0] 3 | Age 6–14; neighbourhood school; children with disabilities: free education 6 to 18 years
  [137:1:1.1] 12(1)(c) | Unaided private schools (excluding minority) reserve 25% entry-level seats for weaker and disadvantaged groups; State reimburses
  [137:1:1.2] 21 | School Management Committees; three-fourths members parents/guardians
  [137:1:1.3] 29(2)(f) | Medium of instruction, as far as practicable, the child's mother tongue
  [137:1:1.4] 38 | Rules by the appropriate Government (e.g. AP RTE Rules, 2010, framed under the Act)
[137:1:2] - **Pupil-teacher ratio**: **30:1** primary; **35:1** upper primary. **Teacher qualifications**: the **NCTE** (not a State council).
[137:1:3] - No **screening**, no **capitation fee**; out-of-school child admitted to an **age-appropriate class**.
[137:1:4] - Monitoring and grievance redressal: **NCPCR and SCPCRs**.
[137:1:5] - **No-detention:** original Act – none till Class 8; **RTE (Amendment) Act 2019** – regular exams in Classes 5 and 8, a child failing the re-exam can be held back.
[137:1:6] - **Not features of RTE:** early childhood care below 6 (Art. 45); pre-school and secondary education; **Centre bearing all funds** (shared); minority schools under the 25% quota.
[137:1:7] - **Education is in the Concurrent List** (42nd Amendment) → a State law **repugnant** to the RTE Act is **void to the extent of repugnancy** (Art. 254).
[137:1:8] TABLE head: Case | Issue decided
  [137:1:8.0] Unni Krishnan v. State of AP (1993) | Children below 14 have a fundamental right to free education under Art. 21; arose from Andhra Pradesh
  [137:1:8.1] Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan (2012) | Upheld the 25% quota; not for unaided minority schools
  [137:1:8.2] Pramati Educational Trust (2014) | RTE Act not applicable to minority schools
  [137:1:8.3] Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. UoI (2011) | Child trafficking, children in circuses
[137:1:9] - **January 2026**: SC reaffirmed Sec. 12(1)(c); States to frame admission rules under **Sec. 38**. **4 Sep 2026**: SC called quality elementary teacher education vital to **Art. 21A**.
[137:1:10] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.176; app notes 2:137 sub 1, 2
## SUB 2 | Constitutional Provisions for Children
[137:2:0] TABLE head: Article | Content | Origin / Amendment
  [137:2:0.0] 15(3) | Special provisions for women and children | Original
  [137:2:0.1] 21A | Free and compulsory education, 6–14 years (Fundamental Right) | 86th CAA, 2002
  [137:2:0.2] 23 | Ban on traffic in human beings and forced labour | Original
  [137:2:0.3] 24 | No child below 14 in factories, mines or hazardous employment (Part III) | Original
  [137:2:0.4] 39(e) | Tender age of children not abused; not forced by economic necessity into unsuited avocations | Original
  [137:2:0.5] 39(f) | Develop healthily in freedom and dignity | Reworded by 42nd CAA, 1976
  [137:2:0.6] 45 | Early childhood care and education till 6 | Substituted by 86th
  [137:2:0.7] 51A(k) | Parent/guardian's duty to give opportunities for education to a child 6–14 | Added by 86th
[137:2:1] - **86th Amendment, 2002** – three changes: inserted **Art. 21A**, rewrote **Art. 45**, added **Art. 51A(k)**; the **first** amendment to make education a **Fundamental Right** (distractors: 82nd, 85th, 93rd, 103rd).
[137:2:2] - Other "education" Articles are distractors: 44 = Uniform Civil Code, 39A = legal aid, 12 = definition of State.
[137:2:3] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt) p.154 (Art. 24), p.176 (86th Amendment), p.191 (51A(k)); app notes 2:137 sub 0
## SUB 3 | Child Rights – UNCRC, Days, NCPCR, Helplines
[137:3:0] TABLE head: Fact | Detail
  [137:3:0.0] UNCRC adopted | UNGA, 20 November 1989; 54 articles
  [137:3:0.1] India | Acceded 11 December 1992
  [137:3:0.2] Optional Protocols 2000 | India ratified 2005; not a party to the 2011 communications protocol
[137:3:1] - **Four rights:** survival, development, protection, **participation**. **Core principles:** non-discrimination, best interests, life/survival/development, views of the child (not free secondary education).
[137:3:2] TABLE head: Day | Date
  [137:3:2.0] Universal Children's Day | 20 November
  [137:3:2.1] India's Children's Day | 14 November (Nehru's birthday)
[137:3:3] - **Kailash Satyarthi**: founder of **Bachpan Bachao Andolan** (1980); **Nobel Peace Prize 2014** (with Malala). Shantha Sinha = first NCPCR chairperson.
[137:3:4] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [137:3:4.0] NCPCR | CPCR Act, 2005; set up 2007; Chairperson + 6 members (≥2 women); civil-court powers; monitors JJ, POCSO, RTE
  [137:3:4.1] e-Baal Nidan | NCPCR portal (2015; updated Sept 2022) for online complaints on child-rights violations
  [137:3:4.2] CHILDLINE 1098 | 24×7 helpline for all children in need of care and protection; integrated with ERSS-112
  [137:3:4.3] CARINGS / TrackChild / Khoya-Paya / Poshan Tracker | Adoption (CARA) / missing children (Mission Vatsalya) / citizens report missing children / Anganwadi tracking 0–6
[137:3:5] - **AP SCPCR**: directed admission of migrant and fisherfolk children (Kolleru); **Operation Muskaan** (Feb 2026) rescued over 1,200 children.
[137:3:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 (src/society/nextgen-society-group2-03.txt) p.12; app notes 2:137 sub 4, 5, 8
## SUB 4 | POCSO, Juvenile Justice and Adoption
[137:4:0] - **POCSO Act, 2012**: in force **14 November 2012**; child = **below 18**; **gender-neutral**. **Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, April 2018**: death penalty possible for rape of a girl **below 12**. **POCSO (Amendment) Act 2019**: death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
[137:4:1] - **JJ Act, 2015** (first JJ law **1986**): **16–18** accused of heinous offences → **Juvenile Justice Board** makes a preliminary assessment; **Child Welfare Committees** handle children in need of care and protection; **2021 amendment**: **District Magistrate** issues adoption orders.
[137:4:2] TABLE head: Law / body | Fact
  [137:4:2.0] CARA | Statutory under the JJ Act 2015
  [137:4:2.1] Adoption Regulations 2022 | Surrendered child: 2-month reconsideration period
  [137:4:2.2] HAMA 1956 | Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs (not Muslims)
  [137:4:2.3] JJ Act route | Open to all religions
[137:4:3] - **DPDP Act 2023**: child = below 18; **verifiable parental consent**.
[137:4:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:137 sub 6
## SUB 5 | Child Policy, Child Labour and Indicators
[137:5:0] - **National Policy for Children**: first **1974**; **NPC 2013**, child = **below 18**; priority areas: survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; **participation**. **National Plan of Action for Children 2016** operationalises NPC 2013. **Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat**: 100-day campaign from Dec 2025.
[137:5:1] - **Children (Pledging of Labour) Act, 1933** = first child labour law; **Child Labour (P&R) Act, 1986** = key law (below 14 in hazardous work).
[137:5:2] - Age thresholds: **POCSO below 18 | child labour below 14 | RTE 6–14**.
[137:5:3] TABLE head: Indicator | Figure
  [137:5:3.0] Child sex ratio (0–6), Census 2011 | 914 provisional (final 918); 2001: 927
  [137:5:3.1] Overall sex ratio | Census 2011 943; NFHS-5 1,020
  [137:5:3.2] NFHS-5 | IMR 35.2; U5MR 41.9; TFR 2.0
  [137:5:3.3] Child labour (5–14), Census 2011 | 4.35 million main workers

=== NOTES 2:138 | Juvenile Justice Act 2015, Pocso Act 2012, Child Labour Amendment 2016
## SUB 0 | Child Labour – Article 24 and the 1986 Act as Amended in 2016
[138:0:0] # Constitution and age limits
[138:0:1] TABLE head: Provision | Content
  [138:0:1.0] Article 24 | No child below 14 years to be employed in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment (Right against Exploitation) – the Article on child labour (not Arts. 23, 26 or 29)
  [138:0:1.1] Article 21A | Free and compulsory education, 6–14 years (RTE Act, 2009)
  [138:0:1.2] Article 39(e) | Tender age of children not abused
  [138:0:1.3] Article 39(f) | Children protected against exploitation and against moral and material abandonment
  [138:0:1.4] Factories Act, 1948 | No child below 14 in a factory
  [138:0:1.5] Mines Act, 1952 | No person below 18 in a mine (not 16)
[138:0:2] - **National Policy for Children, 2013**: every person **below 18** is a child; best interests first. The **Draft National Policy on Child Protection** asks for a **zero-tolerance code of conduct** in all organisations.
[138:0:3] # Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 and the 2016 Amendment
[138:0:4] - Enacted **1986** (in force **23 December 1986**) – the first comprehensive child labour law; child = a person who has not completed **14 years**. Followed the **Gurupadaswamy Committee (1979)**, Ministry of Labour: poverty the root cause; **dual approach** – ban hazardous work, regulate the rest → 1986 Act and **National Policy on Child Labour, 1987**.
[138:0:5] - **2016 Amendment** (in force **1 September 2016**) renamed it the **Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act**.
[138:0:6] TABLE head: Feature | 1986 Act | 2016 Amendment
  [138:0:6.0] Below 14 | Banned in 18 occupations and 65 processes; rest regulated | Banned in all occupations and processes (linked to RTE age)
  [138:0:6.1] 14–18 | — | New "adolescent" – banned in hazardous occupations only (mines, inflammable substances/explosives, Factories Act hazardous processes; earlier list had 83 entries)
  [138:0:6.2] Exceptions | — | Child helping the family enterprise after school hours; child artist in audio-visual entertainment (not circus)
  [138:0:6.3] Penalty | 3 months–1 year and/or fine ₹10,000–20,000 | Cognizable; 6 months–2 years and/or fine ₹20,000–50,000
[138:0:7] - **Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund** set up; enforcement through the **District Magistrate**.
[138:0:8] - **Penalty PYQ (APPSC):** the key is "**2 years imprisonment and fine up to ₹20,000**"; strictly the 2016 law gives 6 months–2 years and/or ₹20,000–50,000.
[138:0:9] - **Bonded labour** = work without freedom to leave, against a debt – e.g. a **child in a brick kiln not allowed to leave** (not unpaid help in a family shop or occasional work). **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**; debt bondage can run across generations.
[138:0:10] > Exam angle: Art. 24 = below 14; Act year = 1986; "adolescent" exists only since 2016.
[138:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society - Group 2 Prelims Part 1 p.70-74; NextGen Society Part 3 p.32; Rocket Indian Society p.88, p.101; NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams (Art. 24)
## SUB 1 | Child Labour – Magnitude, Enforcement, ILO Conventions and Cases
[138:1:0] # Magnitude
[138:1:1] - **Census 2011 (5–14 years)**: about **10.1 million** child workers (incl. marginal; **4.35 million main workers**) – about **5.6 million boys and 4.5 million girls (≈55:45)**; most in rural areas, rising in urban areas.
[138:1:2] - **Uttar Pradesh** had the largest number (about **21.8 lakh**, **one-fifth**), followed by Bihar, Rajasthan, MP, Maharashtra. India has the **largest number** of child labourers in the world.
[138:1:3] - Causes: **poverty**, demand for cheap labour, family breakdown, illiteracy, debt bondage, migration, weak enforcement.
[138:1:4] # Enforcement
[138:1:5] TABLE head: Mechanism | Fact
  [138:1:5.0] PENCIL (2017) | Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour; Ministry of Labour and Employment; for enforcing the amended Child and Adolescent Labour Act; inter-agency tracking of child labour cases; components: Child Tracking System, Complaint Corner, State Government, NCLP, Convergence (not a National Adoption Registry). Wrong options: SPARC, SRIJAN, YUKTI
  [138:1:5.1] NCLP (1988) | National Child Labour Project, Ministry of Labour and Employment (not Social Justice); withdraws children from labour; Special Training Centres for 9–14: bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal, stipend
  [138:1:5.2] Operation Smile / Operation Muskaan | MHA campaign-mode drives to trace, rescue and rehabilitate missing children (2015)
  [138:1:5.3] CHILDLINE 1098 | Integrated with ERSS-112
[138:1:6] - Trafficking: widened by the **Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013** (sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour, organ removal) – now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.
[138:1:7] # ILO conventions and cases
[138:1:8] TABLE head: ILO Convention | Subject | India
  [138:1:8.0] 138 (1973) | Minimum age for admission to employment | Ratified 13 June 2017
  [138:1:8.1] 182 (1999) | Worst forms of child labour | Ratified 13 June 2017
[138:1:9] - Both relate to **child labour** (UPSC 2018) and are among the **eight fundamental** ILO conventions. **World Day Against Child Labour: 12 June**.
[138:1:10] TABLE head: Case | Ruling
  [138:1:10.0] PUDR v. UoI (1982) | Child labour in construction violates Fundamental Rights
  [138:1:10.1] M.C. Mehta v. State of TN (1996) | Sivakasi; ban in hazardous industries; employer deposits ₹20,000 per child in a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund
  [138:1:10.2] Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011) | Trafficking, child begging, circus children; oversight of child care institutions
  [138:1:10.3] Independent Thought (2017) | Marital-rape exception (Sec. 375 IPC) struck down for wives below 18
[138:1:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society - Group 2 Prelims Part 1 p.71-74; Rocket Indian Society p.79, p.84, p.96; ILO conventions (UPSC 2018 key)
## SUB 2 | Juvenile Justice Act 2015 and Earlier Juvenile Laws
[138:2:0] # Earlier laws
[138:2:1] TABLE head: Law | Note
  [138:2:1.0] Children Act 1960 | For Union Territories
  [138:2:1.1] Juvenile Justice Act 1986 | First uniform juvenile law; juvenile = boys 16, girls 18
  [138:2:1.2] JJ (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2000 | Uniform age 18; homes: Observation Homes, Special Homes, Children's Homes, Shelter Homes – a "Protective Home" is not one of them (that is under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act)
  [138:2:1.3] JJ Act 2015 | In force 15 January 2016; response to the Delhi gang rape case (2012)
[138:2:2] # Key features of the 2015 Act
[138:2:3] - Replaced "**juvenile**" with "**child**" / "child in conflict with law"; two categories – children **in conflict with law** and children **in need of care and protection**.
[138:2:4] - A **delinquent** = a **minor** (below 18) who commits an offence – a "juvenile in conflict with law".
[138:2:5] - **Heinous offence** = minimum punishment **7 years or more**. A child of **16–18** accused of a heinous offence: **JJB preliminary assessment** (not a finding of guilt) → may transfer to the **Children's Court** (a **Sessions Court**) to be tried as an adult.
[138:2:6] - **CARA (Central Adoption Resource Authority)** given **statutory** status – the **nodal body for adoption**, under the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**; regulates **in-country and inter-country adoption**.
[138:2:7] - **Compulsory registration** of all **Child Care Institutions**; **working children** = children in need of care and protection.
[138:2:8] TABLE head: Body | Deals with / composition
  [138:2:8.0] Juvenile Justice Board | Children in conflict with law; Principal Magistrate + 2 social workers, at least one a woman
  [138:2:8.1] Child Welfare Committee | Children in need of care and protection; Chairperson + 4 members
  [138:2:8.2] Children's Court | Transferred 16–18 heinous cases; a Sessions Court
[138:2:9] - Every district has a JJB and a CWC. Juvenile delinquents are dealt with by **juvenile courts / Juvenile Justice Boards**, which put the **well-being and best interests of the child** first – child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice (not punishment, humiliation or precedent).
[138:2:10] - **2021 Amendment** (in force **1 September 2022**): **District Magistrate** (and ADM) = focal point; DMs issue **adoption orders** instead of courts.
[138:2:11] - **Private Member's Bill (Dec 2025)**: lower the heinous-offence age threshold from **16 to 14**.
[138:2:12] - **AP**: follows the JJ Act 2015 + **Probation of Offenders Act, 1958**.
[138:2:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society - Group 2 Prelims Part 1 p.72, p.74; Rocket Indian Society p.88, p.101; Rocket Indian Society p.7, p.11
## SUB 3 | POCSO Act 2012
[138:3:0] # Basics
[138:3:1] - **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012** (not "social offences") – addresses **child sexual abuse**; drafted by **MWCD**.
[138:3:2] - In force **14 November 2012** (Children's Day) – the year to remember is **2012**.
[138:3:3] - Child = **below 18**; gender-neutral; consent below 18 **legally irrelevant**. After the **BNS** (from **1 July 2024**) POCSO continues as a **separate special law**.
[138:3:4] # Offences and procedure
[138:3:5] - Offences: penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, their **aggravated** forms (by a person in **trust or authority**), sexual harassment, child pornography. **Child marriage is not** a POCSO offence.
[138:3:6] TABLE head: Section | Provision
  [138:3:6.0] 19 | Mandatory reporting; failure – up to 6 months and/or fine
  [138:3:6.1] 22 | False complaints punishable (except good faith)
  [138:3:6.2] 29–30 | Presumption – burden of proof on the accused
[138:3:7] - Child-friendly procedure: statement at the child's residence by a **woman officer**, not in uniform; **no child kept at the police station at night**; **Special Courts**, **in-camera** trial; investigation in **2 months**, trial in **1 year**. Monitored by NCPCR/SCPCRs; **POCSO e-Box (2016, NCPCR)** – confidential online reporting.
[138:3:8] # Amendments
[138:3:9] TABLE head: Year | Change
  [138:3:9.0] Ordinance, 21 April 2018 | Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance – harsher punishment (up to death) for rape of girls below 12; the POCSO amendment cleared by the Union Cabinet in 2018–19
  [138:3:9.1] 2019 Amendment (16 Aug 2019) | Penetrative assault min 10 years; aggravated penetrative assault min 20 years, up to life or death; child pornography defined; punished giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity
[138:3:10] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society p.88, p.101; NextGen Society - Group 2 Prelims Part 1 p.72
## SUB 4 | Age of Consent and the Juvenile-Age Debate
[138:4:0] TABLE head: Stage | Age of consent
  [138:4:0.0] IPC 1860 | 10
  [138:4:0.1] Age of Consent Act 1891 | 12
  [138:4:0.2] IPC amendment 1925 | 14
  [138:4:0.3] POCSO 2012 / CLA 2013 | 18
  [138:4:0.4] BNS Sec. 63 | Keeps 18
[138:4:1] - Marriage age (distinct from consent): **18 women, 21 men**.
[138:4:2] TABLE head: Body | Stand
  [138:4:2.0] Justice Verma Committee (2013) | Wanted 16
  [138:4:2.1] Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs (Anand Sharma, March 2021, report on crimes against women and children) | Asked the Government to consider reducing the POCSO age from 18 to 16, reasoning that minor sexual offenders left uncorrected may commit graver crimes (later reports: the panel did not press it)
  [138:4:2.2] Law Commission, 283rd Report (2023) | Against lowering – it would make POCSO a "paper law"
[138:4:3] - **Madhya Pradesh High Court** (2023) asked the Centre to lower the consent age to **16**, citing **early puberty due to social-media/internet exposure**.
[138:4:4] - **State of U.P. v. Anurudh** (SC, Jan 2026): flagged POCSO misuse in adolescent relationships; urged a "**Romeo-Juliet**" clause; SC set aside the **Calcutta HC** ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships.

## SUB 5 | Child Abuse – Forms and Data
[138:5:0] TABLE head: Form | Examples
  [138:5:0.0] Physical | Commission (beating, burning) or omission (medical/nutritional neglect)
  [138:5:0.1] Emotional | Verbal battering, educational neglect, encouraging delinquency
  [138:5:0.2] Social | Infanticide, child marriage, child prostitution, beggary
  [138:5:0.3] Online (CSAM) | 4.5 lakh+ reports (2023); IT Act 2000; IT Rules 2021 – large platforms detect CSAM automatically
[138:5:1] - **Causes** (e.g. poverty, family breakdown, **parental alcoholism**) vs consequences (trauma, delinquency, dropout).
[138:5:2] - **Study on Child Abuse: India 2007 (MWCD)**: 13 States; **two out of three** children faced physical abuse; **53.22%** reported sexual abuse; **over 50%** of abusers known to the child or in trust.
[138:5:3] - **NCRB 2021**: **97.1%** of child sexual-abuse offenders known to the child. **NCRB 2023**: **Madhya Pradesh** highest number of crimes against children; **Assam** highest rate.
[138:5:4] - Women are **more likely to be sexually abused at home** (by known persons) than outside; **dress is not a cause** of sexual abuse.

=== NOTES 2:139 | Child Welfare – Icds, Poshan Abhiyaan, Pm Poshan, Child Marriage, Malnutrition
## SUB 0 | ICDS – Services, Beneficiaries, Functionaries and Funding
[139:0:0] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [139:0:0.0] Launch | 2 October 1975 (5th Plan), on an experimental basis in 33 blocks; universalised 2006
  [139:0:0.1] Ministry | Ministry of Women and Child Development
  [139:0:0.2] Nature | Centrally sponsored, implemented by States/UTs – shared funding by Centre and States (60:40 general States; supplementary nutrition 50:50) – not fully Central, State or externally aided
  [139:0:0.3] Convergence | Ministry of Health (NHM) and Ministry of Women and Child Development
  [139:0:0.4] Beneficiaries | Children 0–6 years, pregnant women and lactating mothers; adolescent girls via the Scheme for Adolescent Girls
  [139:0:0.5] Current form | Anganwadi Services under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
  [139:0:0.6] AP start (1975) | Utnoor (Adilabad, tribal) and Kambadur (Anantapur) projects
[139:0:1] # The six services
[139:0:2] TABLE head: Service | Delivered through
  [139:0:2.0] Supplementary Nutrition (SNP) | Anganwadi Centre
  [139:0:2.1] Pre-school non-formal education (children 3–6) | Anganwadi Centre
  [139:0:2.2] Nutrition and health education (women 15–45) | Anganwadi Centre
  [139:0:2.3] Immunisation | Health system (NHM)
  [139:0:2.4] Health check-up | Health system
  [139:0:2.5] Referral services | Health system
[139:0:3] - **Not ICDS services**: **cash maternity benefit** (PMMVY), school meals (PM POSHAN), **100-day job guarantee** (MGNREGA).
[139:0:4] - **Non-formal (pre-school) education** beneficiaries: children **3–6**; nutrition and health education for **women 15–45**, pregnant and lactating mothers.
[139:0:5] # Functionaries
[139:0:6] TABLE head: Functionary | Role
  [139:0:6.0] Anganwadi Worker (AWW) | Grassroots, honorary ICDS functionary; runs the Anganwadi (the government child-care centre in rural India) – the main local-level functionary
  [139:0:6.1] Anganwadi Helper | Cooks and serves meals
  [139:0:6.2] Lady Supervisor | Supervises a cluster of AWCs
  [139:0:6.3] CDPO | Block-level ICDS officer – trained by NIPCCD
[139:0:7] - **NIPCCD** (National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development) trains ICDS staff – itself trains the **CDPOs**; supervisors and AWWs are trained at middle-level and Anganwadi training centres.
[139:0:8] - **ANM and ASHA belong to NHM**, not ICDS; MMU = mobile medical unit.
[139:0:9] - **ICDS at 50 (2025)**: about **14 lakh** AWCs. **AP**: 55,746 AWCs in **257 ICDS projects** (AP SES 2025-26).
[139:0:10] - **One Nation One Anganwadi**: **migrant families** moving to another State keep ICDS benefits for children below 6 and pregnant/lactating women (APPSC 2023).
[139:0:11] - **Mahila Shakti Kendras** (Budget 2017-18): to be set up in **14 lakh Anganwadi Centres**.

## SUB 1 | POSHAN Abhiyaan, Poshan 2.0 and Nutrition Campaigns
[139:1:0] # POSHAN Abhiyaan
[139:1:1] - **Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment** (earlier **National Nutrition Mission**) – the **2018 flagship** for holistic nutrition of children, adolescents, pregnant women and lactating mothers; launched **8 March 2018** at **Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan**. Goal: **Suposhit Bharat**, a **Jan Andolan**.
[139:1:2] - Targets: reduce **stunting**, undernutrition, **anaemia**, low birth weight; stunting to **25% by 2022** ("Mission 25 by 2022").
[139:1:3] - **Objectives (UPSC 2017)**: awareness of malnutrition among pregnant women and lactating mothers; reduce **anaemia** in young children, adolescent girls and women – **not** promoting millets/unpolished rice or poultry eggs.
[139:1:4] # Campaigns and tools
[139:1:5] TABLE head: Campaign / tool | Fact
  [139:1:5.0] Rashtriya Poshan Maah | September; 5th in 2022 (celebrated through Gram Panchayats as "Poshan Panchayats"), 6th in 2023, 9th in 2026 at Varanasi
  [139:1:5.1] Poshan Pakhwada | A fortnight, March–April; 8th edition April 2026 on brain development in the first six years

[139:1:6] # Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (2021)
[139:1:7] - Introduced in **2021** (MWCD, CSS, 2021-22 to 2025-26); merged **Anganwadi Services**, **POSHAN Abhiyaan** and the **Scheme for Adolescent Girls** (girls **14–18** in Aspirational Districts and NER); **PM POSHAN is not merged**. One of MWCD's three umbrella missions.

## SUB 2 | Mid-Day Meal to PM POSHAN
[139:2:0] TABLE head: Item | Fact
  [139:2:0.0] Started | 15 August 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NP-NSPE)
  [139:2:0.1] First State | Tamil Nadu
  [139:2:0.2] Renamed | PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman), 2021
  [139:2:0.3] Nature | Rights-based CSS under the NFSA 2013; cost 60:40
  [139:2:0.4] Ministry | Ministry of Education (not MWCD)
  [139:2:0.5] Coverage | Bal Vatika + Classes I–VIII, government and aided schools
  [139:2:0.6] Norms | Primary 450 kcal + 12 g protein; upper primary 700 kcal + 20 g
[139:2:1] - Aims: better **nutrition**, tackle **classroom hunger**, and **increase enrolment, attendance and retention** (school attendance) of disadvantaged children; also seen as fostering **social equality** (children eat together), educational advancement and the **right to food** (SC orders in PUCL v. UoI, 2001; NFSA 2013).
[139:2:2] - **Tithi Bhojan** (community meals) – first by **Gujarat**; **mandatory social audit** in every district.
[139:2:3] - **Akshaya Patra Foundation** (**Bengaluru**, 2000): the **largest not-for-profit/NGO** mid-day meal programme (not SEWA or Annapurna).
[139:2:4] - **AP – Dokka Seethamma Mid-Day Meal**: extended to **Intermediate (Classes 11–12)** in 2024-25.
[139:2:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Indian Economy p1 (APPSC) 03 p.3, 04 p.25; Rocket Indian Society p.3; app notes (old row 139)
## SUB 3 | Early Childhood Care and Education and Child Development
[139:3:0] # ECCE
[139:3:1] - **Article 45** (after the 86th Amendment, 2002): **early childhood care and education** for all children until they complete **six years**.
[139:3:2] - National ECCE Policy **2013**. **NEP 2020 foundational stage**: ages **3–8** = 3 years Anganwadi/pre-school + **Classes 1–2**.
[139:3:3] - **NCERT's National Curricular and Pedagogical Framework for ECCE** (children up to 8) is in **two parts** (0–3 and 3–8).
[139:3:4] - **NCF for the Foundational Stage (3–8)** – **Panchakosha**: **Sharirik** (physical), **Pranik** (life energy), **Manasik** (mental), **Bauddhik** (intellectual), **Chaitsik** (spiritual) vikas – **Dharmik vikas is not one**.
[139:3:5] - **NISHTHA 4.0** = online teacher training for **ECCE** (NISHTHA 1.0–3.0: elementary, secondary, FLN).
[139:3:6] - **Montessori** method: curriculum **child-centred**, based on the child's natural abilities and self-paced activity.
[139:3:7] # Child development and learning (psychology)
[139:3:8] TABLE head: Concept | Fact
  [139:3:8.0] 2–6 years (early childhood) | Pre-gang age (Hurlock); 6–12 = gang age
  [139:3:8.1] Adolescence | "Stress and storm" – G. Stanley Hall
  [139:3:8.2] IQ | Mental age ÷ chronological age × 100 → 10/15 × 100 ≈ 67
  [139:3:8.3] Punishment | Presenting a negative stimulus or removing a positive one
  [139:3:8.4] Reinforcement | Motivated behaviour should be followed by reward
  [139:3:8.5] Counselling | Non-directive = client-centred (Carl Rogers); directive = counsellor-centred
  [139:3:8.6] Authoritarian parenting | Parent strictly controls all aspects of the child's life; little warmth
  [139:3:8.7] Psychomotor domain (Harrow) | Begins with reflex movements; analysis = cognitive, receiving/character = affective
[139:3:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams (Art. 45); app notes (old row 139); general knowledge for the psychology table, not checked against a library file

## SUB 5 | Girl Child and Child Marriage
[139:5:0] # Child marriage law
[139:5:1] - **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**: minimum age **18 (girls) / 21 (boys)** – the minimum marriageable age of girls under law is **18**. Adult male contracting it: RI up to **2 years** + fine up to **₹1 lakh**. Child marriage is **voidable**; petition for annulment within **two years of attaining majority**. Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appointed by **State Governments**.
[139:5:2] - **PCM (Amendment) Bill, 2021**: women's age to **21**; annulment window **two → five years** after majority; **overrides any other law, custom or practice**; amends the 2006 Act → statements A, C, D correct. Referred to a Standing Committee; **lapsed** with the 17th Lok Sabha. **Jaya Jaitly Task Force (2020)** recommended it.
[139:5:3] - **Allahabad HC (1 July 2026)**: PCMA age limits apply to all citizens **irrespective of religion**. **NFHS-5**: **23.3%** of women 20–24 married before 18; highest **West Bengal**.
[139:5:4] - **ALIVA**: data-driven model to end child marriage – **Nayagarh district, Odisha**.
[139:5:5] # Girl child schemes
[139:5:6] TABLE head: Scheme | Fact
  [139:5:6.0] Beti Bachao Beti Padhao | 22 Jan 2015, Panipat; MWCD nodal; under Sambal; no DBT; SRB 918 → 929
  [139:5:6.1] Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana | 2015; Ministry of Finance; up to two girls; min ₹250 a year; matures at 21
  [139:5:6.2] Balika Samriddhi Yojana / Dhanalakshmi | 1997 / 2008 (pilot conditional cash transfer)
  [139:5:6.3] Bangaru Talli (AP) | Incentive to parents to take care of the girl child from birth to graduation
[139:5:7] - **National Girl Child Day: 24 January**.
[139:5:8] ~~ Sources: PRS Legislative Brief/Highlights, Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill 2021 (prsindia.org); NextGen Society - Group 2 Prelims Part 1 p.24-25; app notes (old row 139)

[139:6:0] - **National Nutrition Policy**: adopted **1993** under the Department of Women and Child Development.
[139:6:1] - **Food and Nutrition Board**: transferred in **1993** to the Department of WCD, then part of the **Ministry of Human Resource Development** (UPSC 2005 key); now under the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** (since 2006).
[139:6:2] TABLE head: Indicator (under 5, NFHS-5) | India | AP
  [139:6:2.0] Stunting | 35.5% | 31.2%
  [139:6:2.1] Wasting | 19.3% | 16.1%
  [139:6:2.2] Underweight | 32.1% | 29.6%
[139:6:3] - Anaemia in women 15–49: **57.0%** (**Anaemia Mukt Bharat**). U5MR = deaths before the **fifth birthday** per 1,000 live births.
[139:6:4] - **Global Hunger Index 2025**: India **102nd of 123**, "**serious**".
