## SUB 7 | Child Protection – Mission Vatsalya, Creches and Balwadis
[139:7:0] - **Mission Vatsalya** (MWCD, CSS, **2021-22**): child protection, **happy childhood** and development aligned to the **SDGs** (not Laalana, Bala Vihar or Balsamrudhi); **subsumed ICPS**; outlay **₹10,916 crore**; CHILDLINE 1098 with ERSS-112.
[139:7:1] TABLE head: Component | Norm
  [139:7:1.0] Sponsorship / foster care | ₹4,000 per child per month
  [139:7:1.1] Aftercare | 18–21 (extendable to 23)
[139:7:2] - **PM CARES for Children (2021)**: COVID-19 orphans; **₹10 lakh** at **23**. JJ Amendment 2021: **District Magistrate** focal point for adoption.
[139:7:3] - **Creches**: first started by the **Central Social Welfare Board** for children **0–5** of working mothers (agricultural, construction work) → Rajiv Gandhi National Creche Scheme → **Palna** (**6 months–6 years**, open whether or not the mother is employed).
[139:7:4] - **Balwadi Nutrition Programme**: **supplementary nutrition** to children **3–5 years** in **Balwadis** and/or creches.
[139:7:5] - **Green Passage** (Odisha, 2020): **orphan students** – free higher education. **Mission DAKSH** (Bihar): remedial classes to minimise **school dropouts**.
[139:7:6] - **National Bravery Award (ICCW)**: **Bharat Award** (announced **January 2017**) posthumously to **Tarh Peeju** (8, Arunachal Pradesh), who died saving two friends from drowning.

=== NOTES 2:140 | Rights of Persons with Disabilities – RPwD Act 2016, Uncrpd, Sugamya Bharat
## SUB 0 | Schemes, Portals and Initiatives for Persons with Disabilities
[140:0:0] # Campaigns and portals (DEPwD, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment)
[140:0:1] TABLE head: Scheme / portal | Purpose
  [140:0:1.0] Accessible India Campaign = Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan | For persons with disabilities; launched 3 December 2015; DEPwD flagship; universal accessibility in built environment, transport and ICT
  [140:0:1.1] Sugamya Bharat App | Crowdsourced reporting of accessibility gaps in buildings, transport, infrastructure
  [140:0:1.2] UDID (Swavlamban portal) | Single national disability ID and digital certificate; centralised national database
  [140:0:1.3] ADIP | Free aids and appliances (plus corrective surgery) below income ₹22,500/month; subsidised up to ₹30,000
  [140:0:1.4] DDRS | Grants-in-aid to NGOs for rehabilitation
  [140:0:1.5] SIPDA | Grant-in-aid to implement the RPwD Act
  [140:0:1.6] PM-DAKSH-DEPwD portal (2023) | UDID-based skilling + Divyangjan Rozgar Setu (jobs); MoSJE, not Minority Affairs
  [140:0:1.7] IGNDPS (NSAP) | Pension to severely disabled BPL persons (MoRD)
  [140:0:1.8] Scholarships | 6 components: pre-matric, post-matric, Top Class, National Fellowship, Overseas, Free Coaching
  [140:0:1.9] PRASHAST App | NCERT / Dept. of School Education & Literacy (September 2022), not DEPwD; teachers screen children for disability conditions (the 21 RPwD disabilities)
  [140:0:1.10] Sugamya Pustakalaya | Online library of accessible books – DAISY, audio, Braille
[140:0:2] - The three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign: **built environment, transport, ICT**.
[140:0:3] - **Accessible elections:** accessible booths, **Braille-enabled EVMs**.
[140:0:4] - 3 December = International Day of Persons with Disabilities **and** launch of the Accessible India Campaign (2015).
[140:0:5] # Inclusion and entrepreneurship
[140:0:6] - **Inclusive India initiative** (MoSJE / **National Trust**): brings persons with **intellectual and developmental disabilities** into the mainstream (inclusive education, employment, community life) – not women, PVTGs or the third gender.
[140:0:7] - **EKAM Fest** (**E**ntrepreneurship, **K**nowledge, **A**wareness, **M**arketing): organised by **NHFDC** (now NDFDC), first held 2-9 March 2020 in New Delhi; promotes **Divyangjan entrepreneurship** and awareness of the potential of PwDs.
[140:0:8] - **Divya Kala Shakti** (DEPwD): cultural showcase of the artistic talent of PwDs.
[140:0:9] - **Indian Sign Language Dictionary** (ISLRTC, DEPwD): 1st edition March 2018 (~3,000 terms); **2nd edition 27 February 2019** (~6,000 terms – the edition asked as "released in March 2019"); 3rd edition February 2021 (10,000 terms).
[140:0:10] - **"Access to libraries for persons with disabilities – Checklist"**: developed by **IFLA** (International Federation of Library Associations), Professional Report No. 89, 2005.
[140:0:11] # Inclusive education
[140:0:12] - **Special education** targets **children with disabilities (CwSN)**, not gifted children.
[140:0:13] - **Samagra Shiksha** inclusive component: assessment, aids, assistive technology, therapy for all RPwD disabilities – exclusive education of gifted children is **not** part of it.
[140:0:14] > Trap: PRASHAST = Education ministry/NCERT, not DEPwD; ADIP = aids to individuals; DDRS = grants to NGOs; EKAM = entrepreneurship.

## SUB 1 | RPwD Act 2016 and the Disability Laws
[140:1:0] # Laws and milestones
[140:1:1] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [140:1:1.0] 1981 | UN International Year of Disabled Persons
  [140:1:1.1] 1992 | Rehabilitation Council of India Act – constitution of the RCI for regulating the training of rehabilitation professionals (statutory body from 1993)
  [140:1:1.2] 1995 | PwD (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act – first comprehensive, welfare-based law; 7 disabilities; created the Chief Commissioner
  [140:1:1.3] 1999 | National Trust Act – autism, cerebral palsy, mental retardation, multiple disabilities
  [140:1:1.4] 2006 | First National Policy for PwDs
  [140:1:1.5] 13 Dec 2006 | UNGA adopted the UNCRPD
  [140:1:1.6] Oct 2007 | India ratified the UNCRPD
  [140:1:1.7] 2010 | Sudha Kaul Committee (MoSJE) drafted the replacement Bill
  [140:1:1.8] 2016 | Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act enacted (Bill passed by Parliament December 2016)
  [140:1:1.9] 19 Apr 2017 | RPwD Act in force
[140:1:2] - Order: UNCRPD adopted → India ratified → RPwD enacted → in force.
[140:1:3] # RPwD Act 2016 – key provisions
[140:1:4] - **First rights-based** disability law; **replaced the 1995 Act**; meets UNCRPD obligations; bars discrimination in government employment.
[140:1:5] - The 2016 law is named **"The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act"** – the 1995 law was "Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act".
[140:1:6] - **Sec. 2(s)**: PwD = long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairment which, with barriers, blocks full participation.
[140:1:7] TABLE head: Provision | Value
  [140:1:7.0] Specified disabilities | 21 (from 7), e.g. autism, acid attack victims, sickle cell disease; Centre may add
  [140:1:7.1] Benchmark disability | At least 40%
  [140:1:7.2] Government jobs | 4%
  [140:1:7.3] Higher education | 5% seats
  [140:1:7.4] Free education | Benchmark-disability children 6–18
  [140:1:7.5] Monitoring | Chief Commissioner for PwDs, Sec. 75(1)
[140:1:8] - Survivors of **forcible acid ingestion** recognised as acid attack victims (SC, 5 May 2026).
[140:1:9] > Trap: passed **2016** (not 2014/2018), in force 19 April 2017; 4% jobs vs 5% higher education; 7 → **21** (not 17 or 15).
[140:1:10] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society (src/society/rocket-indian-society.txt) p.41, p.87, p.91, p.102; NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 p.8; app notes 2:140 sub 1-2
## SUB 2 | Types of Disability – Learning Disability and Blindness
[140:2:0] - **Learning disability** = difficulty in a specific academic skill despite normal intelligence: **dyslexia** (reading), dysgraphia (writing), dyscalculia (maths).
[140:2:1] - **Dyslexia** is the example specific to learning disability; **autism spectrum disorder**, **ADHD** and **mental retardation (intellectual disability)** are separate developmental conditions, not specific learning disabilities.
[140:2:2] - RPwD Act 2016 lists **specific learning disabilities** among its 21 disabilities, separately from autism and intellectual disability.
[140:2:3] - **New definition of blindness (April 2017, MoHFW, WHO criteria):** a person is blind if unable to **count fingers from 3 metres** (the 1976 definition used **6 metres**); programme renamed National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment.
[140:2:4] > Trap: dyslexia = learning disability; ADHD and autism are not "specific learning disabilities"; blindness now 3 m, not 6 m.
[140:2:5] ~~ Sources: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/india-changes-definition-of-blindness-394675; general knowledge, not checked (learning-disability types); app notes 2:140 sub 2
## SUB 3 | Institutions for Persons with Disabilities
[140:3:0] TABLE head: Body | Mandate
  [140:3:0.0] Chief Commissioner for PwDs | Statutory authority under RPwD Act; monitors, takes up complaints
  [140:3:0.1] State Commissioners | Same role in each State
  [140:3:0.2] National Trust | Legal guardians; Niramaya (health insurance up to ₹1 lakh/year), Disha, Vikas, Samarth, Gharaunda
  [140:3:0.3] RCI (Act 1992; statutory 1993) | Regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals; maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register
  [140:3:0.4] NDFDC (formerly NHFDC) | Under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (DEPwD), working since 1997; concessional loans for self-employment up to ₹50 lakh at 5–9%; education loans 4%; 40%+ disability, 18+; organises EKAM Fest
  [140:3:0.5] ALIMCO | CPSE, 1972; aids and artificial limbs
  [140:3:0.6] Institute | Place
  [140:3:0.7] SVNIRTAR | Cuttack
  [140:3:0.8] NIEPID (intellectual disabilities) | Secunderabad
  [140:3:0.9] Visual disability | Dehradun
  [140:3:0.10] Locomotor disability | Kolkata
[140:3:1] - Nodal ministry for PwDs: **Social Justice and Empowerment** (DEPwD).
[140:3:2] - **Teacher–pupil ratio** for visually impaired children in integrated education: **1:8** (special-teacher norm of the integrated education scheme; also the 8:1 ratio the Supreme Court notified for schools for the visually impaired, 2021).
[140:3:3] - **First university only for the disabled:** **Jagadguru Rambhadracharya Handicapped (now Divyanga) University**, **Chitrakoot (UP)**, set up 2001.
[140:3:4] > Trap: NIEPID = Secunderabad; locomotor = Kolkata; NHFDC is under MoSJE, not HRD or Rural Development.
[140:3:5] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society (src/society/rocket-indian-society.txt) p.11, p.41; https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1604780 (NHFDC under MoSJE); https://future.indiankanoon.org/doc/119243333/ (ratio 1:8); https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/compulsory-tet-rule-robs-tn-s-children-visual-impairments-right-education-171413; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagadguru_Rambhadracharya_Divyanga_University; app notes 2:140 sub 3
## SUB 4 | Constitutional Basis, UNCRPD, Days and MoUs
[140:4:0] TABLE head: Provision | Content
  [140:4:0.0] Art. 41 (DPSP) | Public assistance in disablement
  [140:4:0.1] Art. 46 | Weaker sections
  [140:4:0.2] State List Entry 9 | "Relief of the disabled and unemployable"
[140:4:1] - India has ratified the UNCRPD (2007) but **not** its **Optional Protocol** (individual complaints).
[140:4:2] - Spending about **0.02% of GDP** (South Africa 0.12–0.15%); proposed national minimum disability pension ₹8,000 a month under Art. 41 (13 Jun 2026).

## SUB 5 | Cases on Disability Rights
[140:5:0] TABLE head: Case | Issue
  [140:5:0.0] Jeeja Ghosh v. UoI (12 May 2016) | Woman with cerebral palsy deplaned (Kolkata–Goa, 2012); right to live with dignity; SpiceJet ordered to pay ₹10 lakh
  [140:5:0.1] Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021) | Scribe not limited to benchmark disability; reasonable accommodation part of equality
  [140:5:0.2] Rajive Raturi v. UoI (8 Nov 2024) | Mandatory accessibility standards; Rule 15(1) of RPwD Rules ultra vires; time-bound directions for transport and buildings
  [140:5:0.3] SC, March 2026 (Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta) | 40% is a floor, not a ceiling; suitability by functional ability
  [140:5:0.4] T.M.A. Pai (2002) | Minority status unit = State (distractor)
[140:5:1] - SC: **safe footpaths** part of Art. 21, minimum width **1.8 m**; **digital access** part of Art. 21, citing the **UNCRPD**.
[140:5:2] - **Prisoners with disabilities (SC, Dec 2025):** prisons to be made accessible and **prison manuals revised** in line with the **RPwD Act, 2016**.
[140:5:3] ~~ Sources: https://moneylife.in/article/spicejet-asked-to-pay-rs10-lakh-for-offloading-a-disabled-passenger/46918.html; Rocket Indian Society p.94-95; app notes 2:140 sub 4, 8
## SUB 6 | Data and Andhra Pradesh – SADAREM
[140:6:0] - **Census 2011**: **2.68 crore** PwDs = **2.21%** (about **2.2%**) of the population (2001: 2.13%); largest: **movement 20.3%**, hearing 18.9%, seeing 18.8%. WHO estimate ~16% → under-reporting.
[140:6:1] - **Census 2027**: adds acid attack, neurological and blood disorders; autism and dwarfism left out.
[140:6:2] - **SADAREM** (Software for Assessment of Disability for Access, Rehabilitation and Empowerment), Andhra Pradesh: **centralised database** that assesses **disabled persons** and issues digitally signed permanent disability certificates; 3,14,211 certificates in 2024-25.
[140:6:3] - **AP**: **11.04 lakh** PwDs (Census 2011); largest type orthopaedic.
[140:6:4] - **Divyang Shakti** (AP): **100% free APSRTC travel** from **18 March 2026** for 40%+ disability; escort 50%; SADAREM certification.
[140:6:5] - AP pension **₹6,000** a month; 52,263 assistive devices (11 Jun 2026).
[140:6:6] - **AP Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation**: aids, appliances, economic rehabilitation.
[140:6:7] - AP Samagra Shiksha: **Best State** in implementing RPwD Act (2024-25); ₹3,500 per CwSN; 679 Bhavitha Centres; 9 DDRCs, 70 NGOs under DDRS.
[140:6:8] > Trap: SADAREM = AP disability database (not minorities/women/children); UDID = the national one.
[140:6:9] ~~ Sources: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 (src/economy/ap-socio-economic-survey-2024-25.txt) p.232; https://www.governancenow.com/news/regular-story/-268-crore-disabled-in-india-govt-report; NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 p.6, p.16; app notes 2:140 sub 9

=== NOTES 2:141 | Rights of the Elderly – Senior Citizens Act 2007 and Schemes
## SUB 0 | NSAP and Old-age Pensions
[141:0:0] # National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)
[141:0:1] - Launched **15 August 1995** (first national social assistance programme); ministry **Rural Development (MoRD)**, not Social Justice; rests on **Articles 41 and 42**.
[141:0:2] - Cabinet approved continuation **FY 2026-27 to 2030-31** (outlay ₹53,428 crore); renamed **Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana** (sub-schemes e.g. PM Vriddhavastha Pension Yojana, PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana) (2026).
[141:0:3] - Five components:
[141:0:4]   - 1. **IGNOAPS** – old-age pension (BPL, 60+): Rs 200/month (60-79), Rs 500 (80+); Centre's share frozen at Rs 200 since 2007; about 2.2 crore beneficiaries (June 2026).
[141:0:5]   - 2. **IGNWPS** – widow pension (BPL widows 40-79).
[141:0:6]   - 3. **IGNDPS** – disability pension (80% or more disability).
[141:0:7]   - 4. **NFBS** – lump sum on death of the primary breadwinner (Rs 20,000).
[141:0:8]   - 5. **Annapurna** – **10 kg free food grains** a month to seniors eligible for but not getting IGNOAPS.
[141:0:9] # State schemes
[141:0:10] TABLE head: Scheme | State | Feature
  [141:0:10.0] Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana | Bihar (2019) | Universal: all aged 60+ with no other pension; Rs 400 (60-79), Rs 500 (80+); no income bar
  [141:0:10.1] NTR Bharosa Pension (earlier YSR Pension Kanuka) | Andhra Pradesh | Old-age pension raised from Rs 3,000 to Rs 4,000/month (G.O. 43, 13 June 2024); minimum age 60, but 50 for STs (incl. PVTGs)
[141:0:11] - AP: 7 physiotherapy centres under the National Action Plan for Senior Citizens treated 87,240 patients (APSES 2024-25).
[141:0:12] > Trap: NSAP began **1995** (not 1997/1999); it is under **MoRD**; NFBS belongs to NSAP, not AVYAY.
[141:0:13] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society (src/society/rocket-indian-society.txt) p.9; Rocket CA 2026-01 (src/current-affairs/rocket-ca-2026-01.txt) p.153-154; https://www.myscheme.gov.in/schemes/ysrpk (ST age 50); app notes 2:141 sub 4
## SUB 1 | Central Schemes for the Elderly
[141:1:0] TABLE head: Scheme | Ministry / agency | Benefit
  [141:1:0.0] Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana | MoSJE; ALIMCO | Free physical aids (walking sticks, wheelchairs, hearing aids, dentures) to BPL seniors (60+, or income up to Rs 15,000/month); funded from the Senior Citizens' Welfare Fund (unclaimed deposits); at least 30% women per district; launched 1 April 2017 at Nellore, AP
  [141:1:0.1] AVYAY (Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana) | MoSJE | April 2021, renamed from National Action Plan for Senior Citizens; umbrella of 4: Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, State Action Plan, RVY, Elder Line; Rs 287.81 crore utilised (ES 2025-26)
  [141:1:0.2] PMVVY (PM Vaya Vandana Yojana) | Ministry of Finance; LIC | 2017; social security in old age with assured pension 8% for 10 years; max purchase Rs 7.5 lakh at launch (raised to Rs 15 lakh in 2018); closed for new subscription after 31 March 2023
  [141:1:0.3] Varishtha Pension Bima Yojana | LIC (Budget 2003-04) | Launched 14 July 2003 for senior citizens (55+ in 2003; 60+ in the 2014 version); single premium, assured 9% return
  [141:1:0.4] Senior Citizen Savings Scheme | India Post / banks | Safe fixed-interest savings for seniors
  [141:1:0.5] Ayushman Vay Vandana card | MoHFW (AB-PMJAY) | Health cover of Rs 5 lakh for all aged 70+, irrespective of income (2024)
[141:1:1] - Matching set (2023): **PMFBY** = crop insurance; **PMVVY** = old-age pension at 8%; **PMJDY** = basic bank account for every unbanked household.
[141:1:2] - **IPOP / Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC):** up to **90%** of project cost to **NGOs** for old-age homes, day-care centres, mobile medicare units.
[141:1:3] - **SAGE** (Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine): up to **Rs 1 crore** equity for elder-care start-ups (Govt stake below 49%) (Aug 2026).
[141:1:4] - **SACRED portal**: re-employment of senior citizens.
[141:1:5] > Trap: PMVVY = pension (LIC, Finance); Vay Vandana = health (70+); Vayoshri = aids (ALIMCO); Varishtha = senior citizens, not the disabled.
[141:1:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 (src/society/nextgen-society-group2-03.txt) p.5; https://www.pmindia.gov.in/en/news_updates/cabinet-gives-ex-post-facto-approval-to-varistha-pension-bima-yojana-2003-and-varistha-pension-bima-yojana-2014/; app notes 2:141 sub 2
## SUB 2 | Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
[141:2:0] - Enacted in **2007**; nodal ministry **MoSJE**; brought into force **state by state** from **29 December 2007**.
[141:2:1] - Creates a **legal obligation** on adult **children (biological, adopted, step)** and **legal heirs** to maintain parents and senior citizens who cannot maintain themselves.
[141:2:2] - The Act **punishes children for neglecting old parents**: **abandonment** of a senior citizen – up to **3 months** jail and/or **Rs 5,000** fine.
[141:2:3] - **Old age homes:** at least **one per district**.
[141:2:4] TABLE head: Section | Provision
  [141:2:4.0] Section 20 | Medical care of senior citizens; basis of the NPHCE
  [141:2:4.1] Section 23 | Property transfer made on condition of care can be declared void by the Tribunal if the transferee neglects the parent
  [141:2:4.2] Feature | Detail
  [141:2:4.3] Maintenance Tribunal | Sub-division level; in AP headed by RDO / Sub-Collector
  [141:2:4.4] Appellate Tribunal | District level; in AP headed by the District Collector
  [141:2:4.5] Maximum maintenance | Rs 10,000 per month
  [141:2:4.6] Time limit | Case decided within 90 days
[141:2:5] - **2019 Amendment Bill:** proposed **removing the Rs 10,000 cap** and covering **in-laws and grandchildren**; it **lapsed** (not passed).
[141:2:6] - **First State law:** **Himachal Pradesh** Maintenance of Parents and Dependents Act, **2001**.
[141:2:7] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society (src/society/rocket-indian-society.txt) p.88, p.102; NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 p.5; app notes 2:141 sub 0
## SUB 3 | National Policies on Older Persons
[141:3:0] TABLE head: Policy | Year / ministry | Focus
  [141:3:0.0] NPOP (National Policy on Older Persons) | 1999; MoSJE | Older person = 60 years or above; 14 principal areas of intervention incl. health care and nutrition
  [141:3:0.1] NPHCE | 2010-11; MoHFW (not MoSJE) | Health care of the elderly; based on Section 20 of the 2007 Act
  [141:3:0.2] NPSC (National Policy for Senior Citizens) | 2011 | Elderly women, "ageing in place"; harsh punishment for elder abuse; income security, homecare, health insurance; destitution among rural elderly
[141:3:1] ~~ Sources: NextGen Society Group 2 Part 3 (src/society/nextgen-society-group2-03.txt) p.12-15; app notes 2:141 sub 1
## SUB 4 | Elder Line, Ageing Data and Elder Abuse
[141:4:0] - **Elder Line 14567** – National Helpline for Senior Citizens; **MoSJE**; component of **AVYAY**; technical support from **Tata Trusts** and **NSE Foundation**.
[141:4:1] - **LASI** (Longitudinal Ageing Study in India), Wave 1 **2017-18**, by **IIPS, Mumbai**, under MoHFW; about **72,250** persons aged **45+** and their spouses.
[141:4:2] - **India Ageing Report 2023** – by **UNFPA** with **IIPS** (not HelpAge India): elderly to **exceed children (0-14) by 2046**; feminisation and ruralisation of ageing.
[141:4:3] - **AP elderly share:** about **12.4%** of AP's population aged **60+** in **2021** (*Elderly in India 2021*, NSO); India **10.1%**; Kerala 16.5%.
[141:4:4] - **HelpAge India:** elderly-care services; releases **elder-abuse surveys**.
[141:4:5] - **Shyam Saran Negi** (Kalpa, Kinnaur, HP) – independent India's **first voter** (Oct 1951).
[141:4:6] TABLE head: Framework / day | Year / date
  [141:4:6.0] Madrid International Plan of Action on Ageing | 2002
  [141:4:6.1] UN Decade of Healthy Ageing | 2021-2030
  [141:4:6.2] International Day of Older Persons | 1 October
  [141:4:6.3] World Elder Abuse Awareness Day | 15 June
[141:4:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:141 sub 3, 5-7

=== NOTES 2:143 | Transgender Persons – Nalsa Judgment, 2019 Act; Provisions for the Elderly
## SUB 0 | State Measures and Reservation for Transgender Persons
[143:0:0] TABLE head: State | Measure
  [143:0:0.0] Karnataka | First State with 1% reservation for transgender persons in all government (civil) services by direct recruitment – notification 6 July 2021 (horizontal)
  [143:0:0.1] Tamil Nadu | First Transgender Welfare Board (2008); Third Gender Tailoring Cooperative (2020); Thirunangaigal app (2021)
  [143:0:0.2] Kerala | First State transgender policy (November 2015); Sthree Suraksha scheme
  [143:0:0.3] Andhra Pradesh | State Transgender Policy 2025; ~3,125 certificates via the National Portal
[143:0:1] - **Horizontal reservation** (cutting across SC/ST/OBC/General) is the community's demand; NALSA had given a **vertical**, OBC-type quota.
[143:0:2] - The horizontal-reservation demand returned in **June 2023**: **27 June 2023** Mumbai protest by **transgender** persons over **Maharashtra's** reply to the **Bombay High Court** that more reservation was "difficult".
[143:0:3] > Trap: Karnataka = job quota; Tamil Nadu = welfare board; Kerala = policy.
[143:0:4] ~~ Sources: https://www.barandbench.com/news/litigation/karnataka-becomes-first-in-the-country-to-provide-1-reservation-for-transgender-persons-in-public-employment; https://ksgindia.com/study-material/today-s-editorial/todays-editorial-18-july-2023.html; app notes 2:143 sub 7-8
## SUB 1 | First Transgender Persons
[143:1:0] TABLE head: Person | First
  [143:1:0.0] Joyita Mondal (West Bengal) | Judge – Lok Adalat, Islampur, Uttar Dinajpur, 8 July 2017

[143:1:1] ~~ Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyita_Mondal; app notes 2:143 sub 6
## SUB 2 | NALSA v. Union of India (2014) and Related Judgements
[143:2:0] - Delivered **15 April 2014** by Justices **K.S. Radhakrishnan** and **A.K. Sikri**; recognised transgender persons as the **"third gender"**.
[143:2:1] - **Gender identity is self-determined** – not by biological examination.
[143:2:2] - Directions: treat as **SEBC** for reservation (**vertical, OBC-type** quota); separate **public toilets**, health facilities, welfare schemes.
[143:2:3] TABLE head: Case | Year | Issue decided
  [143:2:3.0] K.S. Puttaswamy | 2017 | Nine-judge bench: privacy a fundamental right (Art. 21)
  [143:2:3.1] Navtej Singh Johar | 2018 | Decriminalised same-sex relations (Section 377 IPC)
  [143:2:3.2] Supriyo v. Union of India | 17 Oct 2023 | 5-judge bench, 3:2: no legal recognition of same-sex marriage; left to Parliament
[143:2:4] ~~ Sources: Rocket Indian Society (src/society/rocket-indian-society.txt) p.96; app notes 2:143 sub 0-1
## SUB 3 | Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 and 2026 Amendment
[143:3:0] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [143:3:0.0] 2014 | Rights of Transgender Persons Bill – private member's Bill by Tiruchi Siva (DMK)
  [143:3:0.1] April 2015 | Rajya Sabha passed it – first private member's Bill passed there in over four decades; not passed by Lok Sabha
  [143:3:0.2] 2019 | Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act; in force 10 January 2020
  [143:3:0.3] 13 Mar 2026 | Amendment Bill introduced by Virendra Kumar in Lok Sabha
[143:3:1] - **Definition:** includes trans men/women, **intersex variations**, genderqueer and socio-cultural identities (kinner, hijra, aravani, jogta); administered by **MoSJE**.
[143:3:2] - **Certificate of identity:** **District Magistrate**; revised certificate **after surgery**; application through the **National Portal for Transgender Persons** (Rules 2020).
[143:3:3] - Offences (forced labour, abuse etc.) = **6 months to 2 years + fine**; criticism: lighter penalties, DM gatekeeping, **no reservation**.
[143:3:4] - **2026 Amendment:** self-perceived identity **excluded** (Sec. 4(2) omitted); certificate by DM on a medical board's advice – criticised for **reversing NALSA's self-identification**; challenged by **Laxmi Narayan Tripathi** and **Zainab Javid Patel**.
[143:3:5] - **National Council for Transgender Persons:** statutory (Sec. 16, 2019 Act), constituted **21 August 2020**; chair = **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**; non-official term **3 years**.
[143:3:6] - **NHRC Advisory 2.0** (May 2026): separate **intersex, trans men, trans women** categories in Census 2027.
[143:3:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:143 sub 2-4
## SUB 4 | SMILE, Garima Greh and Data
[143:4:0] - **SMILE** (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise): 2022, **MoSJE**; outlay **Rs 365 crore**; goal **"Bhiksha Vritti Mukt Bharat"**; skilling via **PM-DAKSH**.
[143:4:1] - **Garima Greh** = **shelter homes** for transgender persons – **23 in 17** States/UTs (ES 2025-26).
[143:4:2] - **Census 2011:** about **4.88 lakh** transgender persons; highest **Uttar Pradesh**.
[143:4:3] - **NTR Bharosa Pension (AP):** **Rs 4,000/month** for elderly (60+), widows and transgender persons.
[143:4:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:143 sub 5, 8
## SUB 5 | Provisions for the Elderly
[143:5:0] - NSAP rests on **Articles 41 and 42**; **"invalidity and old age pensions"** = **Concurrent List Entry 24**.
[143:5:1] - Senior Citizens Act 2007: **Maintenance Tribunal** (sub-division) and Appellate Tribunal (district); max **Rs 10,000/month**; earlier law **Himachal Pradesh, 2001**.
[143:5:2] - **NPOP 1999** (older person = **60+**); **NPSC 2011** (elderly women, ageing in place).
[143:5:3] - **Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana:** physical aids to BPL seniors; launched **1 April 2017, Nellore**; **AVYAY** (2021) = umbrella of **4**; **SACRED portal** = **re-employment**.
[143:5:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:143 sub 9

=== NOTES 2:148 | Phases of Indian Foreign Policy
## SUB 0 | Prime Ministers and Their Foreign-Policy Landmarks
[148:0:0] # PM → term → initiative
[148:0:1] TABLE head: PM | Term | Foreign-policy / landmark
  [148:0:1.0] Jawaharlal Nehru | 1947–64 | Non-alignment (announced as interim PM, 1946), Panchsheel; held External Affairs himself – free India's first Foreign Minister
  [148:0:1.1] Lal Bahadur Shastri | 1964–66 | Tashkent Declaration (10 January 1966)
  [148:0:1.2] Indira Gandhi | 1966–77, 1980–84 | Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla Agreement (1972) with Z.A. Bhutto, Pokhran-I; MISA 1971; Twenty Point Programme (1975); Sarkaria Commission (1983)
  [148:0:1.3] Rajiv Gandhi | 31 Oct 1984 – 1 Dec 1989 | Sri Lanka Accord, IPKF, SAARC; 1988 action plan for nuclear disarmament; first brought the Nagarpalika Bill (1989)
  [148:0:1.4] P.V. Narasimha Rao | 21 June 1991 – 16 May 1996 | Look East Policy (1991–92), full ties with Israel (1992), economic reforms (FM Manmohan Singh)
  [148:0:1.5] I.K. Gujral | 1997–98 | Gujral Doctrine (as Foreign Minister, 1996)
  [148:0:1.6] A.B. Vajpayee | 1998–2004 | Pokhran-II, NFU, Lahore bus, Golden Quadrilateral
  [148:0:1.7] Manmohan Singh | 2004–14 | Nuclear deal, NSG waiver 2008
  [148:0:1.8] Narendra Modi | 2014– | Neighbourhood First, Act East, G20, Voice of Global South; Kartarpur Corridor inaugurated (9 Nov 2019); first PM to visit Israel
[148:0:2] - **First PM to visit Israel:** **Narendra Modi**, **4–6 July 2017** – marked **25 years** of full diplomatic ties (set up **1992** under Narasimha Rao); not Vajpayee, Manmohan or Gujral.
[148:0:3] - **Look East Policy** formulated by **P.V. Narasimha Rao** (Laxmikanth: first initiated 1992); upgraded to **Act East (2014)**.
[148:0:4] - **Half-Lion** (2016) – a book on Narasimha Rao by **Vinay Sitapati**.
[148:0:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.694 (Tashkent), p.704-706 (MISA, Twenty Point Programme), p.729 (Simla), p.776-777 (Rao: Look East, Nagarpalika), p.787-788 (Vajpayee: Lahore, Kargil, Golden Quadrilateral); Laxmikanth Ch89 p.864 (Look East 1992, Act East 2014); app notes 2:148 sub 6
## SUB 1 | Six Phases of Indian Foreign Policy
[148:1:0] TABLE head: Phase | Label | Features
  [148:1:0.0] 1946–62 | Optimistic non-alignment | Idealism, Panchsheel, NAM, Commonwealth, anti-imperialism; "Hindi-Chini Bhai-Bhai"
  [148:1:0.1] 1962–71 | Realism and recovery | 1965 war, Tashkent (1966); defence pact with the US (1964); no NPT (1968)
  [148:1:0.2] 1971–91 | Regional assertion | Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Pokhran-I, IPKF
  [148:1:0.3] 1991–98 | Safeguarding strategic autonomy | USSR collapse, 1991 crisis; Look East, Gujral Doctrine
  [148:1:0.4] 1998–2013 | Balancing power | Pokhran-II, NFU, Indo-US deal (NSG waiver 2008)
  [148:1:0.5] 2014 onwards | Energetic engagement | Multi-alignment, "5S" (Samman, Samvad, Sahyog, Shanti, Samriddhi)
[148:1:1] - Idealism → realism; non-alignment → multi-alignment; the constant is **strategic autonomy**.
[148:1:2] # Nehruvian era
[148:1:3] - NAM, Panchsheel, Commonwealth membership.
[148:1:4] - **Korean War**: India headed the **Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission** for POWs – **Gen. K.S. Thimayya**.
[148:1:5] - Kashmir taken to the UN (Jan 1948); the **1962 war** with China showed the **limits of idealism**.
[148:1:6] # 1971–1991: regional assertion
[148:1:7] TABLE head: Event | Date | Fact
  [148:1:7.0] Tashkent Declaration | 10 Jan 1966 | Shastri–Ayub Khan, Soviet mediation
  [148:1:7.1] Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation | 9 Aug 1971 | 20 years; checked US-China-Pakistan axis
  [148:1:7.2] Bangladesh liberation | 16 Dec 1971 | Pakistan army surrendered in Dhaka
  [148:1:7.3] Simla Agreement | 2 July 1972 | India–Pakistan; bilateralism, no third party
  [148:1:7.4] Pokhran-I | 18 May 1974 | "Peaceful nuclear explosion"
  [148:1:7.5] Katchatheevu ceded to Sri Lanka | 1974 | —
  [148:1:7.6] Farakka Accord | 1977 | Ganga water, India–Bangladesh
  [148:1:7.7] IPKF in Sri Lanka | 1987–90 | India-Sri Lanka Accord 1987 (Rajiv Gandhi–J.R. Jayewardene)
[148:1:8] - **Chronology (UPPSC 2002):** **Tashkent (1966) → Indo-Soviet Treaty (1971) → Simla (1972) → Farakka (1977)** = code **4, 2, 1, 3**; later Lahore (1999) → 123 Agreement (2008).
[148:1:9] # Post-Cold War (1991–98)
[148:1:10] - **Look East Policy** 1991–92, **P.V. Narasimha Rao**; closer to ASEAN; ties with **Israel**.
[148:1:11] - **LPG reforms**: attracting **FDI and markets** became foreign-policy goals; strategic ties with the US in the "unipolar moment".
[148:1:12] - **Gujral Doctrine (1996)**: goodwill to neighbours without asking anything in return.
[148:1:13] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.1-2 (phases); Spectrum p.694, p.726-729, p.777; app notes 2:148 sub 0-3
## SUB 2 | Post-1998 and Contemporary Multi-alignment
[148:2:0] # Pokhran-II and after
[148:2:1] - **Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti), May 1998**, PM **Vajpayee**: India declared itself a **nuclear-weapon state** (not NPT-recognised, not NSG member).
[148:2:2] - **No First Use** announced by the **Vajpayee** government; formal doctrine 2003.
[148:2:3] - Sanctions: US (**Glenn Amendment**), Japan; followed by **Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott** talks (after the tests, not before).
[148:2:4] - **Lahore Declaration, Feb 1999** with Delhi–Lahore **bus diplomacy**.
[148:2:5] - **Kargil 1999**: first conflict after both had tested nuclear weapons; US pressure made Pakistan withdraw.
[148:2:6] TABLE head: Indo-US civil nuclear deal | Date
  [148:2:6.0] Hyde Act | 2006
  [148:2:6.1] NSG waiver | 6 Sept 2008
  [148:2:6.2] 123 Agreement signed | Oct 2008
[148:2:7] # Multi-alignment
[148:2:8] - Since 2008 the world moves to multipolarity → **issue-based alignment**: US (security, technology), Russia (defence, energy).
[148:2:9] TABLE head: Platform | Key fact
  [148:2:9.0] Quad | India, US, Japan, Australia; formed 2007, revived 2017
  [148:2:9.1] SCO | Full member 2017
  [148:2:9.2] BRICS | Founding member; India chaired 2026: New Delhi Declaration backed UN reform, opposed one-sided sanctions (Sep 2026)
  [148:2:9.3] Act East | Upgraded from Look East, 2014
  [148:2:9.4] Neighbourhood First | 2014
  [148:2:9.5] G20 Presidency | Dec 2022–Nov 2023; "One Earth, One Family, One Future"; African Union made permanent member
[148:2:10] - **India-UK CETA** signed July 2025 (PM's UK visit). First **Voice of Global South Summit**: **January 2023**.
[148:2:11] # Terms
[148:2:12] TABLE head: Term | Meaning
  [148:2:12.0] Strategic autonomy | Judge each issue on merits without military blocs; ≠ neutrality
  [148:2:12.1] Multi-alignment | Working with rival powers at once (Quad + BRICS/SCO)
  [148:2:12.2] Issue-based coalitions | Partners by issue, not fixed alliances
  [148:2:12.3] Global South voice | Reformed multilateralism, climate finance, DPI
[148:2:13] - **Contemporary policy with neighbours** = Neighbourhood First, Look/Act East via Myanmar, SAARC, Panchsheel; **non-alignment** is a Cold War bloc policy, not a neighbourhood policy (CDS 2015).
[148:2:14] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.1-3; Spectrum p.787-788; app notes 2:148 sub 4, 5, 7
## SUB 3 | Cold War and World-Order Concepts
[148:3:0] - **Cold War**: decades-long US–Soviet rivalry (1947–91) – anti-communist suspicion, arms race, brink of nuclear war (Cuban Missile Crisis 1962); not the "Space Race" or "Missile Crisis" alone.
[148:3:1] - **Truman Doctrine (1947)**: US aid to Greece and Turkey to **contain the USSR** (containment) – not farm output or the UN.
[148:3:2] - **Hegemony**: the dominant or preponderant position of one state over others (caucus = party meeting; demagogue = rabble-rouser; gerrymander = rigging constituency boundaries).
[148:3:3] - **Age of Enlightenment** (18th c.): society can be improved through the **use of reason** (not religion, realism or idealism).
[148:3:4] - **Post-Cold War order (after 1991)**: US-led liberal order ("end of history") → today multipolarity, minilaterals (Quad, AUKUS, I2U2), geo-economic fragmentation.
[148:3:5] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth Ch89 p.860 (cold war blocs); PMF IAS International Relations p.4-6 (world order, minilaterals); hegemony, Truman Doctrine and Enlightenment: general knowledge, not checked

=== NOTES 2:149 | India-pakistan Relations – Kashmir, Terrorism, Indus Waters Treaty, Trade and Dialogue
## SUB 0 | Article 370 and Jammu and Kashmir
[149:0:0] # Article 370 – special status
[149:0:1] - **Article 370** (Part XXI, "temporary provisions") gave **special status to Jammu and Kashmir** – not Art. 365, 367, 369, 371, 372 or 373 (asked 11 times, APPSC 2012–2019).
[149:0:2] - J&K had its **own Constitution**; only defence, external affairs and communications automatically applied.
[149:0:3] - **Art. 370(3)**: the President could declare it inoperative only on the **recommendation of the Constituent Assembly of the State**.
[149:0:4] TABLE head: Event | Date
  [149:0:4.0] Article 370 operative | 17 November 1952
  [149:0:4.1] J&K Constituent Assembly adopted its Constitution | 17 November 1956
  [149:0:4.2] J&K Constitution in force | 26 January 1957
  [149:0:4.3] Article 370 abrogated (Constitution (Application to J&K) Order, 2019); J&K and Ladakh UTs | 5 August 2019
  [149:0:4.4] Supreme Court upheld abrogation | December 2023
[149:0:5] - **Pakistan's response**: downgraded diplomatic ties, suspended bilateral trade and the **Samjhauta Express**, raised it at the UN.
[149:0:6] - **Gilgit-Baltistan**: India claims it as part of J&K – a political status issue, not a border dispute.
[149:0:7] > Trap: Art. 371 = special provisions for Maharashtra/Gujarat etc.; Tenth Schedule = defections, not J&K.
[149:0:8] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Ch4 p.63, Ch6 p.101-111 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01.txt); NextGen Polity - APPSC Exams (src/polity/nextgen-polity-full.txt p.1, Art. 370); app notes 2:149 sub 1
## SUB 1 | Kashmir, Wars and Agreements
[149:1:0] # Accession and the UN
[149:1:1] - **Instrument of Accession**: **Maharaja Hari Singh**, **26 October 1947**, after the **tribal invasion**; Indian troops airlifted **27 October**.
[149:1:2] - Ceded only **defence, external affairs and communications**; land revenue stayed with the State.
[149:1:3] - Sequence: tribal invasion → accession → airlift → **First Indo-Pak war**.
[149:1:4] - **India (Nehru)** first referred Kashmir to the **UNSC** on **1 January 1948** under **Article 35** of the UN Charter – not Pakistan; **UNSC Resolution 47 (1948)**: plebiscite conditional on Pakistan's withdrawal – never held.
[149:1:5] # Wars and operations
[149:1:6] TABLE head: War | Trigger / operation | Outcome
  [149:1:6.0] 1947–48 (first Kashmir war) | Pakistan-backed tribal invasion | UN ceasefire 1 January 1949; Karachi Agreement 1949
  [149:1:6.1] 1965 | Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar, Operation Grand Slam | Tashkent Declaration 1966
  [149:1:6.2] 1971 | Bangladesh crisis; Army chief Gen. Sam Manekshaw | Pakistan surrendered 16 December 1971; Simla 1972
  [149:1:6.3] 1984 Siachen | India's Operation Meghdoot (April 1984) | Line beyond NJ9842 unmarked
  [149:1:6.4] 1999 Kargil | Pakistani intrusion; India's Operation Vijay | Pakistan withdrew under US pressure; first war between nuclear-armed states
[149:1:7] - **Navy Day, 4 December** – marks **Operation Trident**, the Indian Navy's attack on Karachi in the 1971 war.
[149:1:8] - **2003 LoC ceasefire**, reaffirmed in **2021**. 1965 was NOT the first Kashmir war – that was 1947–48.
[149:1:9] # Agreements → year and signatories
[149:1:10] TABLE head: Agreement | Year | Signatories / key point
  [149:1:10.0] Karachi Agreement | July 1949 | Military representatives under UNCIP; fixed the ceasefire line
  [149:1:10.1] Tashkent Declaration | 10 January 1966 | Shastri–Ayub Khan; Soviet mediation; Haji Pir Pass returned to Pakistan; Shastri died at Tashkent
  [149:1:10.2] Simla Agreement | 2 July 1972 | Indira Gandhi–Z.A. Bhutto; bilateral settlement, no third party; ceasefire line → LoC
  [149:1:10.3] Lahore Declaration | February 1999 | Vajpayee–Nawaz Sharif; nuclear CBMs; bus diplomacy
  [149:1:10.4] Agra Summit | July 2001 | Vajpayee–Pervez Musharraf; no joint declaration
[149:1:11] - Tashkent did NOT create the LoC – Simla (1972) did. Simla: signed **2 July 1972** (not June 2; talks began late June).
[149:1:12] # Composite Dialogue and disputed places
[149:1:13] - **Composite Dialogue**: agreed **1997** → restarted **2004** → stopped after **26/11 (2008)**.
[149:1:14] - **Eight baskets**: peace and security/CBMs; J&K; Siachen; **Wullar Barrage/Tulbul**; Sir Creek; terrorism and drugs; economic cooperation; friendly exchanges – **not** nuclear disarmament.
[149:1:15] TABLE head: Place | Feature
  [149:1:15.0] Sir Creek | 96-km tidal estuary, Rann of Kutch, between Gujarat and Sindh; Pakistan: 1914 map line; India: mid-channel thalweg rule; unsettled
  [149:1:15.1] Siachen | Saltoro Ridge held since Operation Meghdoot; line beyond NJ9842 unmarked
[149:1:16] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.694-696 (Tashkent), p.727-729 (1971, Manekshaw, Simla 2 July), p.787 (Lahore, Kargil); PMF IAS International Relations p.18 (Simla, Siachen, Sir Creek); app notes 2:149 sub 0, 2, 3, 4; Navy Day: general knowledge, not checked

[149:2:7] - **FATF grey list** (increased monitoring): Pakistan **June 2018 → October 2022**.
[149:2:8] # Pakistan in the news (asked as current affairs)
[149:2:9] - **Pervez Musharraf**: escaped two assassination bids in **Rawalpindi** (14 and 25 December 2003); sentenced to **death for high treason** by a special court, **December 2019** (died 2023).
[149:2:10] - **Kulbhushan Jadhav** case at the **ICJ**: India argued by **Harish Salve**; ICJ ruled for India (July 2019 – consular access).
[149:2:11] - **January 2003**: Pakistan expelled four Indian mission staff incl. **Vipin Handa** (tit-for-tat).

## SUB 3 | Indus Waters Treaty 1960
[149:3:0] - Signed at **Karachi, 19 September 1960** by **Nehru and President Ayub Khan**; broker: **World Bank** (APPSC G2 2017).
[149:3:1] TABLE head: Rivers | Allotted to
  [149:3:1.0] Eastern: Ravi, Beas, Sutlej | India
  [149:3:1.1] Western: Indus, Jhelum, Chenab | Pakistan (India: domestic use, agriculture, run-of-river hydropower, limited storage)
[149:3:2] - Pakistan gets about **80%** (80.52%) of the waters, India about **20%** (19.48%); no aquifer or drought clause.
[149:3:3] - **Permanent Indus Commission**: one Commissioner from each country.
[149:3:4] TABLE head: Article IX level | Handled by
  [149:3:4.0] "Questions" | PIC
  [149:3:4.1] "Differences" | Neutral Expert
  [149:3:4.2] "Disputes" | Court of Arbitration
[149:3:5] - No hierarchy → World Bank appointed both for **Kishanganga and Ratle**.
[149:3:6] # Abeyance (2025) and after
[149:3:7] - After Pahalgam the **CCS** put the Treaty "**in abeyance**" from **23 April 2025** – until Pakistan "**credibly and irrevocably**" abjures cross-border terrorism. First ever suspension; the Treaty has no abeyance clause.
[149:3:8] - Effects: India stops sharing flow data; storage on western rivers; Chenab projects **Kirthai-II (930 MW)** and **Sawalkote (1,856 MW)** (Jun 2026).
[149:3:9] - **Jul 2026**: India sent a formal notice to renegotiate. **Aug–Sep 2026**: PCA Court of Arbitration (The Hague), **Ratle** case: Treaty "remains in force"; India **rejected** it – "**no jurisdiction**" (1 Sep 2026).
[149:3:10] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.18-19; app notes 2:149 sub 8
## SUB 4 | Trade and Connectivity
[149:4:0] - **Kartarpur Corridor**: agreement (MoU) **October 2019**; inaugurated by **PM Modi**, **9 November 2019**, **Guru Nanak's 550th birth anniversary**; **4.7-km visa-free** corridor from **Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur)** to **Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur (Narowal)**.
[149:4:1] - Agreement renewed for 5 years in **October 2024**; India closed the corridor in **May 2025** after Operation Sindoor; still closed (Apr 2026).
[149:4:2] - **MFN**: granted to Pakistan **1996**; withdrawn **February 2019** after Pulwama with **200% customs duty**; Pakistan never reciprocated. After Pahalgam: ban on all imports from Pakistan.
[149:4:3] - **Samjhauta Express** (Attari–Lahore): started **1976** after Simla; suspended 2019.
[149:4:4] - **Wagah–Attari**: main land trade route. After Pahalgam India closed the **Attari ICP**, revoked SAARC visa-exemption and cut High Commission strength **55 → 35**.
[149:4:5] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.19-20 (Kartarpur 4.7 km, MFN, import ban); app notes 2:149 sub 7

=== NOTES 2:150 | India-china Relations – Boundary, Lac, Trade and Neighbourhood
## SUB 0 | Belt and Road Initiative and Encirclement
[150:0:0] - **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)** = **One Belt One Road (OBOR)**, "21st Century Silk Road": proposed by **China's Xi Jinping, 2013** (UPSC 2016, 2018; asked 5 times) – land "Belt" + Maritime Silk "Road".
[150:0:1] - **India's objection**: **CPEC** passes through **PoJK** → India boycotted the **Belt and Road Forum (May 2017)** on **territorial sovereignty** grounds (not finance); India (June 2018): connectivity projects must respect **sovereignty and territorial integrity**.
[150:0:2] - **String of Pearls**: China's network of **military and commercial facilities** (ports) around India in the Indian Ocean – not Japanese or Pakistani.
[150:0:3] TABLE head: Port | Country
  [150:0:3.0] Hambantota | Sri Lanka
  [150:0:3.1] Gwadar | Pakistan
  [150:0:3.2] Chittagong | Bangladesh
  [150:0:3.3] Kyaukphyu | Myanmar
[150:0:4] - Military ties: **Hand-in-Hand** – India-China anti-terror army exercise, first **2007, Kunming**. China-Pakistan exercises: **Warrior** (army), **Shaheen** (air force), **Sea Guardian** (navy; first January 2020, Arabian Sea).
[150:0:5] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.5-6 (BRI), p.24-25 (String of Pearls), p.18 (CPEC through PoK); app notes 2:150 sub 6
## SUB 1 | Boundary, LAC and Arunachal
[150:1:0] - India recognised the **PRC** on **30 December 1949**; ties from **1 April 1950** – **first non-socialist-bloc** country to do so.
[150:1:1] TABLE head: Line | Origin | Position
  [150:1:1.0] Johnson Line | 1865, W.H. Johnson | Aksai Chin in Ladakh – India's claim
  [150:1:1.1] Macartney-MacDonald Line | 1899 | Aksai Chin under China – China's preferred
  [150:1:1.2] McMahon Line | Simla Convention 1914, Henry McMahon | Eastern Tibet-India boundary; China rejects
[150:1:2] - China occupies ~**38,000 sq km** in Aksai Chin; claims ~**90,000 sq km** in the north-east (most of **Arunachal**, "South Tibet").
[150:1:3] - **Shaksgam Valley** (Trans-Karakoram Tract): ceded by Pakistan to China, **1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement** (after the war, not a cause); fresh dispute **January 2026**.
[150:1:4] - **Arunachal**: China denied visas to Arunachal members of India's delegation to the **Fourth World Conference on Women, Beijing 1995**; the **USA** reaffirmed Arunachal as part of India.
[150:1:5] - **Diphu Pass** (Arunachal): the **India–China–Myanmar tri-junction**.
[150:1:6] # LAC sectors (3,488 km)
[150:1:7] TABLE head: Sector | States / UT | Note
  [150:1:7.0] Western | Ladakh | Aksai Chin; most standoffs
  [150:1:7.1] Middle | Himachal, Uttarakhand | Least contested
  [150:1:7.2] Eastern | Sikkim, Arunachal | McMahon Line

=== NOTES 2:151 | India and Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Maldives, Afghanistan
## SUB 0 | Myanmar, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan
[151:0:0] # Myanmar
[151:0:1] - **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** (conceived 2008): **Kolkata → Sittwe port (Myanmar) → Kaladan river and road → Mizoram** – with **Myanmar** (APPSC 2018).
[151:0:2] - **India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway** (~1,360 km): **Moreh (Manipur)–Bagan–Mae Sot (Thailand)**.
[151:0:3] - **Military coup, 1 February 2021** – Senior General **Min Aung Hlaing**; India engages the junta for Act East and north-east security.
[151:0:4] - Burma joined the UN in 1948 and stayed neutral – refused to name China the aggressor in the Korean War (NDA 2019). **Kyaiktiyo (Golden Rock) pagoda** is in Myanmar.
[151:0:5] # Bhutan
[151:0:6] - **Treaty of Friendship 1949**, revised **2007** – removed the clause that Bhutan be "**guided**" by India in **foreign affairs**.
[151:0:7] - India **imports hydropower from Bhutan** (APPSC G2 2017): Chukha, Tala, **Mangdechhu (720 MW, inaugurated 2019)**, Punatsangchhu I and II.
[151:0:8] - **Doklam (2017)** – India-Bhutan-China tri-junction.
[151:0:9] # Maldives
[151:0:10] - Smallest neighbour (≈300 sq km). **Operation Cactus (1988)** – India foiled a coup.
[151:0:11] - **Sheikh Imran Abdulla** – Home Minister, visited India February 2020. "**India Out**" campaign → ties repaired; PM visited 2025; **Favara** linked with **UPI** (Aug 2026); **Greater Male Connectivity** = bridge-causeway (not a tunnel); India built the **Institute of Security and Law Enforcement Studies**.
[151:0:12] # Afghanistan
[151:0:13] - **Salma Dam** (Afghan-India Friendship Dam, 42 MW), **Hari Rud, Herat** – inaugurated by Modi and Ghani, **June 2016**.
[151:0:14] - **Zaranj–Delaram highway** (218 km, **BRO**); **Afghan Parliament building** (Modi, 2015); **Stor Palace** restored with the **Aga Khan Trust for Culture** (2016); India-funded **public library** (Kabul, in news Jan 2019).
[151:0:15] - Nehru visited Kabul (Sept 1959). After the **Taliban takeover (Aug 2021)**: wheat, medicines, vaccines; **technical team in Kabul (2022)**.
[151:0:16] # Operations → country

## SUB 1 | Bangladesh
[151:1:0] # Land boundary
[151:1:1] - **Longest land border**: Bangladesh **4,096.7 km** (then China 3,488, Pakistan 3,323, Nepal 1,751, Myanmar 1,643, Bhutan 699, Afghanistan ~106 – shortest).
[151:1:2] - **Land Boundary Agreement**: signed **1974** (Indira–Mujib); ratified by the **100th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2015**: **111 Indian enclaves → Bangladesh**, **51 Bangladeshi enclaves → India** (162 in all); **6.1 km** undemarcated boundary settled; territory of **four States** (Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya, Tripura) changed.
[151:1:3] - **Tin Bigha**: corridor **leased** to Bangladesh in **1992** for access to **Dahagram-Angarpota** enclaves (UPSC 1999: Kachchativu and Tin Bigha were handed to Sri Lanka and Bangladesh respectively).
[151:1:4] - **Dawki (Meghalaya)–Tamabil (Sylhet)** – India–**Bangladesh** border crossing (not China).
[151:1:5] - **Border haat** at **Bholaganj** (Companiganj, Sylhet) inaugurated **May 2023**.
[151:1:6] # Ties and connectivity
[151:1:7] - **Maitri Diwas – 6 December**: India **recognised Bangladesh on 6 December 1971**.
[151:1:8] - **Maitri Express** Kolkata–Dhaka: launched **April 2008**.
[151:1:9] - **July 2020**: first container ship **Kolkata → Agartala** via **Chattogram (Chittagong) port**.
[151:1:10] - Water: **Farakka Accord 1977**; **Ganga Water Treaty 1996** (Farakka, **30 years**, Gujral Doctrine); **Teesta** still unsettled.
[151:1:11] - **Akhaura–Agartala** rail link; **Friendship Pipeline** (diesel); **Rooppur** (nuclear, Russia-built) and **Maitree** (thermal, Rampal).
[151:1:12] - Politics: **two-party system** – Awami League vs BNP (UPSC 1996 key); after the 2024 upheaval, **Tarique Rahman (BNP)** government sworn in **February 2026** (Speaker Om Birla represented India). Rohingya refugee issue (from Myanmar).
[151:1:13] > Trap: under the LBA India **received** 51 enclaves and **transferred 111** – "India transferred 51 enclaves" is false.

## SUB 2 | Sri Lanka
[151:2:0] - **Indo-Sri Lanka Accord, 1987**: **Rajiv Gandhi–J.R. Jayewardene**; merger of **Northern and Eastern** provinces; **13th Amendment** (provincial councils); **IPKF (Operation Pawan)** – ended up fighting the LTTE; withdrawn on **V.P. Singh**'s order (last troops **24 March 1990**).
[151:2:1] - **LTTE** killed **Rajiv Gandhi (1991)** → India banned it **1992** (not part of the 1987 Accord). Banned also by **Sri Lanka and the USA** (UPPSC 1998: India, Sri Lanka, USA). **2009**: Sri Lankan Army crushed the LTTE; chief **V. Prabhakaran** killed.
[151:2:2] - **Katchatheevu** ceded to Sri Lanka in **1974**; fishermen issue.
[151:2:3] - Leaders: **Chandrika Kumaratunga** – first woman **President** (1994); Sirimavo Bandaranaike – world's first woman **PM** (1960). **Mahinda Rajapaksa** became PM in **November 2019** (brother Gotabaya – President).
[151:2:4] - In the news: banned **drones and unmanned aircraft** after the **Easter Sunday bombings (April 2019)**; waived tourist-visa fee for **48 countries** (2019); **Colombo** – largest city; Knuckles range is in Sri Lanka.
[151:2:5] - India's aid: economic crisis support **~$4 billion (2022)**; **KKS (Kankesanthurai)** port; **Dickoya district hospital**; DTAA protocol (2020). **Hambantota** = Chinese, not Pakistani, encirclement.

## SUB 3 | Nepal
[151:3:0] - **Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950**: open border, security cooperation; Nepal seeks revision.
[151:3:1] - **First Constituent Assembly** abolished the monarchy – **28 May 2008**; new Constitution **20 September 2015**.
[151:3:2] - **Dr. Ram Baran Yadav** – **first (elected) President**, July 2008 (not G.P. Koirala or Paramananda Jha, the first Vice-President).
[151:3:3] - **Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda'** (UCPN-Maoist) – **first PM** of the Federal Democratic Republic, August 2008.
[151:3:4] - **K.P. Sharma Oli** – PM for the **third time** in 2021 (APPSC Endowment 2022); fourth term July 2024 – September 2025 (fell in the Gen-Z protests; **Sushila Karki** interim PM).
[151:3:5] - **March 2026**: **Balen Shah** (Rastriya Swatantra Party) became Nepal's **youngest PM (35)**; youth-led government pushes to revise the 1950 Treaty.
[151:3:6] - Water: **Kosi (1954)**, **Gandak (1959)**, **Mahakali Treaty 1996** (Sarada, Tanakpur, **Pancheshwar**) – Nepal, not Bangladesh; Arun III; hydro potential **83,000 MW**.
[151:3:7] - Dispute: **Kalapani–Limpiyadhura–Lipulekh** (Sugauli Treaty 1816; Nepal's new map 2020).
[151:3:8] - **Operation Maitri** – India's **earthquake relief, 2015**.
[151:3:9] - **First trilateral power deal**: Nepal supplies Bangladesh through the **Indian grid**.

## SUB 2 | Status and US Doctrines
[153:2:0] - Present status: **Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership**.
[153:2:1] - The **2008 civil nuclear deal** = turning point in India-US ties.
[153:2:2] TABLE head: Doctrine / law | Year | Purpose
  [153:2:2.0] Pressler Amendment | 1985 | Stopped US aid to Pakistan unless the President certified it had no nuclear device; applied in 1990
  [153:2:2.1] Pivot to Asia / Rebalance | 2011 (Obama era) | USA's foreign-policy shift of focus to the Asia-Pacific
  [153:2:2.2] CAATSA | 2017 | Sanctions on buyers of Russian arms; India sought a waiver over the S-400
[153:2:3] - **Larry Pressler** = US Senator; linked aid to non-proliferation; **criticised the proposed US military help to Pakistan** (Clinton era) over its nuclear programme.
[153:2:4] > Exam angle: Pressler targeted Pakistan, not India; 'Pivot to Asia' is a US plan.

## SUB 3 | Diaspora and Visas
[153:3:0] - US has the world's **largest PIO community** (Malaysia second) (Feb 2026).
[153:3:1] - 2020 Census: about **4.4 million** "Indian-alone" – largest Asian-alone group.
[153:3:2] - **Remittances**: US is the largest source – **27.7%** (RBI survey, 2023-24), ahead of the UAE.
[153:3:3] - **Telugu** = fastest-growing foreign language in the US (2010-17).
[153:3:4] - **Dalip Singh Saund:** first **Indian American** (and first Asian American) elected to the US Congress – House of Representatives, California, **1956**.
[153:3:5] - **Pramila Jayapal** (Washington, 2016): **first Indian-American woman elected to the US House of Representatives** (Kamala Harris – Senate, then Vice President; Ami Bera – a man).
[153:3:6] - **H-1B**: **June 2023** (PM Modi's state visit) – the **US** announced **in-country renewal** of H-1B visas (pilot); **$100,000 fee** on new petitions from **21 Sept 2025**; Indians get about **71%** of approved H-1Bs.
[153:3:7] ~~ Sources: app notes 2:153 sub 4, 7; general knowledge for Jayapal and the 2023 H-1B renewal (not checked)
## SUB 4 | Civil Nuclear Cooperation
[153:4:0] - Order: **Hyde Act 2006** (signed **18 December 2006**; made the deal possible under US law) → **123 Agreement 2008** → **NSG clean waiver, Sept 2008** (allowed civil nuclear trade).

=== NOTES 2:154 | India-russia, India-eu, India-japan, India-israel, India-gulf and India-africa Relations
## SUB 0 | India-Japan
[154:0:0] - Status: **Special Strategic and Global Partnership**.
[154:0:1] - **First India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue: New Delhi, 30 November 2019**.
[154:0:2] - **Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail** – Japan's **Shinkansen** technology, Japanese **ODA**.
[154:0:3] - Act East Forum; **ACSA** (Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement) – **2020**.
[154:0:4] - **15th Summit** (2025): **10 trillion yen** (~$67 bn) over ten years; 16th Summit 2026.
[154:0:5] - Trade **$27.47 bn** (2025-26); Japan = **5th-largest** FDI source (not the largest).
[154:0:6] - Culture: **Shintoism** = indigenous religion of **Japan**; **Ikebana** = Japanese art of **flower arrangement** (origami = paper folding, bonsai = miniature trees).
[154:0:7] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes (src/international-relations/pmf-international-relations.txt) pdf p.69-70; app notes 2:154 sub 4; general knowledge for the 2019 2+2 venue, Shinto and Ikebana (not checked)
## SUB 1 | India-Gulf and Iran
[154:1:0] - **UAE**: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (**2017**); **3rd-largest** trading partner (over $100 bn); **first foreign investor** in India's **SPR at Mangaluru**.
[154:1:1] - **Republic Day 2017**: chief guest Abu Dhabi Crown Prince; a **UAE armed forces contingent led the parade** – first foreign contingent after France (2016).
[154:1:2] - **Saudi Arabia**: Strategic Partnership Council (**2019**); PM **Modi** received Saudi Arabia's highest civilian award, the **Order of King Abdulaziz (April 2016)**.
[154:1:3] - **IMEC** (G20 New Delhi, **Sept 2023**): east (India-Gulf) + northern (Gulf-Europe) corridors.
[154:1:4] - **Oman CEPA**: signed Dec 2025, in force **1 June 2026**; 99% duty-free; India's **2nd** GCC CEPA after UAE. India-GCC FTA talks on (2026).
[154:1:5] - **Remittances:** **UAE** = India's **second-largest** source – 19.2%, after the US (27.7%) (RBI survey, 2023-24).
[154:1:6] - **Iran** = predominantly **Shia** (Twelver Shia state religion, about 90% of Muslims); Iraq also Shia-majority but less so; Pakistan, Afghanistan Sunni-majority.
[154:1:7] > Exam angle: UAE is the 3rd-largest (not 2nd-largest) trading partner but the 2nd-largest remittance source.
[154:1:8] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.90; app notes 2:154 sub 0, 5; general knowledge for the 2016 Saudi award, 2017 Republic Day and Iran (not checked)
## SUB 2 | India-Israel and the Arab-Israeli Question
[154:2:0] - Full diplomatic relations: **1992**, **P.V. Narasimha Rao** government.
[154:2:1] - **Narendra Modi** = first Indian PM to visit Israel (**2017**); visited twice by March 2026.
[154:2:2] - Status: **Special Strategic Partnership**; **defence (incl. joint R&D)** = main pillar.
[154:2:3] - **Indo-Israel Centres of Excellence**: AP centre at **Kuppam** – vegetables and flowers.
[154:2:4] - Bilateral Investment Agreement – Sept 2025; FTA Terms of Reference – Nov 2025; trade $3.75 bn (2024-25).
[154:2:5] - **I2U2** = India, Israel, **UAE**, USA.
[154:2:6] - **Abraham Accords (2020)**: Israel normalised ties with Arab States – **UAE**, **Bahrain**, Morocco, Sudan – so "Israel has diplomatic relations with some Arab States" is true (Egypt 1979, Jordan 1994 earlier).
[154:2:7] - **Arab Peace Initiative (2002)**: a **Saudi proposal endorsed by the Arab League** (Beirut summit) – **never signed by Israel**.
[154:2:8] - **Yom Kippur War (October 1973)**: **Israel vs Arab states led by Egypt and Syria**.
[154:2:9] - **Yair Lapid** became Israel's **14th Prime Minister** on 1 July 2022 (caretaker, after Naftali Bennett).
[154:2:10] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.84, p.86; app notes 2:154 sub 1; general knowledge for the Arab Peace Initiative, Yom Kippur War and Lapid (not checked)

[154:4:9] - **INSTC**: sea from Mumbai to **Bandar Abbas** (Iran), then road/rail through Iran and the Caspian region to Russia; Chabahar being linked.

=== NOTES 2:155 | United Nations – Principal Organs, Unga, Unsc and Reform; India's Candidature
## SUB 0 | Security Council
[155:0:0] - **15 members**: **5 permanent (P5) – China, France, Russia, UK, USA** + **10 non-permanent**.
[155:0:1] - Non-permanent members: elected by the **UNGA**, two-thirds secret ballot, for **2 years**; **no immediate re-election (Art. 23)**.
[155:0:2] - **Veto (Art. 27)**: only the P5; a P5 negative vote on a **substantive** matter blocks a decision; **procedural matters need 9 affirmative votes and no veto applies**. The Charter never uses the word "veto" (Art. 27(3) speaks of the "concurring votes of the permanent members").
[155:0:3] - **Germany, Japan, India, Canada are NOT** permanent members; India has been an elected (non-permanent) member, never a permanent one.
[155:0:4] - Only organ whose decisions **bind** all members (Ch. VII: Art. 41 sanctions, Art. 42 military action).
[155:0:5] - **P5 + 1** (Iran nuclear talks, JCPOA 2015): the **+1 = Germany**.
[155:0:6] - Resolutions: **2328 (Dec 2016)** – UN monitors for evacuations from **Aleppo** (Syria); **2428 (July 2018)** – arms embargo on **South Sudan**.
[155:0:7] - **April 2024**: full UN membership for **Palestine** – **vetoed by the USA**; UK and Switzerland abstained.
[155:0:8] TABLE head: Resolution | Year | Subject
  [155:0:8.0] 1267 | 1999 | Sanctions on Al-Qaida / ISIL; terrorist listings (Masood Azhar listed 2019)
  [155:0:8.1] 1373 | 2001 | Counter-Terrorism Committee (after 9/11)
  [155:0:8.2] 1540 | 2004 | Stopping WMD reaching non-state actors
[155:0:9] - AP angle: India's first **UNSCR 1540** capacity-building programme for Asia-Pacific – **NACIN, Palasamudram (AP)**, Feb 2025.
[155:0:10] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes (src/international-relations/pmf-international-relations.txt) pdf p.141, p.144-145; PMF IR notes pdf p.86 (JCPOA, P5+1); app notes 2:155 sub 2, 4; general knowledge for resolutions 2328 and 2428 (not checked)
## SUB 1 | Charter, Founding, Languages and UN Days
[155:1:0] - **Atlantic Charter (1941)** → **Declaration by United Nations (1 Jan 1942)** – name "United Nations" devised by US President **Franklin D. Roosevelt**.
[155:1:1] - Charter signed by **50 nations** at the **San Francisco Conference**, **26 June 1945**; **Poland** signed later (ratified 16 Oct 1945) as the **51st original member**.
[155:1:2] - In force **24 October 1945** = **UN founded** = **UN Day**.
[155:1:3] - Members: **193**.
[155:1:4] - **Six official languages**: **Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish**. **Working languages** (Secretariat): **English and French**. **Hindi is NOT** an official UN language.
[155:1:5] - **UNGA resolution on multilingualism (June 2022, India co-sponsored)**: mentioned **Hindi** for the first time (also Bangla and Urdu).
[155:1:6] - **Amendment** (e.g. UNSC reform): **two-thirds** of members, incl. ratification by **all P5** (Art. 108).
[155:1:7] TABLE head: Article | Provision
  [155:1:7.0] Art. 1 | Purposes – peace and security, friendly relations, cooperation, harmonising action
  [155:1:7.1] Art. 2 | Sovereign equality
  [155:1:7.2] Art. 18 | UNGA "important questions" = two-thirds majority
  [155:1:7.3] Art. 23 | No immediate re-election of a retiring non-permanent UNSC member
  [155:1:7.4] Art. 27 | Voting in the UNSC; P5 veto
[155:1:8] - **UN Decade of Sustainable Energy for All (2014–2024)**: declared by the **UN General Assembly**.
[155:1:9] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.141, p.146; app notes 2:155 sub 0; general knowledge for Roosevelt, the 2022 multilingualism resolution and the SE4All decade (not checked)
## SUB 2 | International Court of Justice
[155:2:0] - **Principal judicial organ**; seat **The Hague** (Netherlands) – the only principal organ outside New York.
[155:2:1] - **15 judges**, **9-year** terms (one-third elected every three years); elected by the **UNGA and UNSC voting separately** (absolute majority in both).
[155:2:2] - Indian judges: **B.N. Rau**, **Nagendra Singh** (ICJ President **1985-88**), **R.S. Pathak**, **Dalveer Bhandari**.
[155:2:3] - **Dalveer Bhandari**: elected **27 April 2012** (remaining term to Feb 2018); **re-elected** (second time) from 6 Feb 2018 for nine years.
[155:2:4] - **Kulbhushan Jadhav case (2019)**: ICJ **stayed his execution**; Pakistan breached the **Vienna Convention on Consular Relations**; review of conviction ordered.
[155:2:5] - **July 2025**: unanimous **advisory opinion on climate** obligations.
[155:2:6] > Exam angle: 15 = UNSC members and ICJ judges; 9 = ICJ term; 54 = ECOSOC.
[155:2:7] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.141, p.147; app notes 2:155 sub 8
## SUB 3 | Principal Organs, General Assembly and ECOSOC
[155:3:0] - **Six principal organs**: **General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, Secretariat**. Amnesty International is an NGO, not a UN organ.
[155:3:1] TABLE head: Organ | Composition / mandate
  [155:3:1.0] General Assembly | All 193 members, one vote each – the "World Parliament"; meets in annual regular session
  [155:3:1.1] Security Council | 15 members; binding decisions
  [155:3:1.2] ECOSOC | 54 members, 3-year terms, elected by the UNGA (two-thirds majority, Art. 18)
  [155:3:1.3] Trusteeship Council | Inactive since 1994, after Palau became self-governing
  [155:3:1.4] ICJ | Judicial organ, The Hague
  [155:3:1.5] Secretariat | Headed by the Secretary-General
[155:3:2] - **UDHR (10 Dec 1948)** = a **UN General Assembly resolution (217 A)** – not a treaty.
[155:3:3] - UNGA: important questions need two-thirds (Art. 18); **Credentials Committee** – **9** members each session.
[155:3:4] - **Uniting for Peace (Res. 377), 1950**: lets the UNGA act when a veto blocks the UNSC; first used in the **1956 Suez Crisis** to send peacekeepers.
[155:3:5] - Emergency special sessions: the 10th – resolution ES-10/23 (10 May 2024) upgraded Palestine's rights as an observer State.
[155:3:6] - **Non-member observer States** (2): **Holy See** (since 1964) and **State of Palestine** (2012).
[155:3:7] - **Sweden** (Oct 2014) – first EU member state (while a member) to officially recognise the State of Palestine.
[155:3:8] - **Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit** – President of the 8th UNGA (1953), the first woman (and first Indian) to hold the post.
[155:3:9] - **81st UNGA President** (2026-27): **Khalilur Rahman** (Bangladesh).
[155:3:10] - 22 May 2026 climate resolution: India abstained (141-8-28).
[155:3:11] # ECOSOC functional commissions
[155:3:12] - **Commission on the Status of Women** (**1946**) – CSW-70 held 2026.
[155:3:13] - **Commission on Sustainable Development** – reviewed **Agenda 21** and the Rio Declaration; replaced by the **High-Level Political Forum** in **2013**.
[155:3:14] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.141, p.146-148; app notes 2:155 sub 1, 3; general knowledge for UDHR res. 217 A and Sweden 2014 (not checked)
## SUB 4 | Secretaries-General
[155:4:0] TABLE head: # | Secretary-General | Country | Tenure
  [155:4:0.0] 1 | Trygve Lie (first) | Norway | 1946-52
  [155:4:0.1] 2 | Dag Hammarskjold | Sweden | 1953-61
  [155:4:0.2] 3 | U Thant (first Asian) | Burma | Nov 1961-Dec 1971 – longest tenure (about 10 years 2 months)
  [155:4:0.3] 4 | Kurt Waldheim | Austria | 1972-81
  [155:4:0.4] 5 | Javier Perez de Cuellar (first Latin American) | Peru | 1982-91
  [155:4:0.5] 6 | Boutros Boutros-Ghali (first African/Arab) | Egypt | 1992-96
  [155:4:0.6] 7 | Kofi Annan (second African) | Ghana | 1997-2006
  [155:4:0.7] 8 | Ban Ki-moon | South Korea | 2007-16
  [155:4:0.8] 9 | Antonio Guterres (former PM of Portugal) | Portugal | from 1 Jan 2017
[155:4:1] - Present SG: **Guterres** (second term ends 31 Dec 2026). Next SG selection under way: four candidates (two women) addressed the UNGA, 21-22 April 2026.
[155:4:2] - The SG is **appointed by the UNGA on the recommendation of the UNSC**.

## SUB 5 | India at the UN
[155:5:0] - **Founding member**: signed the Charter as **British India** (June 1945).
[155:5:1] - **Eight UNSC terms**: 1950-51, 1967-68, 1972-73, 1977-78, 1984-85, 1991-92, 2011-12, 2021-22. Bid for **2028-29** launched by EAM Jaishankar, 13 July 2026.
[155:5:2] - **First Hindi speech** at the UNGA: **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, as External Affairs Minister, **4 October 1977**.
[155:5:3] - **International Day of Yoga** (21 June): UNGA res. **69/131**, 11 Dec 2014, **177** co-sponsors.
[155:5:4] TABLE head: Permanent Representative (New York) | Period
  [155:5:4.0] T.S. Tirumurti | May 2020 – June 2022
  [155:5:4.1] Ruchira Kamboj (first woman; earlier PR to UNESCO, Paris) | Aug 2022 – May 2024
  [155:5:4.2] Parvathaneni Harish | From Sept 2024 (present, 2026)
[155:5:5] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.145; app notes 2:155 sub 7
## SUB 6 | UNSC Reform
[155:6:0] TABLE head: Group | Members / demand
  [155:6:0.0] G4 | Brazil, Germany, India, Japan – support each other's permanent seats, plus seats for Africa (China is not in it – already P5)
  [155:6:0.1] Uniting for Consensus ("Coffee Club") | Led by Italy; includes Pakistan; opposes new permanent seats
  [155:6:0.2] L.69 | Developing countries of Asia, Africa, Latin America, Pacific; India a member
  [155:6:0.3] Ezulwini Consensus (2005) | African Union: 2 permanent seats with veto + 5 non-permanent
[155:6:1] - G4 model: expand the UNSC from 15 to 25–26.
[155:6:2] - **IGN** (Inter-Governmental Negotiations): informal **UNGA** process, set up **2008**; annual "Elements Paper". India demands text-based negotiations (June 2026).
[155:6:3] - **China** opposes India's permanent seat.
[155:6:4] ~~ Sources: PMF IR notes pdf p.144, p.146; app notes 2:155 sub 5

## SUB 1 | UNESCO – Lists, Prizes and Membership
[156:1:0] - **Members**: **194** Member States + 12 Associate Members (2025-26). **Palestine** became the **195th** member in **October 2011** (South Sudan the 194th, days earlier); the US announced its withdrawal again in July 2025.
[156:1:1] - **Executive Board**: **58** members; India re-elected in **November 2021** for **four years** (2021-25).
[156:1:2] - **First woman Director-General**: **Irina Bokova** (Bulgaria), 2009. Now **Khaled El-Enany** (Egypt) – from **15 Nov 2025**; first Arab DG.
[156:1:3] - Programmes: **Information for All Programme (IFAP)**; **Man and the Biosphere (MAB)**; Memory of the World (1992); leads **SDG-4** (Education 2030).
[156:1:4] - **Kalinga Prize** for the popularisation of science – awarded by **UNESCO** (since 1952).
[156:1:5] - **Delors Commission** report to UNESCO (1996): "**Learning: The Treasure Within**" (four pillars of learning).
[156:1:6] - **World Capital of Architecture** (UNESCO + UIA): **Rio de Janeiro, 2020** – the first.

## SUB 2 | Mandates, Programmes and Reports
[156:2:0] # Who does what
[156:2:1] TABLE head: Body | Mandate / programme
  [156:2:1.0] UNICEF | Children's rights and well-being; first UN body to hold and transact in cryptocurrency (UNICEF Cryptocurrency Fund, October 2019); Danny Kaye Humanitarian Award – Priyanka Chopra (Dec 2019)
  [156:2:1.1] FAO | Food and agriculture; launched the "Freedom from Hunger" campaign (1960)
  [156:2:1.2] WFP | World's largest humanitarian agency against hunger; funded entirely by voluntary contributions; India's five-year rice supply deal (2026)
  [156:2:1.3] IFAD | Both a specialised agency and an international financial institution for the rural poor
  [156:2:1.4] UNHCR | Refugees
  [156:2:1.5] UNEP | Climate, biodiversity, pollution
  [156:2:1.6] UNDP | Development and poverty; co-builds the Global MPI with OPHI
  [156:2:1.7] UNFPA | Population; State of World Population
  [156:2:1.8] UN Women | Gender equality; proposed partnering Kerala's Gender Park (Kozhikode) as a South Asia hub (2020)
  [156:2:1.9] GEF (1992) | Financial mechanism run by UNDP, UNEP and the World Bank
  [156:2:1.10] WHO | Global Centre for Traditional Medicine – Jamnagar, Gujarat (agreement with the Ministry of AYUSH, March 2022; first such centre)
[156:2:2] # ILO
[156:2:3] - **Tripartite** (governments, employers, workers) – in the International Labour Conference and the **Governing Body** (not ECOSOC). Indian industrialist **Y.K. Modi** was elected to the **ILO Governing Body** (2011, employers' group).
[156:2:4] - Conventions: India has ratified **C29, C105** (forced labour), **C100, C111** (equality), **C138, C182** (child labour, **2017**); **not** ratified **C87, C98** (freedom of association, collective bargaining) and **C189** (Domestic Workers, adopted **2011**).
[156:2:5] - Child labour (ILO-UNICEF): **160 million** (2020, released 2021); about **138 million** (2024, released 2025).

=== NOTES 2:157 | Bretton Woods Institutions – Imf (quota, Sdr), World Bank Group; Adb, Aiib, Ndb
## SUB 0 | Bretton Woods Conference and the IMF
[157:0:0] # Bretton Woods (1944)
[157:0:1] - **United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference** = **Bretton Woods Conference**, **July 1944**, Mount Washington Hotel, **Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, USA** – **44 allied nations**, 730 delegates; plans of **Harry Dexter White** (US, adopted) and **John Maynard Keynes** (UK).
[157:0:2] - Created the "Bretton Woods twins": **IMF + IBRD (World Bank)**, both HQ **Washington, D.C.**; the planned **ITO** was never born → **GATT (1947)** filled the gap until the **WTO (1995)**.
[157:0:3] - Fixed exchange rates (dollar pegged to gold); **Smithsonian Agreement (1971)** widened the band to **2.25%**, lasted about **14 months**.
[157:0:4] TABLE head: Event | Date
  [157:0:4.0] IMF and IBRD founded (conceived) | July 1944
  [157:0:4.1] IMF Articles in force – formal existence (29 members) | 27 December 1945
  [157:0:4.2] IMF began operations | 1 March 1947
  [157:0:4.3] First IMF borrower | France, 8 May 1947
  [157:0:4.4] SDR created ("paper gold") | 1967-69 (first allocation 1970)
[157:0:5] - **India** = founding member of both the IMF and the IBRD.
[157:0:6] # IMF – functions and lending
[157:0:7] - **IMF** = **International Monetary Fund** – monetary stability; **short-term balance-of-payments (BoP)** support; technical assistance; **not** project/development finance (that is the World Bank's job).
[157:0:8] - Lends **only to member countries** (UPSC 2011, MPPSC 2017) – not to "any country", not only to developed ones, not to central banks as such.
[157:0:9] - Facilities: **Stand-By Arrangement**, **Extended Fund Facility**, **Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI)** and **Rapid Credit Facility (RCF)** (urgent BoP needs; RCF concessional for low-income members), PRGT. **Political-risk guarantees** = MIGA, not IMF.
[157:0:10] - **1991 BoP crisis**: India borrowed from the **IMF** (SDR 3.56 billion) – with the World Bank about **$7 bn** in all → New Economic Policy.
[157:0:11] # Quotas, votes, SDR
[157:0:12] - **Members: 191** – Liechtenstein the 191st (21 Oct 2024); **189** in January 2020 (Nauru 190th, 2021).
[157:0:13] - **Quotas** (in SDRs) decide financial contribution, **borrowing access** and **voting power**; do **not** fix exchange rates. Formula: GDP **50%**, openness **30%**, variability **15%**, reserves **5%**.
[157:0:14] - Major decisions need **85%** of votes → the **US** (~16.5%) alone holds a **veto**. **India 8th** by quota (~2.75%).
[157:0:15] - **SDR** basket of **five** currencies since **1 October 2016**: US dollar, euro, **Chinese renminbi (yuan)** (added 2016), yen, pound.
[157:0:16] - **IMFC** advises the Board of Governors; **Article IV consultations** = regular review of each member's economy.
[157:0:17] > Trap: 27 Dec 1945 = formal existence; 1 March 1947 = operations; 1944 = founding conference. HQ = Washington, not New York.
[157:0:18] ~~ Sources: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, ch.16 p.188-190 (src/economy/ramesh-singh-indian-economy-05.txt: Bretton Woods 44 nations, July 1944, White and Keynes, twins in Washington; IMF Articles in force 27 Dec 1945; India's 1991 borrowing SDR 3.56 bn; India 8th quota 2.75%); NextGen Rocket Sheet #28 Indian Economy p.41-42 (src/economy/rocket-indian-economy.txt: formally established 27 Dec 1945, RFI, RCF, BoP); PMF IAS International Relations p.164-165 (191 members, quota formula, US veto, WEO/GFSR); NextGen Indian Economy p.21 (src/economy/nextgen-indian-economy-p1-appsc-01.txt, SDR five currencies); app notes 2:157 sub 0, 1, 2
## SUB 1 | World Bank Group
[157:1:0] - **IBRD** = the original "**World Bank**" (1944; began 1946); HQ **Washington, D.C.** (not New York, Manila, Geneva, Vienna or Brussels); gives **medium- and long-term** loans; **India a founding member**; first loan to India 1949 (Railways).
[157:1:1] TABLE head: Institution | Year | Function
  [157:1:1.0] IBRD | 1944 | Loans to middle-income governments for infrastructure, reconstruction and development
  [157:1:1.1] IFC | 1956 | Private-sector investment; conceived "Doing Business"
  [157:1:1.2] IDA | 1960 | "Soft window": interest-free credits, concessional (soft) loans and grants to the poorest; an affiliate of the World Bank, administered by the IBRD (same staff)
  [157:1:1.3] ICSID | 1966 (not 1976) | Settles investment disputes; India not a member
  [157:1:1.4] MIGA | 1988 | Political-risk insurance and guarantees (India joined 1994)
[157:1:2] - IBRD, IDA and IFC are UN specialised agencies; ICSID and MIGA are not.
[157:1:3] - **Match (UPSC 1999)**: WTO – multilateral trade negotiations; **IDA – soft loans**; **IMF – short-term BoP loans**; **IBRD – lending for reconstruction and development**.
[157:1:4] - **Aid India Consortium** (World Bank-chaired donor group, 1958) → renamed **India Development Forum**.
[157:1:5] - World Bank funds: **BioCarbon Fund Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscapes (ISFL)** – managed by the **World Bank**; **Bangladesh Road Safety Project** – **$358 million** (June 2023; Gazipur-Elenga N4, Natore-Nawabganj N6 highways).
[157:1:6] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.168-169 (World Bank founded 1944, India founding member, five institutions, India not in ICSID, 1949 Railways loan); Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, ch.16 p.191-192 (IBRD, IDA "soft window" 1960, IFC 1956, MIGA 1988, ICSID 1966); app notes 2:157 sub 1, 3; Aid India Consortium, ISFL, Bangladesh road safety loan: general knowledge, not checked

## SUB 4 | NDB, ADB and AIIB
[157:4:0] # New Development Bank (BRICS)
[157:4:1] - Idea: **4th BRICS Summit, New Delhi, 2012**. Agreement: **6th Summit, Fortaleza, Brazil, 15 July 2014** – the **Fortaleza Declaration** (BRICS, not ASEAN/OECD/WTO); operations 2015.
[157:4:2] - HQ **Shanghai, China**; regional offices Johannesburg, São Paulo, **GIFT City** (India), Moscow. First President **K.V. Kamath**.
[157:4:3] - Founders hold **equal votes; no veto**; open to all UN members. New members: Bangladesh, UAE (2021), **Egypt** (2023), Algeria (2025).
[157:4:4] - **Russia** = 20% shareholder; NDB froze Russia-linked work, March 2022. 16th BRICS Summit: **Kazan**, Oct 2024; **New Delhi Declaration** (18th, 2026): Global North (~15% of people) holds ~**60%** of IMF/WB votes.
[157:4:5] # Asian Development Bank
[157:4:6] - Est. **1966** at **UN-ESCAP's** initiative (not UNCTAD); HQ **Manila, Philippines**; **India a founding member** (31 founders); **69 members**; **Türkiye** newest (2025).
[157:4:7] - Largest shareholders **Japan and USA** (~15.6% each); **India 4th** (~6.3%); President traditionally **Japanese**.
[157:4:8] - Launched the **Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific** (2023).
[157:4:9] - India is a member of **ADB** and the **Colombo Plan**; **not** of **APEC** or the **OECD** (UPSC 2008).
[157:4:10] # AIIB
[157:4:11] - China-proposed; HQ **Beijing**; Articles signed **2015**; operations **January 2016**.
[157:4:12] - **Founding members** include **India, China and the UK**; the **USA** (and Japan) stayed out.
[157:4:13] - **111** approved members; **China largest** (~26.5% votes), **India second** (~7.6%).
[157:4:14] > Trap: Manila = ADB (Japan-led); Beijing = AIIB (China-led); Shanghai = NDB (BRICS, equal votes).
[157:4:15] ~~ Sources: PMF IAS International Relations p.113-114 (NDB: new members Bangladesh, UAE 2021, Egypt 2023, Algeria 2025; equal votes of founders; NDB vs AIIB, China 26.61%, India 2nd); Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, ch.16 p.192-193 (ADB 1966, 31 founders, Manila) and p.197 (BRICS Bank, Fortaleza Declaration, one-nation one-vote); app notes 2:157 sub 6, 7, 8; NDB HQ Shanghai, Nature Solutions Finance Hub, AIIB founders: general knowledge, not checked
